title: 'HLB Islamic salur RM138,600 pembiayaan kepada melalui SURI Inspirasi
body: 'PETALING JAYA: HLB Islamic menyalurkan pembiayaan sebanyak RM138,600 kepada perusahaan sosial SURI Inspirasi (SURI) di bawah kerangka iTEKAD Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM), selaras dengan komitmen untuk memperkasakan ekosistem perantaraan berasaskan Pengantaraan Berasaskan Nilai (VBI). Inisiatif itu secara langsung menyumbang kepada peningkatan purata pendapatan bulanan sebanyak 94 peratus serta menjana jumlah pendapatan baharu melebihi RM14,000 bagi usahawan yang menyertai program Sustainable Reliable Income (SRI) anjuran SURI. Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif HLB Islamic, Dafinah Ahmed Hilmi berkata, visi bank dalam pengurusan kewangan berteraskan Hayat @ HLB Islamic iaitu pengurusan harta dilihat sebagai satu perjalanan yang bermula dengan penciptaan harta. “Melalui kerjasama dengan SURI, kami menyediakan alat dan latihan asas yang diperlukan oleh komuniti untuk mencungkil potensi keusahawanan mereka. “Kami berharap usaha ini akan menjadi pemangkin kepada perjalanan pembinaan kekayaan berterusan ke arah kebebasan kewangan yang bakal memperkayakan komuniti untuk generasi akan datang,” katanya dalam kenyataan. HLB Islamic berkata, program SRI memperkasakan komuniti berpendapatan rendah untuk mengitar semula sisa fabrik menjadi barangan fesyen yang unik, yang secara langsung mewujudkan peluang pekerjaan dan memupuk semangat keusahawanan, di samping mempromosikan fesyen sifar sisa serta pemerkasaan komuniti. “Usahawan yang terlibat, yang majoriti ibu tunggal berpendapatan rendah telah menghasilkan 1,000 pasang pakaian seragam sekolah untuk pelajar bagi lima buah sekolah di Langkawi, sekali gus menjana penjimatan sebanyak RM30,000 bagi keluarga tempatan. “HLB Islamic meraikan pencapaian ini menerusi penyerahan mesin jahit berkualiti tinggi kepada para usahawan yang terlibat, menandakan peralihan daripada pembelajaran di dalam bilik darjah kepada pemilikan perniagaan secara aktif,” ujarnya. Tambahnya, kejayaan ini menandakan satu pencapaian penting dalam kerjasama berterusan antara HLB Islamic dan SURI, yang mula menyertai ekosistem bank ini sebagai peserta inisiatif HLB Jumpstart. “Diperkenalkan bagi memupuk perusahaan sosial Malaysia yang berimpak tinggi menerusi bimbingan komersial, penjenamaan, serta pembinaan kapasiti digital, HLB Jumpstart telah menyediakan kerangka awal kepada SURI untuk memperluas operasinya. “Hal ini membuktikan strategi jangka panjang bank dalam memupuk usaha sosial menjadi rakan pelaksana berdikari yang mampu memberikan impak yang lebih meluas,” jelasnya. – UTUSAN

Inisiatif itu secara langsung menyumbang kepada peningkatan purata pendapatan bulanan sebanyak 94 peratus serta menjana jumlah pendapatan baharu melebihi RM14,000 bagi usahawan yang menyertai program Sustainable Reliable Income (SRI) anjuran SURI. Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif HLB Islamic, Dafinah Ahmed Hilmi berkata, visi bank dalam pengurusan kewangan berteraskan Hayat @ HLB Islamic iaitu pengurusan harta dilihat sebagai satu perjalanan yang bermula dengan penciptaan harta. “Melalui kerjasama dengan SURI, kami menyediakan alat dan latihan asas yang diperlukan oleh komuniti untuk mencungkil potensi keusahawanan mereka. “Kami berharap usaha ini akan menjadi pemangkin kepada perjalanan pembinaan kekayaan berterusan ke arah kebebasan kewangan yang bakal memperkayakan komuniti untuk generasi akan datang,” katanya dalam kenyataan. HLB Islamic berkata, program SRI memperkasakan komuniti berpendapatan rendah untuk mengitar semula sisa fabrik menjadi barangan fesyen yang unik, yang secara langsung mewujudkan peluang pekerjaan dan memupuk semangat keusahawanan, di samping mempromosikan fesyen sifar sisa serta pemerkasaan komuniti. “Usahawan yang terlibat, yang majoriti ibu tunggal berpendapatan rendah telah menghasilkan 1,000 pasang pakaian seragam sekolah untuk pelajar bagi lima buah sekolah di Langkawi, sekali gus menjana penjimatan sebanyak RM30,000 bagi keluarga tempatan. “HLB Islamic meraikan pencapaian ini menerusi penyerahan mesin jahit berkualiti tinggi kepada para usahawan yang terlibat, menandakan peralihan daripada pembelajaran di dalam bilik darjah kepada pemilikan perniagaan secara aktif,” ujarnya. Tambahnya, kejayaan ini menandakan satu pencapaian penting dalam kerjasama berterusan antara HLB Islamic dan SURI, yang mula menyertai ekosistem bank ini sebagai peserta inisiatif HLB Jumpstart. “Diperkenalkan bagi memupuk perusahaan sosial Malaysia yang berimpak tinggi menerusi bimbingan komersial, penjenamaan, serta pembinaan kapasiti digital, HLB Jumpstart telah menyediakan kerangka awal kepada SURI untuk memperluas operasinya. “Hal ini membuktikan strategi jangka panjang bank dalam memupuk usaha sosial menjadi rakan pelaksana berdikari yang mampu memberikan impak yang lebih meluas,” jelasnya. – UTUSAN

title: 'HLB Targets Wealthy Clients With New opus Privilege Ecosystem
body:
'

Hong Leong Bank is strengthening its affluent banking strategy with HLB opus, an invitation-only payment and lifestyle programme built for selected high-value clients.

The launch combines premium banking, travel benefits and wealth relationships into a single proposition.


At the centre is Southeast Asia’s first ceramic credit card.

HLB opus is also the first payment experience in Malaysia to use the Visa Infinite Privilege tier.

However, the bigger story is not the card material.

HLB is using opus to connect business banking, private wealth management and premium lifestyle benefits under one customer relationship.

HLB Connects Business Success With Personal Wealth

HLB calls the strategy its “One Bank” client success model.

The approach reflects how many high-net-worth customers interact with banks.

Their financial relationships can span business financing, corporate accounts, investments, private banking and personal spending.

HLB wants opus to sit at the personal end of that journey.

Business & Corporate Banking supports entrepreneurship and company growth.

Private Banking helps clients structure and preserve wealth.

Personal Financial Services then translates that relationship into travel, lifestyle and rewards benefits.

The model allows HLB to position opus as a product earned through a broader financial relationship rather than a conventional premium credit card application.

Ceramic Card Reinforces Exclusivity

The physical HLB opus card uses Convego Ceramic technology from Giesecke+Devrient.

Ceramic remains uncommon in the payment card industry, where most premium offerings rely on metal.

The HLB card is manufactured using extreme heat and pressure before undergoing diamond finishing.

The result is designed to be scratch resistant while offering a smooth texture and reflective appearance.

HLB sees the material as part of the product’s wider symbolism.

The name “opus” comes from the Latin word associated with work or achievement.

That concept is intended to connect the physical card with the professional and financial achievements of the clients invited to hold it.

Andrew Jong, HLB Managing Director of Personal Financial Services, said the product recognises the personal stories, sacrifices and ambitions behind client success.

Visa Infinite Privilege Expands Global Access

The privileges attached to the card extend well beyond payments.

HLB opus uses Visa Infinite Privilege, one of Visa’s highest-tier premium offerings.

Clients receive unlimited access to Plaza Premium Lounges around the world.

The package also includes immigration fast-track passes and access to selected Visa private clubs.

Additional status-matching benefits include Harrods Gold, ALL Accor+ Explorer Gold and Banyan Voyager.

These benefits target customers who travel frequently for business and leisure.

Visa Malaysia said affluent consumers are increasingly looking for experiences that feel personal and differentiated.

That shift is pushing premium banking products away from simple cashback and points propositions.

Enrich Partnership Strengthens Travel Rewards

Malaysia Airlines’ Enrich programme plays another important role in the HLB opus ecosystem.

Clients receive 60,000 Enrich Points after payment of the annual fee.

HLB has also created a higher conversion tier designed to reward overseas spending.

The bank says the arrangement gives opus clients the strongest Enrich Points earning potential in the region.

Cardholders can additionally earn one Elite Point for every RM10,000 spent overseas.

Elite Points can help travellers progress through Enrich status tiers.

The partnership also connects customers to reward opportunities across Malaysia Airlines and other carriers in the oneworld alliance.

Malaysia Aviation Group said the collaboration is intended to extend premium service beyond individual flights and into the wider travel experience.

HLB Looks Beyond Traditional Luxury Banking

The introduction of opus reflects changing expectations among affluent banking customers.

Luxury financial products once competed mainly through card materials, airport lounges and concierge services.

Those benefits still matter.

However, wealthy customers increasingly expect banks to understand their wider business, investment and personal needs.

HLB appears to be responding by combining multiple banking divisions around the same client.

That can create deeper relationships and make it harder for competitors to win individual parts of a customer’s financial business.

For HLB, the value of opus may therefore extend far beyond spending on the card itself.

Wealth Management Remains a Key Growth Area

HLB has been expanding its wealth capabilities alongside its business and corporate banking operations.

The bank’s Private Bank works with international wealth partners including Lombard Odier.

That gives HLB access to broader investment and wealth-management expertise for high-net-worth clients.

HLB opus adds a lifestyle layer on top of those capabilities.

The strategy allows the bank to follow a client from business growth through wealth accumulation and eventually into legacy planning.

Premium travel and lifestyle services then become part of that broader relationship.

HLB opus Is Really About Client Retention

The ceramic card may attract attention, but HLB’s larger objective is relationship depth.

An invite-only product gives the bank another way to recognise and retain its highest-value customers.

Premium rewards can strengthen loyalty among clients who already use HLB for corporate, private or personal banking.

At the same time, the exclusivity of the product can reinforce the perceived value of the wider banking relationship.

That makes HLB opus as much a customer strategy as a credit card launch.

Its combination of ceramic design, Visa Infinite Privilege services and Malaysia Airlines rewards gives HLB a distinctive premium proposition.

More importantly, it gives the bank another tool for keeping business, wealth and lifestyle banking under one roof.

title: 'Private Deal: Celebrity-founded nasi padang restaurant chain Bumbu Babah aims to raise RM20 mil
body: 'Private Deal: Celebrity-founded nasi padang restaurant chain Bumbu Babah aims to raise RM20 mil This article first appeared in Wealth, The Edge Malaysia Weekly on September 28, 2026 - October 4, 2026 Transitioning from the entertainment industry to the food and beverage (F&B) sector is not easy, but when comedian Ajak Shiro heard his child express a desire to start a fried chicken business, he thought of making the idea a reality. Ajak, whose real name is Mohd Hanaffi Razak, looked for a business partner. This ended up being Aliey Othman, an F&B industry veteran with 20 years of experience and involvement in many notable brands. Starting with fried chicken as the foundation, their conversation gradually evolved into a discussion on nasi padang, a Minangkabau meal of steamed rice and a variety of side dishes. “In Malaysia, nasi padang hasn’t become mainstream yet. Moreover, it is considered expensive, so we thought of coming up with a large-scale nasi padang brand, but with low prices,” says Ajak. He went on to start Babah Ventures Sdn Bhd (BBV) and opened its first stall, named Bumbu Babah, at a food court in Giant Batu Caves in November 2024. There are now more than 50 outlets across Peninsular Malaysia and the company is on track to reaching 60 outlets this year. Delivering affordable and accessible food is important to Ajak. So, a plate of nasi padang can be priced as low as RM9.90. The uncompromised value the company offers in terms of price point and flavour has become Bumbu Babah’s unique selling point, he says. “At this time, we understand the current economic situation. If we look at the customers now, they value the experience of eating in restaurants more, they like good food, but they’re quite sensitive to price,” says Ajak. To accelerate its next stage of growth, BBV will launch an equity crowdfunding (ECF) campaign on pitchIN to attract institutional investors with its numbers, create a fundraising exercise with customer engagement and possibly look at fast-tracking to an initial public offering (IPO) by 2028 at the earliest. On the ECF platform itself, the company aims to raise between RM5 million and RM20 million, with shares issued at RM10 each. BBV plans to allocate 40% of the funds from the ECF campaign to acquiring its top-performing licensed outlets. Two activities, the setting up of corporate-owned outlets in malls and supporting the rollout of the new concept, will be allocated 25% each, while the final 10% will go to enhancing technology and its working capital. Behind the quick expansion The business has been able to expand quickly because its licensees have shown interest in opening more outlets. “We call it a licensed-and-managed concept because we are very mindful that we don’t want licensees or franchisees to run the outlets their own way and steer away from the standard operating procedures (SOPs). So, we came up with a structure where they provide the funding and become a passive investor in the outlet,” says BBV corporate finance manager Chan Eu-Jinn. This is how the system works: the licensee fully owns the outlet, but BBV continues to run it as if it belonged to the company. BBV also charges a management fee based on a percentage of the licensed outlet’s earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda) on a monthly basis. “If the outlet is not profitable, we do not charge the management fee, so we have to ensure that it is run properly,” he notes. There are currently seven corporate-owned Bumbu Babah outlets. The remaining outlets are owned by licensees. BBV aims to continue expanding, but with a strategy centred more on mall outlets. “Our MyTown, Melawati Mall and IOI City Mall outlets are doing well, but we are still not in a lot of the major malls in the market yet. With the funds raised, we can then invest in this,” says Chan. BBV acknowledges that F&B brands have a tendency to overexpand, and Chan says the company has addressed this by setting a target number of outlets for Bumbu Babah restaurants so as to retain operational quality. “When we hit our target number [we may look more into] maintenance, but we will not be growing for the sake of opening and then cannibalising ourselves.” Bumbu Babah was also able to grow quickly with the introduction of a centralised kitchen to ensure the quality of the food across its licensed outlets remains consistent. Chan says the curry, sambal, proteins and sides are prepared in advance and sent straight to the outlets. This contributes to the efficiency of its operations, as the staff are able to run the basic equipment at the outlets by following the SOPs. Ajak plans to develop more offerings beyond Bumbu Babah’s nasi padang menu. Reflecting this resolve is BBV’s recent collaboration with local music group KRU to open a fine-casual-dining restaurant called KRU Cafe. “We will also have stalls where we will have food menus that include Chinese and Indian food. This is one of the projects that we will implement in time to come, and I think this is one of the reasons why Bumbu Babah will continue to grow in the F&B industry for many more years,” he says. On solid operational and financial ground Based on its audited financial statements, BBV is in a strong financial position. The company has four income streams: retail sales at corporate-owned outlets, central kitchen supplies, monthly management fees and turnkey outlet set-ups involving the building and selling of completed outlets to licensees. For its financial year 2025 (FY2025) ended on Dec 31, the parent company made RM10.4 million in revenue, while the consolidated group revenue came up to RM25.9 million. As for net profit, the parent company recorded RM2.5 million, while the group registered RM3.2 million. This gives the group a net profit margin of 12.5%, which Tradeview Capital research analyst Tan Jia Hui says sits at the higher end of the F&B industry norm of 5% to 12%. “The normalised margin is more likely to settle at around 10% in the upcoming years, given the margin mix [of all four income streams],” she adds. The margin is also anchored by a low marketing spend of roughly 1.3% of its revenue due to the marketing pull of Ajak. The group’s FY2025 earnings quality can be considered clean with only RM24,000 coming from one other source of income, which is the interest from its fixed deposits. Tan notes that liquidity was BBV’s clearest improvement in FY2025, with the current ratio moving from 0.21 times to 1.71 times and the quick ratio from 0.20 times to 1.70 times. Working capital swung from -RM560,000 to RM1.52 million, while its return on assets rose sharply from 6.6% to 74%. The company has also fully repaid shareholder advances in FY2025, leaving the group free of debt or borrowings. “In FY2024, the business leaned on RM600,000 of shareholder and director advances and stretched trade payables to fund itself, so its total liabilities-to-equity ratio stood at 13.9 times. In FY2025, those advances were repaid, so there are no borrowings and no non-current liabilities. The group holds net cash of RM1.47 million, taking the liabilities-to-equity ratio down to 0.97 times,” he says. Gordon Low, founder and managing partner of management consulting firm PiValue Strategy, agrees with Tan. He notes that the company’s financial improvements are backed by positive cash flow rather than being just profit on paper. “This is a company entering its next fundraising round from a position of real financial substance, which is a reasonable and encouraging starting point for the growth questions that follow,” he says. On the operational aspects, Low sees that BBV is signalling a strong early product market fit, although the goals set alongside its projected pace of growth may pose a challenge if not met with a grounded strategy. The affordability and everyday-meal positioning allow Bumbu Babah’s nasi padang to be embedded in local eating habits and food that consumers can enjoy regularly. “This naturally supports higher purchase frequency and repeat sales than non-local or occasion-based cuisines,” he says. Zooming in on the numbers Supported by its milestones, such as the record for selling the highest number of nasi padang servings sold in a day (23,674 plates), the business’ traction is generated by genuine consumer acceptance rather than hype alone, says Low. However, to maintain a returning customer base amid the competitive F&B space, the company must be able to align its marketing and promotional activities with its forecast growth. BBV’s projections show its system-wide revenue jumping to RM102 million in FY2026 from RM50 million in FY2025, with a forecast of 80 outlets. It also expects the figure to rise to RM232.4 million in FY2027. Low says this implies a growth of roughly 104% in FY2026, then a further 128% jump in FY2027. He notes that reaching the FY2027 target would require the group to double its footprint again in a single year. “Using the FY2026 target of 80 outlets as a base, a rough per-outlet run rate of around RM1.3 million suggests BBV would need somewhere in the region of 150 to 180 outlets to support the 2027 projected figure at a similar productivity level,” he says. “This indicates nearly doubling the outlet count again within a single year, an even faster pace than the 50 to 80 outlets planned for 2026. It is a mildly aggressive projection, and the credibility of the entire plan rests heavily on the growth strategy behind it.” Looking at its valuation for the ECF campaign, BBV currently has a reasonable trailing price-to-sales ratio of 3.09 times, based on a valuation of RM80 million against the FY2025 group revenue, which will drop to 1.11 times if its FY2026 forecast of RM72 million is met. However, the trailing price-earnings ratio (PER) of 24.7 times, based on its FY2025 net profit, reflects a premium valuation as it comes in higher than peer Oriental Kopi Holdings Bhd’s (KL:KOPI) trailing PER of 20 times at IPO. “This could ease as outlet count and sales scale, giving operating leverage and central production efficiencies room to lift net margins and bring the multiple down over time,” says Low. Tan cautions investors that BBV is materially smaller than the entire system. The audited FY2025 group revenue of RM25.9 million is roughly half the cited system-wide revenue of RM50 million because licensed outlets only contribute to the group through management fees and supply payments, rather than their full retail turnover. This means a huge chunk of the RM50 million earned by its network of 52 stores belongs to the individual licensed store owners rather than the company issuing the shares. The group revenue of RM25.9 million reflects the actual audited revenue recorded on the parent company’s books, which is the pool of money that generates profit for shareholders. Also seen in the financial statements is the parent company’s operating profit for FY2025, which appears to be cushioned from non-operational income. “The parent company’s profit after tax of RM2.5 million is flattered by RM1.5 million of intra-group dividends and a RM280,000 disposal gain. Strip out both and the standalone operating profit is closer to RM900,000,” says Tan. Put simply, intra-group dividends are distributions of profit paid by a subsidiary company to its parent company or another related entity in the same corporate group. Chan offers an explanation for the disposal gain, saying that BBV began reorganising its activities into two new subsidiaries established in the second quarter of FY2025. The subsidiaries are BBV Restaurants Sdn Bhd (BBVR), which handles store management, and BBV Trading Sdn Bhd, which is in charge of supply, trading and store set-up. This internal restructuring led to a transfer of assets and businesses related to the Melawati Mall and TF Value outlets from BBV to BBVR, and created a one-time gain on disposal on BBV’s standalone financial statements. “These dividends are eliminated upon consolidation because they represent intercompany transactions between entities of the same group. Accordingly, these dividend payments have no impact on BBVs consolidated revenue, profit or profit margins. The same principle applies to the one-off gain arising from the disposal of assets,” says Chan. Another accounting flag lies in the brand’s intangible assets that fell from RM590,000 in FY2024 to RM530,000 in FY2025. The figure, which equates to 12% of its total assets, had its amortisation period shortened from 60 years to 10 years and reclassified, posing a potential impairment risk. Key-figure risk Tan also cautions that BBV’s reliance on Ajak as a key figure of the company could potentially be a risk as the marketing spend of roughly 1.3% of its revenue can fluctuate depending on public sentiment on a celebrity’s status. “A reputational event or attention shift affecting the founder would remove that structural cost advantage and force a step-up in marketing spend, compressing margins, and the concentration is compounded by reliance on a single brand and cuisine, as the newer concepts remain unproven,” he says. Furthermore, the F&B space has a low barrier to entry and is fashion-sensitive, which can influence the performance of same-store sales over time. Seasonality is another factor, with business during the Ramadan and Hari Raya Aidil Fitri festive periods running about 50% and 30% respectively below typical months. Tan indicates that the quarterly figures vary too much to be simply multiplied and predict the full year’s results. Nevertheless, Chan says momentum is picking up, especially after the RON95 petrol subsidy cap was restored to 300 litres a month from 200 litres, improving sentiment and driving a spike in revenue. Additionally, Bumbu Babah recently began listing on Grab exclusively and saw an increase of almost 20% at most of the outlets on the food delivery side without cannibalising dine-in traffic. “Last year, we were focusing a lot on dine-in. We didn’t want to have an additional delivery business affect our operations. So we’re confident that even with all these challenges, we’re on track to hitting our target this year,” says Chan. BBV’s ECF campaign is currently at the pre-live stage. Investors can visit pitchIN’s website to find out more information and make an investment. This is one of the projects that we will implement in time to come, and I think this is one of the reasons why Bumbu Babah will continue to grow in the F&B industry for many more years,” he says. On solid operational and financial ground Based on its audited financial statements, BBV is in a strong financial position. The company has four income streams: retail sales at corporate-owned outlets, central kitchen supplies, monthly management fees and turnkey outlet set-ups involving the building and selling of completed outlets to licensees. For its financial year 2025 (FY2025) ended on Dec 31, the parent company made RM10.4 million in revenue, while the consolidated group revenue came up to RM25.9 million. As for net profit, the parent company recorded RM2.5 million, while the group registered RM3.2 million. This gives the group a net profit margin of 12.5%, which Tradeview Capital research analyst Tan Jia Hui says sits at the higher end of the F&B industry norm of 5% to 12%. “The normalised margin is more likely to settle at around 10% in the upcoming years, given the margin mix [of all four income streams],” she adds. The margin is also anchored by a low marketing spend of roughly 1.3% of its revenue due to the marketing pull of Ajak. The group’s FY2025 earnings quality can be considered clean with only RM24,000 coming from one other source of income, which is the interest from its fixed deposits. Tan notes that liquidity was BBV’s clearest improvement in FY2025, with the current ratio moving from 0.21 times to 1.71 times and the quick ratio from 0.20 times to 1.70 times. Working capital swung from -RM560,000 to RM1.52 million, while its return on assets rose sharply from 6.6% to 74%. The company has also fully repaid shareholder advances in FY2025, leaving the group free of debt or borrowings. “In FY2024, the business leaned on RM600,000 of shareholder and director advances and stretched trade payables to fund itself, so its total liabilities-to-equity ratio stood at 13.9 times. In FY2025, those advances were repaid, so there are no borrowings and no non-current liabilities. The group holds net cash of RM1.47 million, taking the liabilities-to-equity ratio down to 0.97 times,” he says. Gordon Low, founder and managing partner of management consulting firm PiValue Strategy, agrees with Tan. He notes that the company’s financial improvements are backed by positive cash flow rather than being just profit on paper. “This is a company entering its next fundraising round from a position of real financial substance, which is a reasonable and encouraging starting point for the growth questions that follow,” he says. On the operational aspects, Low sees that BBV is signalling a strong early product market fit, although the goals set alongside its projected pace of growth may pose a challenge if not met with a grounded strategy. The affordability and everyday-meal positioning allow Bumbu Babah’s nasi padang to be embedded in local eating habits and food that consumers can enjoy regularly. “This naturally supports higher purchase frequency and repeat sales than non-local or occasion-based cuisines,” he says. Zooming in on the numbers Supported by its milestones, such as the record for selling the highest number of nasi padang servings sold in a day (23,674 plates), the business’ traction is generated by genuine consumer acceptance rather than hype alone, says Low. However, to maintain a returning customer base amid the competitive F&B space, the company must be able to align its marketing and promotional activities with its forecast growth. BBV’s projections show its system-wide revenue jumping to RM102 million in FY2026 from RM50 million in FY2025, with a forecast of 80 outlets. It also expects the figure to rise to RM232.4 million in FY2027. Low says this implies a growth of roughly 104% in FY2026, then a further 128% jump in FY2027. He notes that reaching the FY2027 target would require the group to double its footprint again in a single year. “Using the FY2026 target of 80 outlets as a base, a rough per-outlet run rate of around RM1.3 million suggests BBV would need somewhere in the region of 150 to 180 outlets to support the 2027 projected figure at a similar productivity level,” he says. “This indicates nearly doubling the outlet count again within a single year, an even faster pace than the 50 to 80 outlets planned for 2026. It is a mildly aggressive projection, and the credibility of the entire plan rests heavily on the growth strategy behind it.” Looking at its valuation for the ECF campaign, BBV currently has a reasonable trailing price-to-sales ratio of 3.09 times, based on a valuation of RM80 million against the FY2025 group revenue, which will drop to 1.11 times if its FY2026 forecast of RM72 million is met. However, the trailing price-earnings ratio (PER) of 24.7 times, based on its FY2025 net profit, reflects a premium valuation as it comes in higher than peer Oriental Kopi Holdings Bhd’s (KL:KOPI) trailing PER of 20 times at IPO. “This could ease as outlet count and sales scale, giving operating leverage and central production efficiencies room to lift net margins and bring the multiple down over time,” says Low. Tan cautions investors that BBV is materially smaller than the entire system. The audited FY2025 group revenue of RM25.9 million is roughly half the cited system-wide revenue of RM50 million because licensed outlets only contribute to the group through management fees and supply payments, rather than their full retail turnover. This means a huge chunk of the RM50 million earned by its network of 52 stores belongs to the individual licensed store owners rather than the company issuing the shares. The group revenue of RM25.9 million reflects the actual audited revenue recorded on the parent company’s books, which is the pool of money that generates profit for shareholders. Also seen in the financial statements is the parent company’s operating profit for FY2025, which appears to be cushioned from non-operational income. “The parent company’s profit after tax of RM2.5 million is flattered by RM1.5 million of intra-group dividends and a RM280,000 disposal gain. Strip out both and the standalone operating profit is closer to RM900,000,” says Tan. Put simply, intra-group dividends are distributions of profit paid by a subsidiary company to its parent company or another related entity in the same corporate group. Chan offers an explanation for the disposal gain, saying that BBV began reorganising its activities into two new subsidiaries established in the second quarter of FY2025. The subsidiaries are BBV Restaurants Sdn Bhd (BBVR), which handles store management, and BBV Trading Sdn Bhd, which is in charge of supply, trading and store set-up. This internal restructuring led to a transfer of assets and businesses related to the Melawati Mall and TF Value outlets from BBV to BBVR, and created a one-time gain on disposal on BBV’s standalone financial statements. “These dividends are eliminated upon consolidation because they represent intercompany transactions between entities of the same group. Accordingly, these dividend payments have no impact on BBVs consolidated revenue, profit or profit margins. The same principle applies to the one-off gain arising from the disposal of assets,” says Chan. Another accounting flag lies in the brand’s intangible assets that fell from RM590,000 in FY2024 to RM530,000 in FY2025. The figure, which equates to 12% of its total assets, had its amortisation period shortened from 60 years to 10 years and reclassified, posing a potential impairment risk. Key-figure risk Tan also cautions that BBV’s reliance on Ajak as a key figure of the company could potentially be a risk as the marketing spend of roughly 1.3% of its revenue can fluctuate depending on public sentiment on a celebrity’s status. “A reputational event or attention shift affecting the founder would remove that structural cost advantage and force a step-up in marketing spend, compressing margins, and the concentration is compounded by reliance on a single brand and cuisine, as the newer concepts remain unproven,” he says. Furthermore, the F&B space has a low barrier to entry and is fashion-sensitive, which can influence the performance of same-store sales over time. Seasonality is another factor, with business during the Ramadan and Hari Raya Aidil Fitri festive periods running about 50% and 30% respectively below typical months. Tan indicates that the quarterly figures vary too much to be simply multiplied and predict the full year’s results. Nevertheless, Chan says momentum is picking up, especially after the RON95 petrol subsidy cap was restored to 300 litres a month from 200 litres, improving sentiment and driving a spike in revenue. Additionally, Bumbu Babah recently began listing on Grab exclusively and saw an increase of almost 20% at most of the outlets on the food delivery side without cannibalising dine-in traffic. “Last year, we were focusing a lot on dine-in. We didn’t want to have an additional delivery business affect our operations. So we’re confident that even with all these challenges, we’re on track to hitting our target this year,” says Chan. BBV’s ECF campaign is currently at the pre-live stage. Investors can visit pitchIN’s website to find out more information and make an investment. title: 'Wealth
body: 'This article first appeared in Wealth, The Edge Malaysia Weekly on September 28, 2026 - October 4, 2026  Two veterans of Malaysia’s start-up and investment ecosystem — entrepreneur and investor Sivapalan Vivekarajah and former Pitch Platforms Sdn Bhd (pitchIN) chief operating officer Xelia Tong — are launching a RM50 million debut venture fund.  Main Market-listed automotive replacement-parts manufacturer New Hoong Fatt Holdings Bhd (NHF) (KL: NHFATT) has committed up to RM20 million as its anchor limited partner.  The investment will be made through its wholly owned subsidiary Jhi Soon Manufacturing Industries Sdn Bhd, which will subscribe for up to 20 million Class A redeemable preference shares in Cypress Drive Ventures at RM1 each, NHF said in a filing with Bursa Malaysia.  Cypress Drive Ventures is the first fund managed by Cypress Asia Sdn Bhd, which was founded by Sivapalan and Tong. It will target technology-driven local businesses at the pre-Series A and Series A stages that are profitable or have a clear path to profitability.  Cypress Asia is seeking the remaining RM30 million from family offices and other investors.  Investments will range from RM1 million to RM3 million per company. Cypress Asia expects to make five to seven investments initially and build a concentrated portfolio of 10 to 12 companies if the fund reaches its RM50 million target. Depending on the deal, it may lead the round, co-invest with another fund or join an existing group of investors.  The fund has a seven-year term, with the option of two successive one-year extensions.  Cypress Asia expects to make its first investment in the first quarter of 2027. It plans to hold its first investment committee meeting in November and already has a pipeline of potential deals that will undergo due diligence.  The pipeline will draw on the co-founders’ existing networks, including companies from accelerator ScaleUp Malaysia’s portfolio and Sivapalan’s Soonicorn Collective for later-stage technology businesses as well as businesses within the network Tong built at pitchIN, a digital fundraising and investment platform.  Sivapalan and Tong worked together at ScaleUp Malaysia, as a senior partner and a managing partner respectively. They invested in 38 companies under the initiative.  Sivapalan also launched the Soonicorn Collective’s Titan, a 12-month coaching and execution programme for founders seeking to scale their business towards RM100 million in revenue, in which 18 businesses took part.  “We have a network of companies that we can invest in. Because we’ve been in the ecosystem for so long, people trust us,” says Sivapalan, co-managing partner of Cypress Asia.  The firm will also source investments through equity crowdfunding platforms and other venture capital firms.  The fund is sector-agnostic but will invest only in technology-driven businesses, says Tong, CEO and managing partner of Cypress Asia. Potential areas include electrical and electronics, automotive, digital health and agriculture.  “There are certain areas that we don’t touch — highly regulated businesses, those very dependent on state government contracts, businesses that are purely software, such as human resources software, or very e-commerce-driven. Other than that, we’re quite open,” she says.  Cypress Asia will look for companies that can grow profitably and reach a listing or acquisition without having to raise money repeatedly. Tong says an investee should ideally need no more than one or two additional funding rounds after Cypress Asia’s investment.  “Our investment thesis is to look for companies that already have a profitable business. It doesn’t have to be a lot; it can be a small profit, or at least they should be profitable this year. But they must be able to prove to us that they can be profitable,” says Sivapalan.  “We want to take them to RM8 million to RM10 million in profit over a five-year period and then list them on Bursa Malaysia or another exchange. The good thing about getting them to profitability is that they also become interesting for a merger and acquisition, so it serves a dual purpose.”  Endorsement from a public listed company  NHF became Cypress Drive Ventures’ anchor investor after about 2½ years of discussions with Tong, as the automotive-parts group explored ways to gain exposure to innovation and diversify its sources of income.  Tong first came to know the family behind the company through business and start-up networks when she was at Cradle Fund Sdn Bhd. She had previously encouraged a family member involved in running the group to set up a corporate venture capital arm but the proposal was too early for it at the time.  The proposal was subsequently presented to NHF’s board of directors two or three times, with the board raising extensive questions as the company was new to venture investing. Tong says the process gave both sides time to understand what they were entering into and helped build trust.  Initially, NHF committed RM10 million. When Cypress Asia decided to apply for Jelawang Capital’s Emerging Fund Managers’ Programme at the end of 2024, NHF raised it to RM12 million, which was the amount of private capital Cypress Asia needed to meet the programme’s 20% threshold for a fund of at least RM60 million.  In the end, Cypress Asia was not selected for the programme but Tong says NHF proceeded with the investment as its decision was based on the managers’ experience rather than the prospect of matching capital. It later increased its commitment to RM20 million.  “We are blessed to have them as our first and anchor investor. They genuinely want to look at the innovation side of things and potentially diversify into other businesses,” says Tong.  For NHF, the fund offers potential financial returns and exposure to businesses and technologies beyond its existing network.  Tong also sees the commitment as an example of how cash held by profitable listed companies can be put to work in Malaysia’s venture ecosystem.  “I think Securities Commission Malaysia has also always been trying to get more private pockets to actually invest in this space, to make investments in venture funds … A lot of companies, especially listed ones, are sitting on a lot of cash, but it is a lazy balance sheet that is not doing anything for the business,” she says.  Sivapalan adds: “[NHF] is a main board company, and they are willing to take a chance with us. It gives other people the confidence that they can also take a chance with us.”  Experienced investors  Sivapalan and Tong say their previous investments and years spent working with founders will shape how they manage the fund.  “We have been through the mill. We did not just come out of corporate finance and decide to do this. We have worked with many founders,” he says.  Sivapalan has spent close to four decades as an entrepreneur, coach and angel investor. He has personally invested in 16 businesses as an angel investor and also co-founded ScaleUp Malaysia, as well as founded the Soonicorn Collective.  Tong had investment roles at Malaysia Debt Ventures Bhd and Cradle Fund, where she was vice-president of investment and headed the Angel Tax Incentive programme. She later became a managing partner at ScaleUp Malaysia and, most recently, chief operating officer of equity crowdfunding platform pitchIN.  Both see the venture fund as a continuation of their earlier work. During ScaleUp Malaysia’s first three years, investments were made at a fixed valuation of RM2.5 million. Sivapalan says some stronger companies wanted ScaleUp as an investor but eventually declined its offer as the valuation was deemed too low.  A venture fund gives Cypress Asia more flexibility to invest in such companies at a later stage and at valuations that reflect their growth.  “After running an accelerator, the natural progression is to move into a venture capital fund. An accelerator cannot offer different valuations to different companies, so we lost those opportunities … Then Xelia said there might be a corporate investor, and Jelawang came along. So, we thought, ‘Let’s give it a try. Let’s try to raise the fund.’”  Sivapalan adds that the broader aim is to rebuild confidence in Malaysia’s venture capital industry. “There is very low trust in the VC industry today … If the VC industry cannot prove itself, then you can’t raise money to support start-ups and help them grow.  “The VC model can work, and I think we would like to show that we have the right insights, the right model and the right thinking to make this work.”

title: 'Final Sukan Asia Aichi-Nagoya: India pun takut jumpa kita -- Misi Malaysia tamatkan penantian 68 tahun petang ini
body: 'Kontinjen negara kini berpeluang merebut antara pingat emas Sukan Asia paling bernilai dalam sejarah apabila skuad hoki padang lelaki Malaysia hanya selangkah lagi daripada mencipta sejarah di Aichi-Nagoya 2026. The Speedy Tigers akan turun di pentas final dengan satu misi besar -- menamatkan penantian emas Sukan Asia yang tidak pernah dimenangi Malaysia sejak penyertaan pertama pada 1958, sekali gus memperoleh tiket ke Sukan Olimpik Los Angeles (LA) 2028. Sepanjang 18 penampilan di temasya itu termasuk edisi Aichi-Nagoya, pencapaian terbaik skuad hoki lelaki negara setakat ini adalah dua pingat perak dan enam gangsa. Kali terakhir Malaysia merasai pentas final Sukan Asia adalah pada 2018 di Indonesia, namun ketika itu skuad negara terpaksa akur dengan kekalahan pada aksi kemuncak. Wartawan Astro Arena, Karl Nunis, sempat mendapatkan reaksi Olimpian dan bekas kapten hoki negara, Datuk Mirnawan Nawawi, menjelang pertembungan akhir pasukan kebangsaan bertemu musuh tradisi, India, petang ini. “India jumpa kita diorang pon takut” Ucapan eksklusif dari bekas kapten hoki negara, Datuk Mirnawan Nawawi yang juga merupakan pembawa Jalur Gemilang di Olimpik 2000, Sydney, Australia. Let’s go for GOLD Speedy Tigers @ASTROARENA pic.twitter.com/mdV6UZMrSh— karlnunis (@_karlnunis) October 3, 2026 "Tahniah layak ke perlawanan akhir. "Anda semua telah buat yang terbaik setakat ini. "Anda akan bertemu India. Tiada satu pasukan yang sempurna. "Mereka juga mempunyai kelemahan tersendiri. Mereka juga takut bertemu dengan kita. "Jangan tertekan. Berikan yang terbaik," katanya. Kredit foto: Konfederasi Hoki Malaysia (KHM)

title: 'Dialog JV Bags Onshore O&G Concession in Thailand
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Dialog Group Bhd (KL:DIALOG) said its 50.01%-owned joint venture company has been awarded concession rights and operatorship for the L8/66 exploration block onshore Thailand. The joint venture company, Pan Orient Energy (Siam) Ltd (POES), was notified by the Thai government on Monday (Oct 5) that it had been awarded the concession following a joint bid with CanAsia Energy Corp in Thailand’s 25th Onshore Bid Round, according to Dialog's Bursa Malaysia filing on Tuesday. POES will operate the concession with a 70% participating interest, while Canada-listed CanAsia will hold the remaining 30% non-operating interest. The development of L8/66 carries a minimum work commitment of US$14.3 million (RM58.4 million). The award remains subject to the finalisation and execution of the concession agreement and the fulfilment of its conditions precedent, with physical work expected to begin immediately after the agreement is signed. POES is a joint venture between Dialog’s wholly-owned Pan Orient Petroleum Pte Ltd and Thailand-based Sea Oil Energy Ltd, which holds the remaining 49.99%. Dialog, through POES, already operates the producing L53/48 onshore concession in Thailand, which is adjacent to the L8/66 block. L8/66 was previously part of the L53/48 concession before being relinquished to the Thai government under concession terms requiring portions of undeveloped acreage to be surrendered over time. Dialog said the new block has similar geological characteristics to L53/48 and gives POES access to additional acreage surrounding its existing producing fields. “The award of Concession L8/66 to POES further strengthens Dialog’s upstream portfolio and creates operational synergies by leveraging on the group’s integrated technical services across its diversified business model,” the company said. "Dialog will remain focused and steadfast in the pursuit of diversification across the upstream, midstream and downstream energy sector as well as the sustainable and renewable sector, to strategically position the group to weather different economic and oil price cycles, which is in line with the group's strategy of generating long term recurring income," it added. For the financial year ended June 30, 2026 (FY2026), Dialog’s net profit surged 95.4% to RM593.55 million from RM303.83 million a year earlier, as revenue grew 15.3% to RM2.88 billion from RM2.5 billion. The stronger FY2026 performance was driven by positive contributions across the group’s businesses, particularly its Malaysian operations, while its international businesses also recorded higher profit contributions on increased sales of specialist products and services. Dialog proposed a final dividend of three sen per share, bringing its total dividend for FY2026 to 4.7 sen per share or about RM265.93 million. Dialog shares closed two sen or 1.08% higher at RM1.87 on Tuesday, valuing the group at RM10.56 billion. Year to date, the counter has gained over 6%. 'Dialog JV Bags Onshore O&G Concession in Thailand

'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Dialog Group Bhd (KL:DIALOG) said its 50.01%-owned joint venture company has been awarded concession rights and operatorship for the L8/66 exploration block onshore Thailand. The joint venture company, Pan Orient Energy (Siam) Ltd (POES), was notified by the Thai government on Monday (Oct 5) that it had been awarded the concession following a joint bid with CanAsia Energy Corp in Thailand’s 25th Onshore Bid Round, according to Dialog's Bursa Malaysia filing on Tuesday. POES will operate the concession with a 70% participating interest, while Canada-listed CanAsia will hold the remaining 30% non-operating interest. The development of L8/66 carries a minimum work commitment of US$14.3 million (RM58.4 million). The award remains subject to the finalisation and execution of the concession agreement and the fulfilment of its conditions precedent, with physical work expected to begin immediately after the agreement is signed. POES is a joint venture between Dialog’s wholly-owned Pan Orient Petroleum Pte Ltd and Thailand-based Sea Oil Energy Ltd, which holds the remaining 49.99%. Dialog, through POES, already operates the producing L53/48 onshore concession in Thailand, which is adjacent to the L8/66 block. L8/66 was previously part of the L53/48 concession before being relinquished to the Thai government under concession terms requiring portions of undeveloped acreage to be surrendered over time. Dialog said the new block has similar geological characteristics to L53/48 and gives POES access to additional acreage surrounding its existing producing fields. “The award of Concession L8/66 to POES further strengthens Dialog’s upstream portfolio and creates operational synergies by leveraging on the group’s integrated technical services across its diversified business model,” the company said. "Dialog will remain focused and steadfast in the pursuit of diversification across the upstream, midstream and downstream energy sector as well as the sustainable and renewable sector, to strategically position the group to weather different economic and oil price cycles, which is in line with the group's strategy of generating long term recurring income," it added. The stronger FY2026 performance was driven by positive contributions across the group’s businesses, particularly its Malaysian operations, while its international businesses also recorded higher profit contributions on increased sales of specialist products and services. title: 'Mosti’s Cradle Fund Sees Overcrowding in Applicants as 70% Are AI-related Startups
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Artificial intelligence (AI)-related startups now account for about 60% to 70% of the estimated 1,000 applications received by Cradle Fund each year, but investors are becoming more selective as the space grows increasingly crowded. Cradle Fund group chief executive officer Norman Matthieu Vanhaecke said the government agency has seen a sharp increase in startups positioning themselves as AI-driven, AI-enabled or AI-native. “The market is getting really, really crowded. So it's kind of tough for venture capitalists later on, and even for us as well, to really decide where to park, for us, especially taxpayers money into,” he said during a panel session at the Alliance Bank BizSmart Business Conference. "At the end of the day, for us, the return has to come back to the country and the people. So it's tough for us. So you have to really differentiate," he added. This has made it more difficult for investors and Cradle Fund, which manages taxpayer funds, to determine which AI businesses have sufficient potential to warrant funding, he said. Cradle Fund was created by the Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (Mosti) in 2023. It provides grants, equity investment, commercialisation support, and mentorship to tech entrepreneurs. Startups need to differentiate themselves by developing niche solutions that can serve not only the Malaysian market but also regional and international markets, Vanhaecke said. At the same conference, Sunway iLabs — the innovation arm of Sunway Bhd (KL:SUNWAY) — chief operations officer Karen Lau said investors also need to distinguish between companies that genuinely have AI capabilities and those that are simply using AI as part of their positioning. Investors are looking at the defensibility of the technology, including whether a startup is merely building a layer on top of existing frontier models or has technology that can be integrated deeply into customers’ business processes, she said. Meanwhile, fellow panellist 1337 Ventures CEO and founding partner Bikesh Lakhmichand said the firm looks for founders with expertise in a specific industry, such as healthcare, fashion or marketing, rather than startups built around generic AI applications. “What we are funding is your expertise in the sector, not so much AI,” he said, adding that startups need to demonstrate how their technology addresses specific workflows. Lakhmichand said generic AI applications could face greater competition as foundation models continue to develop. The panel also highlighted a broader shift in how investors assess startups, with traction, market potential and the ability to scale becoming more important than simply positioning a company as an AI business. The session was focused on What It Really Takes for Scaling, Funding, and Strategic Exits?, and was moderated by Redwood Global Capital managing partner Lennise Ng. title: 'Berjaya Says Core Berjaya Hills Businesses Unaffected by Pahang Enforcement Action
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Berjaya Corp Bhd (KL:BJCORP) said its main businesses at Berjaya Hills remain fully operational despite enforcement action by the Pahang authorities, and expects no material financial or operational impact from the issue. It said state authorities had sealed and restricted access to the staff quarters, central laundry, rabbit park and Japanese garden on Sept 28, while The Chateau Spa & Wellness Resort, Colmar Tropicale Hotel, Berjaya Hills Golf & Country Club and the greenhouses were unaffected. "The group's core operating facilities, including the hotels, golf club and greenhouses remain unaffected and continue to operate as usual," Berjaya Corp said in a bourse filing Tuesday. The disclosure was made in response to Bursa Malaysia's queries seeking details of the enforcement action — linked to a long-running dispute between Berjaya Hills Resort Bhd and the Pahang government over a sharp increase in quit rent imposed on the company's properties in the state — and how it would financially and operationally affect the group. Berjaya Hills claimed its annual quit rent jumped 13-fold to RM33.7 million in 2020 from about RM2.4 million in 2019, before being reduced to RM25.75 million following 11 appeals to the state government between April 2020 and December 2022. The company said it paid about RM42.65 million in quit rent and penalties "under protest" between 2020 and 2026, while continuing to seek a further review of the rates. In Tuesday's filing, Berjaya Corp said the higher quit rent expenses had been recognised through accruals for the respective financial years since the revised rates took effect in 2020. "Accordingly, the impact arising from the revised annual quit rent rates has been taken into account in the group's financial statements for the respective financial years and the revised rates have no material operational impact to the group," it added. Separately on Tuesday, Pahang Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail said the state government is open to discussions with Berjaya Hills to resolve the impasse, but stressed that any talks must be guided by existing legal provisions and regulations. "That is up to them (Berjaya Hills). We are taking actions based on the law. The state government is open to discussions, but they must be based on and guided by the law. There are regulations, so follow the rules," Wan Rosdy was quoted as saying by Bernama. Berjaya Hills had on Oct 2 called the enforcement action "unconscionable and totally unacceptable", arguing that it was unreasonable given that its application for leave to appeal the quit rent dispute remains pending before the Federal Court. Nevertheless, it also said it hoped the Pahang government would continue to engage with the company towards a "mutually acceptable and amicable resolution". The company, which has been challenging the revised quit rent through legal means with no success so far, first sought a judicial review at the Temerloh High Court. The application was dismissed in May 2024 on grounds that the court could not intervene in the state government's policy decision. That decision was upheld by the Court of Appeal on July 16 this year. This led to Berjaya Hills applying for leave to appeal to the Federal Court on Aug 14, with the hearing scheduled for Dec 8. Berjaya Corp closed unchanged at 25 sen on Tuesday for a market capitalisation of RM1.52 billion. title: 'Daily Newswatch - 7 Oct 2026
body: 'The FBM KLCI rose 0.1% to 1,633 points on Tuesday due to positive regional sentiment, tracking gains across major Asian markets after Wall Street's tech-led rally overnight, although elevated US Treasury yields continued to cap risk appetite. Health Technology (+6.3%), Producer Manufacturing (+1.8%) and Health Services (+1.7%) led sectoral gains, driven by Nestle (+1.3%), Kuala Lumpur Kepong (+0.5%) and Petronas Chemicals (+0.2%). Market breadth was positive, with 664 gainers ahead of 450 losers, while 560 counters closed unchanged. Asian markets closed mixed on Tuesday as most bourses tracked Wall Street's tech-led rally, with Japan further supported by a strong government bond auction that eased yield concerns, while South Korea fell as chip heavyweights came under selling pressure amid worries over elevated bond yields. Japan's Nikkei 225 led regional gains (+1.1%), followed by Hong Kong's Hang Seng (+1.0%) and Taiwan's TAIEX (+0.2%), while South Korea's KOSPI fell 0.9%. Mainland China markets remained closed for the National Day holiday and will resume trading on Thursday. In South Korea, NonEnergy Minerals (-2.7%), Process Industries (-2.0%) and Producer Manufacturing (-1.8%) were the sectoral laggards, dragged by DH Autonex, Exicure Hitron and SG Global. In China, in their last trading sessions, the sectoral gains were led by Health Care (+2.9%), Consumer Staples (+1.7%) and Financials (+1.0%), with CanSino Biologics, Shanghai Model Organisms and Suzhou Novoprotein Scientific as the top performers. European stocks closed firmly higher Tuesday, led by banks, consumer discretionary and autos as sovereign yields' surge paused. Euro STOXX 50 and STOXX Europe 600 each added 0.5%, to 6,272 and 636. Long-dated euroarea yields mostly fell, especially in higher-debt economies, easing ECB antifragmentation intervention fears. Banks tracked rebounding credit: BNP Paribas jumped 2.5%; UniCredit, Santander and Deutsche Bank rose 1.5% each. Intesa Sanpaolo rebounded 1.3% as markets reassessed a potential Banca MPS acquisition's return impact. Schneider Electric sank 4.5% after agreeing to buy US software firm PTC for $22.6 billion. US stocks closed higher Tuesday, supported by heavyweight tech as surging bond yields paused, easing pressure on its credit outlook. The S&P 500 (+0.6%) and Nasdaq 100 (+0.5%) hit record highs, while the Dow gained 253 points. AI infrastructure and hyperscaler stocks mostly rose as fresh sector deals spurred speculative demand. OpenAI discussed $30 billion financing with UAE funds; Alphabet gained 0.3% before acquiring nuclear capacity from Constellation Energy (+12.2%). AMD jumped 2.8% as CEO Lisa Su signalled strong chip demand ahead. Microsoft rose 0.8%, Amazon 1.9% and Nvidia 0.1%. IMF: Cost-of-living crises have lasting impact on inflation expectations, poverty, IMF says 5.33% on Monday Sharp spikes in food and energy prices will likely become more common, the International Monetary Fund said, warning such crises drive inflation expectations higher for longer, worsen poverty and threaten economic stability. IMF research released on Tuesday examined three decades of strategies used by governments to mitigate price surges, as well as a new economic model that accounts for the higher inflation experienced by poorer households, which spend a higher share of their budgets on daily necessities. (Reuters) US: Oil Rises as Mideast Risks Remain 5.33% on Monday Crude oil climbed toward $90 per barrel on Wednesday, recovering from five-week lows as persistent risks to Middle East energy flows overshadowed signs of rising supply from the region. Iran has intensified attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz in recent days, with the UK Maritime Trade Operations reporting nine incidents so far this month. (Trading Economics) US: Trade deficit widens in August amid strong imports 5.33% on Monday The US trade deficit widened more than expected in August, driven by a surge in imports of goods amid robust domestic demand, keeping trade on track to again subtract from economic growth in the third quarter. The trade shortfall increased 13.7% to US$105.6 billion (RM431.5 billion), the Commerce Department's Bureau of Economic Analysis and Census Bureau said on Tuesday. (Trading Economics) US: 10-Year Treasury Yield Softens from 24-Year High The yield on the 10-year US Treasury note was at 5.26% on Tuesday, pausing a surge that peaked at a 24-year high of 5.33% touched yesterday, tracking the momentary dip in wholesale fuel prices. Oil bids were tamed by signs that some laden tankers passed through the Strait of Hormuz. The 10-year yield has surged over 110bps this year as risks of higher rates from the Federal Reserve, soaring federal deficit spending, and increasing corporate debt supply triggered a plunge in demand for duration. (Trading Economics) US: Logistics Growth 2nd-Highest in 4 Years The US Logistics Managers’ Index increased to 70.2 in September 2026 from 66.6 in August. It is the second-highest reading in four years, behind only June’s reading of 71.1. A faster increase was seen for Inventory Levels (58.9 vs 52.8) and Inventory Costs (79.9 vs 78.6) which is also having a significant effect on the warehousing market. Warehousing Capacity shrank the most since March 2022 (39.3 vs 53.5), potentially due to the fact that firms, particularly retailers, had run inventory down a bit and are not rushing goods in now ahead of potential holiday sales. (Trading Economics) US: Gold edges up as dollar, Treasury yields slip Gold ticked up on Tuesday, supported by a pause in the US Treasury yield's rally and a weaker dollar, while investors awaited the minutes of the US Federal Reserve's (Fed) September meeting for fresh clues on its monetary policy outlook. Spot gold rose 0.4% to US$4,155.34 (RM16,977.89) per ounce by 10.09am EDT (1409 GMT). US gold futures for December delivery added 0.6% to US$4,182.30. (Reuters) JP: BOJ chief calls for more focus on anchoring inflation around target Bank of Japan (BOJ) governor Kazuo Ueda said on Tuesday that it was becoming more important to anchor underlying inflation around the central bank's 2% target, signalling readiness to keep raising interest rates to blunt the risk of too-high inflation. The remarks come ahead of the central bank's two-day policy meeting ending on Oct 30, where new quarterly growth and inflation forecasts will be closely watched for clues on the timing of the next rate hike. (Reuters) JP: 10-year bond sale draws solid demand as yields top 3% Japan’s 10-year government bond auction Tuesday saw stronger demand than the 12-month average as elevated yields underpinned buying. The bid-to-cover ratio was 3.76 compared with 3.29 at the previous sale and a 12-month average of 3.21. Bond futures pared their losses after the result. The benchmark 10-year yield hit 3.115% on Tuesday, matching its highest level since 1996. A sale of the same tenor last month passed smoothly after yields reached 3%. (Bloomberg) JP: Nominal Wage Growth Tops 3% for 7th Month Average cash earnings in Japan increased by 3.8% year-on-year in August 2026, slightly exceeding market expectations for a 3.7% gain and staying above 3% for a seventh month, the longest such run since 1992. While it slowed from a revised 4.3% rise in July, it also marked the 56th consecutive month of nominal wage growth. Regular pay, including base salaries, rose 3.8% to mark continued solid wage growth, while overtime pay accelerated to 5.2% from a revised 4.5% increase in July. (Trading Economics) MY: BNM: Banks working towards fraud alert before transaction is completed Malaysian banks are working towards introducing fraud alert capabilities that can flag potential risks before a transaction is completed. A pilot test involving selected banks is targeted for the first half of 2027 ahead of wider implementation, Bank Negara Malaysia governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said in his speech text for a conference on financial crime and counter terrorism financing on Tuesday. (The Edge) MY: And France to sign energy transition MOU soon, says Fadillah Malaysia and France are expected to sign a memorandum of understanding (MOU) on energy transition soon to accelerate efforts towards a cleaner and more sustainable future, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof said on Tuesday. Fadillah, who is also the energy transition and water transformation minister, said the matter was discussed during a courtesy call by French Ambassador to Malaysia Marc Abensour at the Parliament building on Tuesday. (Bernama) CIMB: Considers selling Philippine business - Bloomberg CIMB Group Holdings Bhd is exploring a sale of its business in the Philippines as part of efforts to streamline and focus on bigger markets for growth, according to people with knowledge of the matter. The Malaysian lender is working with a financial adviser on the potential divestment and has reached out to prospective buyers to gauge interest, said the people, asking not to be identified because the process is private. (The Edge) ZETRIX: Still finalising amount owed to JPJ after Loke reveals RM314m arrears Zetrix AI Bhd (KL:ZETRIX) said the exact amount it owes the Road Transport Department (JPJ) is still being finalised between the two parties, a day after Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook said the company had accumulated RM314 million in unpaid remittances. It said this in a bourse filing on Tuesday following queries from Bursa Malaysia about several news reports by The Edge about the arrears, and the subsequent suspension of Zetrix and its subsidiary MyEG Sdn Bhd as JPJ collection agents, which Zetrix confirmed. 'The FBM KLCI rose 0.1% to 1,633 points on Tuesday due to positive regional sentiment, tracking gains across major Asian markets after Wall Street's tech-led rally overnight, although elevated US Treasury yields continued to cap risk appetite. Health Technology (+6.3%), Producer Manufacturing (+1.8%) and Health Services (+1.7%) led sectoral gains, driven by Nestle (+1.3%), Kuala Lumpur Kepong (+0.5%) and Petronas Chemicals (+0.2%). Market breadth was positive, with 664 gainers ahead of 450 losers, while 560 counters closed unchanged. Asian markets closed mixed on Tuesday as most bourses tracked Wall Street's tech-led rally, with Japan further supported by a strong government bond auction that eased yield concerns, while South Korea fell as chip heavyweights came under selling pressure amid worries over elevated bond yields. Japan's Nikkei 225 led regional gains (+1.1%), followed by Hong Kong's Hang Seng (+1.0%) and Taiwan's TAIEX (+0.2%), while South Korea's KOSPI fell 0.9%. Mainland China markets remained closed for the National Day holiday and will resume trading on Thursday. In South Korea, NonEnergy Minerals (-2.7%), Process Industries (-2.0%) and Producer Manufacturing (-1.8%) were the sectoral laggards, dragged by DH Autonex, Exicure Hitron and SG Global. In China, in their last trading sessions, the sectoral gains were led by Health Care (+2.9%), Consumer Staples (+1.7%) and Financials (+1.0%), with CanSino Biologics, Shanghai Model Organisms and Suzhou Novoprotein Scientific as the top performers. European stocks closed firmly higher Tuesday, led by banks, consumer discretionary and autos as sovereign yields' surge paused. Euro STOXX 50 and STOXX Europe 600 each added 0.5%, to 6,272 and 636. Long-dated euroarea yields mostly fell, especially in higher-debt economies, easing ECB antifragmentation intervention fears. Banks tracked rebounding credit: BNP Paribas jumped 2.5%; UniCredit, Santander and Deutsche Bank rose 1.5% each. Intesa Sanpaolo rebounded 1.3% as markets reassessed a potential Banca MPS acquisition's return impact. Schneider Electric sank 4.5% after agreeing to buy US software firm PTC for $22.6 billion. US stocks closed higher Tuesday, supported by heavyweight tech as surging bond yields paused, easing pressure on its credit outlook. The S&P 500 (+0.6%) and Nasdaq 100 (+0.5%) hit record highs, while the Dow gained 253 points. AI infrastructure and hyperscaler stocks mostly rose as fresh sector deals spurred speculative demand. OpenAI discussed $30 billion financing with UAE funds; Alphabet gained 0.3% before acquiring nuclear capacity from Constellation Energy (+12.2%). AMD jumped 2.8% as CEO Lisa Su signalled strong chip demand ahead. Microsoft rose 0.8%, Amazon 1.9% and Nvidia 0.1%. IMF: Cost-of-living crises have lasting impact on inflation expectations, poverty, IMF says 5.33% on Monday Sharp spikes in food and energy prices will likely become more common, the International Monetary Fund said, warning such crises drive inflation expectations higher for longer, worsen poverty and threaten economic stability. IMF research released on Tuesday examined three decades of strategies used by governments to mitigate price surges, as well as a new economic model that accounts for the higher inflation experienced by poorer households, which spend a higher share of their budgets on daily necessities. (Reuters) US: Oil Rises as Mideast Risks Remain 5.33% on Monday Crude oil climbed toward $90 per barrel on Wednesday, recovering from five-week lows as persistent risks to Middle East energy flows overshadowed signs of rising supply from the region. Iran has intensified attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz in recent days, with the UK Maritime Trade Operations reporting nine incidents so far this month. (Trading Economics) US: Trade deficit widens in August amid strong imports 5.33% on Monday The US trade deficit widened more than expected in August, driven by a surge in imports of goods amid robust domestic demand, keeping trade on track to again subtract from economic growth in the third quarter. The trade shortfall increased 13.7% to US$105.6 billion (RM431.5 billion), the Commerce Department's Bureau of Economic Analysis and Census Bureau said on Tuesday. (Trading Economics) US: 10-Year Treasury Yield Softens from 24-Year High The yield on the 10-year US Treasury note was at 5.26% on Tuesday, pausing a surge that peaked at a 24-year high of 5.33% touched yesterday, tracking the momentary dip in wholesale fuel prices. Oil bids were tamed by signs that some laden tankers passed through the Strait of Hormuz. The 10-year yield has surged over 110bps this year as risks of higher rates from the Federal Reserve, soaring federal deficit spending, and increasing corporate debt supply triggered a plunge in demand for duration. (Trading Economics) US: Logistics Growth 2nd-Highest in 4 Years The US Logistics Managers’ Index increased to 70.2 in September 2026 from 66.6 in August. It is the second-highest reading in four years, behind only June’s reading of 71.1. A faster increase was seen for Inventory Levels (58.9 vs 52.8) and Inventory Costs (79.9 vs 78.6) which is also having a significant effect on the warehousing market. Warehousing Capacity shrank the most since March 2022 (39.3 vs 53.5), potentially due to the fact that firms, particularly retailers, had run inventory down a bit and are not rushing goods in now ahead of potential holiday sales. (Trading Economics) US: Gold edges up as dollar, Treasury yields slip Gold ticked up on Tuesday, supported by a pause in the US Treasury yield's rally and a weaker dollar, while investors awaited the minutes of the US Federal Reserve's (Fed) September meeting for fresh clues on its monetary policy outlook. Spot gold rose 0.4% to US$4,155.34 (RM16,977.89) per ounce by 10.09am EDT (1409 GMT). US gold futures for December delivery added 0.6% to US$4,182.30. (Reuters) JP: BOJ chief calls for more focus on anchoring inflation around target Bank of Japan (BOJ) governor Kazuo Ueda said on Tuesday that it was becoming more important to anchor underlying inflation around the central bank's 2% target, signalling readiness to keep raising interest rates to blunt the risk of too-high inflation. The remarks come ahead of the central bank's two-day policy meeting ending on Oct 30, where new quarterly growth and inflation forecasts will be closely watched for clues on the timing of the next rate hike. (Reuters) JP: 10-year bond sale draws solid demand as yields top 3% Japan’s 10-year government bond auction Tuesday saw stronger demand than the 12-month average as elevated yields underpinned buying. The bid-to-cover ratio was 3.76 compared with 3.29 at the previous sale and a 12-month average of 3.21. Bond futures pared their losses after the result. The benchmark 10-year yield hit 3.115% on Tuesday, matching its highest level since 1996. A sale of the same tenor last month passed smoothly after yields reached 3%. While it slowed from a revised 4.3% rise in July, it also marked the 56th consecutive month of nominal wage growth. title: 'Mplus Market Pulse - 07 Oct 2026
body: 'MY: Tracking positive regional performance, the local bourse continued to trade higher ahead of the Budget 2027 announcement. Market breadth turned positive, with 667 gainers against 456 losers. Sector-wise, both Technology and Healthcare outperformed with gains exceeding 3%, while Financial Services lagged the most. US: Wall Street logged solid gains with the Dow rising 0.5%, the S&P 500 gaining 0.6% to reach new record highs, and the Nasdaq jumping 0.5% higher as US 10-year Treasury yields slipped to 5.3%, while Brent crude hovered at USD100/bbl amid potential Strait of Hormuz supply disruptions. US: Wall Street may retain its constructive tone after the S&P 500 and Nasdaq reached fresh record highs, helped by easing Treasury yields and stabilising oil prices. AI remains a key earnings driver, with Marvell (MRVL) in focus after raising its FY2028 revenue target to USD20.0bn and guiding FY2031 revenue to USD70.0- 90.0bn, underpinned by strong demand for custom AI silicon and optical connectivity. Meanwhile, Salesforce (CRM) could benefit from renewed strength in enterprise software as concerns over AI disruption ease, while Meta (META) continues expanding its AI offerings to businesses through its Meta Enterprise Platform. MY: On the local front, the FBMKLCI is poised to track global tech strength, with sentiment supported by robust earnings and positioning ahead of Budget 2027 on 9 October. The semiconductor and automation space could remain in focus, with semiconductors, AI and high-value investments among the Government's key priorities. UWC stands out after 4QFY26 revenue jumped 71.1% to RM186.2m, while net profit surged 129.7%, reflecting stronger semiconductor demand and project execution. VITROX could also attract interest following a sharp improvement in 2QFY26 earnings. Meanwhile, TOPGLOV offers an earnings-driven play after 4QFY26 revenue rose 39.7% to RM1.25bn, with net profit surging 352.6%. Selective buying provided a minor lift to the local bourse on Tuesday, though the benchmark remains capped under key moving averages. Downside risk persists as the MACD histogram stays below zero while the RSI is oversold below 30. Key resistance is pegged at 1,648-1,663, while support is expected around 1,603-1,618. CIMB Group Holdings Bhd (CIMB) is exploring a sale of its business in the Philippines as part of efforts to streamline and focus on bigger markets for growth, according to people with knowledge of the matter. The Malaysian lender is working with a financial adviser on the potential divestment and has reached out to prospective buyers to gauge interest, said the people. A deal could value the business at as much as US$200m (RM817m). (The Edge) Zetrix AI Bhd (ZETRIX) said the exact amount it owes the Road Transport Department (JPJ) is still being finalised between the two parties, a day after Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook said the company had accumulated RM314m in unpaid remittances. In response to queries from Bursa Malaysia, the group reiterated that it had submitted a payment proposal to settle the arrears, and that the final sum and settlement terms remain subject to further discussions and formal agreement with authorities. (The Edge) Top Glove Corporation Bhd (TOPGLOV) said labour shortage remains a primary constraint in scaling up production as it seeks to capture rising global demand following its best year since 2021. The group is targeting to raise annual running capacity by 8% to 78bn pieces in the financial year ending Aug 31, 2027 (FY2027), from 72bn in FY2026. The group's net profit jumped nearly five times to RM157.63m in the three months ended Aug 31, 2026 (4QFY2026) from RM34.83m in the same quarter a year earlier. Revenue for the quarter surged 40% year-on-year to RM1.25bn. A final dividend of 1.50 sen per share was also declared for FY2026 and payable on Dec 15.
