Samaiden's wholly-owned subsidiary Samaiden Sdn Bhd had on Oct 2 entered into a works contract and a contract for the supply of solar components with Syarikat Pembenaan Yeoh Tiong Lay Sdn Bhd (YTL Construction), the construction unit of YTL Corporation Bhd (YTL). The project is among the LSS5+ projects approved by the Energy Commission in September 2025. (The Edge) Mesiniaga Bhd (MSNIAGA) has won a RM32.3m contract from the Royal Malaysian Customs Department (RMDC) for the maintenance and licence renewal of its MyGST System. The contract marks a continuation of the information technology product and service provider's earlier MyGST system agreement with RMCD that first started in November 2023. The new extension, which takes effect from Oct 16, 2026, will run until Oct 15, 2028. (The Edge) Scientex Bhd (SCIENTX) is acquiring 503 acres in Pulai, Johor, for RM580m to boost the property developer's land bank. The plan is to turn the 14 plots of land currently owned by the Lau family of Leong Hup International Bhd (LHI) into mixed development, the company said. However, it is too early to determine development value and other details, it noted. (The Edge) Dialog Group Bhd (DIALOG) said its 50.01%-owned joint venture company has been awarded concession rights and operatorship for the L8/66 exploration block onshore Thailand. The joint venture company, Pan Orient Energy (Siam) Ltd (POES), was notified by the Thai government on Oct 5 that it had been awarded the concession following a joint bid with CanAsia Energy Corp in Thailand's 25th Onshore Bid Round. POES will operate the concession with a 70% participating interest, while Canada-listed CanAsia will hold the remaining 30% non-operating interest. (The Edge) Elridge Energy Holdings Bhd (ELRIDGE) is investing RM45m to venture into the manufacturing and sale of activated carbon business for use across water treatment, industrial purification and related filtration. This marks Elridge's move further downstream from its existing palm kernel shell biomass operations. Elridge said its wholly-owned subsidiary Lumeria Power Sdn Bhd (LP) had accepted a quotation from United Equipment Services (M) Sdn Bhd for the acquisition, installation and commissioning of six integrated activated carbon production chains for RM45m in cash. (The Edge) Insights Analytics Bhd (IAB), which mainly provides asset management systems to water utilities, has secured a RM14.44m subcontract to construct a water treatment plant in Sarawak's Miri division. The contract involves the construction, operation and maintenance of the Suai water treatment plant, which will have a capacity of seven million litres per day, as part of a project aimed at addressing acute water supply shortages in the Suai area. The construction is scheduled to begin on Oct 13 and to be completed by April 10, 2027, followed by a 60-month operation and maintenance period. (The Edge) Building construction contractor SLGC Bhd (SLG) ended its first trading day on the ACE Market below its initial public offering (IPO) price. The construction firm's shares closed at 25 sen on Tuesday, three sen or 10.71% lower than the IPO price of 28 sen per share, after hitting an intra-day low of 24 sen as more than 83m shares exchanged hands. At the closing price, the company based in Johor had a market capitalisation of RM140m. Ahead of the listing, SLGC shares were oversubscribed by just over three times by retail investors, while a portion of the IPO was undersubscribed and had to be reallocated to other investors. (The Edge) ZenaTech, Inc. (ZENA) advanced its ZenaDrone 2000 heavy-lift autonomous interceptor through prototype assembly in Sharjah, UAE, targeting Q1 2027 flight testing. Built with a 40 kg payload capacity and four-plus hours of hover endurance, the gasoline-powered platform will validate autonomous navigation and multi-target threat pursuit alongside its Interceptor P-1 system. (Investing.com) ONEOK, Inc. (OKE) completed its acquisition of Brazos Midstream's Permian Midland Basin natural gas gathering and processing assets for approximately USD 4.425 billion in cash. The transaction more than doubles ONEOK's Midland Basin processing capacity to roughly 2.3 billion cubic feet per day and adds 600,000 dedicated acres backed by long-term fixed-fee contracts averaging over 12 years. title: 'Bursa Malaysia ditutup tinggi susulan sentimen positif serantau
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia ditutup tinggi hari ini, sejajar dengan peningkatan dalam kebanyakan pasaran utama Asia susulan kenaikan saham teknologi di Wall Street dalam tempoh semalaman, walaupun hasil bon Perbendaharaan Amerika Syarikat (AS) yang tinggi terus mengehadkan minat terhadap risiko. Pada 5 petang, FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) meningkat 1.60 mata kepada 1,633.35 berbanding 1,631.75 semasa ditutup pada Isnin. Indeks petunjuk pasaran itu yang dibuka 4.63 mata lebih tinggi kepada 1,636.38, bergerak antara 1,632.77 dan 1,641.20 sepanjang sesi dagangan. Dalam pasaran secara menyeluruh, kaunter untung mengatasi kaunter rugi sebanyak 667 berbanding 456 manakala 551 kaunter tidak berubah, 1,108 tidak diniagakan dan 13 yang lain digantung dagangan. Jumlah dagangan susut kepada 4.18 bilion unit bernilai RM2.95 bilion berbanding 4.78 bilion unit bernilai RM2.89 bilion semalam. Naib Presiden Penyelidikan Ekuiti Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd Thong Pak Leng berkata hasil bon Perbendaharaan AS dalam tempoh 10 tahun mencecah 5.349 peratus, paras tertinggi sejak 2002 manakala hasil bon 30 tahun meningkat seketika kepada 5.703 peratus. Semasa ditutup pada Isnin, S&P 500 meningkat 0.66 peratus kepada 7,773.95 mata manakala Indeks Komposit Nasdaq naik 1.05 peratus kepada 27,477.31 mata. “Dari sudut positif, harga minyak mentah Brent menyusut di bawah US$100 setong apabila eksport Asia Barat yang kekal kukuh serta pelepasan stok simpanan kecemasan oleh negara-negara Kumpulan Tujuh (G7) membantu mengurangkan kebimbangan terhadap bekalan,” katanya kepada Bernama. Menurutnya di dalam negara, minat belian dapat dilihat dalam saham telekomunikasi dan berkaitan komoditi manakala aktiviti dagangan turut meluas kepada beberapa kaunter teknologi bermodal kecil, tenaga dan perladangan. “Kami yakin bahawa saham mewah terpilih boleh terus menarik aktiviti pembelian saham ketika harga rendah susulan pembetulan yang ketara minggu lepas. Bagaimanapun, ketiadaan pembelian susulan sepanjang tiga sesi dagangan lepas menunjukkan pelabur terus berwaspada, dengan jualan berterusan oleh pelabur asing dan hasil bon yang tinggi dijangka mengehadkan kadar pemulihan,” katanya. title: 'Bursa Malaysia Stays Higher At Midday Tracking Regional Markets
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 – Bursa Malaysia maintained its positive momentum at midday on Tuesday, October 6, 2026, tracking regional equity market gains following an overnight rally on Wall Street powered by megacap technology stocks and artificial intelligence (AI) investment optimism. At 12:30 PM, the benchmark FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) advanced 5.49 points, or 0.34 per cent, to trade at 1,637.24 compared to Monday’s closing mark of 1,631.75. After opening 4.63 points higher at 1,636.38, the index fluctuated within a range of 1,635.21 to 1,641.20 during the morning trading session. Global Dynamics and Market Breadth Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB) noted that strong earnings momentum and robust AI investments supported US markets despite rising Treasury yields. Key market factors and breadth metrics at midday include: - Global Commodity & Debt Markets: Brent crude oil eased below US$102 per barrel amid recovering West Asia exports, G7 emergency stockpile releases, and Saudi price cuts. Meanwhile, the US 10-year Treasury yield rose to 5.33 per cent amid persistent inflation concerns. - Market Breadth: Advancing counters outpaced decliners 524 to 428, with 520 counters remaining unchanged, 1,310 untraded, and 13 suspended. - Trading Volume: Total turnover reached 2.36 billion units valued at RM1.24 billion. Top Stock Movements and Sector Performance Gains across technology, consumer products, and plantation counters helped sustain the market’s upward drive. Key individual stock and sector highlights include: - Heavyweights: Maybank rose two sen to RM10.02 and IHH Healthcare gained seven sen to RM7.83. Public Bank fell five sen to RM4.66, CIMB shed two sen to RM7.71, and Tenaga Nasional traded flat at RM13.00. - Active Counters: Zetrix AI rose three sen to 9.5 sen, while ACE Market debutant SLGC fell three sen to 25 sen. V.S Industry dropped half a sen to 31.5 sen and Ramssol slipped two sen to 81.5 sen. - Top Gainers: Technology and plantation stocks posted sharp gains, led by Malaysian Pacific Industries (up 86 sen to RM44.26), Nestle (up 70 sen to RM90.70), Kuala Lumpur Kepong (up 48 sen to RM21.34), Mi Technovation (up 38 sen to RM5.79), and Batu Kawan (up 24 sen to RM19.22). - Top Decliners: Dutch Lady Milk Industries led losses, falling 40 sen to RM29.60, followed by BLD Plantation (down 18 sen to RM14.82), Ayer Holdings (down 15 sen to RM7.55), Samaiden (down 12 sen to RM3.07), and Kelington (down 10 sen to RM9.02). - Sectoral Indices: The Plantation Index surged 114.24 points to 9,045.27, the Energy Index gained 5.98 points to 835.92, and the Industrial Products and Services Index edged up 0.98 of a point to 179.95. The Financial Services Index declined 20.24 points to 19,119.90. On the broader index board, the FBM Mid 70 Index jumped 97.32 points to 17,640.81, the FBM Emas Shariah Index gained 74.37 points to 12,143.38, and the FBM ACE Index added 8.10 points to reach 5,614.71. –NMT

title: 'Bursa Malaysia Opens Higher On Positive Wall Street Momentum
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 – Bursa Malaysia opened higher on Tuesday morning, tracking positive overnight momentum on Wall Street as subdued crude oil prices—driven by a recovery in West Asia crude exports—helped offset a ongoing sell-off in US Treasuries. At 9:21 AM, the benchmark FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) advanced 7.14 points, or 0.44 per cent, to reach 1,638.89 compared to Monday’s close of 1,631.75. The index had initially opened 4.63 points higher at 1,636.38. Across the broader market, advancing counters outpaced decliners 272 to 202, with 364 counters remaining unchanged, 1,944 untraded, and 13 suspended. Market turnover stood at 440.19 million units valued at RM164.76 million. Heavyweight Movements and Sector Performance Heavyweight banking and energy-linked stocks led the early morning gains, helping push all main index boards higher. Key market movements across categories during early trade included: - Heavyweight Performance: Maybank and Tenaga Nasional each gained four sen to RM10.04 and RM13.04, respectively, while CIMB rose three sen to RM7.76. IHH Healthcare added two sen to RM7.78, while Public Bank traded flat at RM4.71. - Active Counters: Zetrix AI inched up half a sen to seven sen, Divfex added one sen to 16.5 sen, and Ramssol rose 2.5 sen to 86 sen. Meanwhile, ACE Market debutant SLGC fell 3.5 sen to 24.5 sen, and Dagang NeXchange edged down half a sen to 50 sen. - Top Gainers: Plantation counters saw strong demand, led by Batu Kawan, which surged RM1.24 to RM20.22. Nestle and Kuala Lumpur Kepong gained 20 sen each to RM90.20 and RM21.06, respectively, followed by Petronas Dagangan (up 18 sen to RM19.38) and Genting Plantations (up 16 sen to RM5.82). - Top Decliners: HeiTech Padu dropped seven sen to 88 sen, while Thong Guan Industries, Sunway Construction Group, and Allianz Malaysia declined six sen each to RM1.44, RM7.55, and RM20.74, respectively. UMS Integration lost four sen to trade at RM9.36. - Index Breakdown: The Plantation Index posted significant gains, jumping 73.78 points to 9,004.81. The Financial Services Index surged 56.47 points to 19,196.61, the Energy Index gained 1.78 points to 831.72, and the Industrial Products and Services Index edged up 0.16 of a point to 179.13. The FBM Mid 70 Index advanced 41.29 points to 17,584.78, the FBM Emas Index added 44.30 points to 12,234.65, and the FBM ACE Index rose 7.73 points to 5,614.34. –NMT

title: 'Carbon Tax Deferment Gives Ministry More Time to Finalise Regulatory, Policy Framework, Says Arthur
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 5): The deferment of the carbon tax implementation is aligned with the Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry’s efforts to establish a complete regulatory and policy framework before enforcing emission caps. Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said the government decided to delay the tax, originally planned for this year, following global geopolitical developments that led to volatile energy prices, providing affected industries with a necessary buffer. Speaking during a Concorde Club dialogue session at Wisma Bernama on Monday, he said the postponement is also timely as the ministry works towards solidifying the required legal structure, including the National Carbon Market Policy and the upcoming Climate Change Act. “[The postponement] is also right because we need to have the proper framework and all that in place first. That’s why we’ve been successful in launching the National Carbon Market Policy and I hope that we can table the Climate Change Act soon. “Once that is up, then we have the framework and the policies all clearly in place, including the regulation, enforcement, the regulatory powers to give us to set the emission ceiling, and then we can know anything above the ceiling, then the carbon tax will come into place as a penalty to the polluters. “So, we’re not looking at this year for the carbon tax,” he said. Meanwhile, on Clean Air Regulations exemption, Arthur said exemptions for industrial plants under the regulation would only be extended to factory operators who demonstrate proactive measures toward technology adoption. He said while no new blanket extensions are being issued, factory operators whose exemptions expire by January next year must show clear steps toward compliance, with 2030 set as the final deadline for total compliance across all industries. “We had the Clean Air Regulations, which came into force in 2014, where plants, factories are not allowed to pollute above the 600 milligram per cubic metre...that was the regulation set...however, they have been enjoying exemptions up to this year. “So when I came in as the minister, I decided that I will not be issuing any more exemptions because the technology is available, the technology is accessible and if we are to meet our target of net zero emissions by 2050, we need to have all this in place and we definitely need the cooperation from the industries as well,” he said. He added that while operators need adequate time for feasibility studies and modifications, strict progress is required to qualify for temporary extensions. The session, titled “Building A Resilient Malaysia: Environment, Climate And Our Future”, was moderated by Bernama chairman Datuk Seri Wong Chun Wai. Also present was Bernama chief executive officer Datin Paduka Nur-ul Afida Kamaludin, as well as members of the local and foreign media based in Malaysia. title: 'Bar Fails in Bid to Challenge Ex-AG Terrirudin's Appointment to Judicial Appointments Commission
body: '"The JAC merely recommends. The power of appointment lies with the Yang di-Pertuan Agong on the prime minister’s advice under [the law]. The alleged fear of bias from one of nine members of a body that decides nothing is remote, indirect, and speculative.” — High Court judge Norliza Othman. KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 5): The Malaysian Bar has failed to get the green light to challenge former attorney general (AG) and sitting Federal Court judge Tan Sri Ahmad Terrirudin Mohd Salleh's appointment to the Judicial Appointments Commission (JAC). In dismissing the Bar's leave (permission) application to commence a judicial review, High Court judge Norliza Othman on Monday said that Terrirudin's appointment satisfies the criterium in law, namely that an apex court judge must be appointed by the prime minister. She said that the law does not extend to other implied requirements, such as seniority or length of service, as contended by the Bar. "[The law] is plain. It specifies the category of person: a Federal Court judge; and the appointing authority: the prime minister — and stops there. The applicant asserts both are satisfied, yet asks the court to read in implied requirements: seniority, length of service, prior High Court/Court of Appeal experience, freedom from unresolved allegations, consultation, and conformity with an asserted convention — none of which appear in the text. "Our function is to interpret the words used, not to supply the words omitted," she said adding that case law is against the Bar in this case. Terrirudin, who was appointed a Federal Court judge in November 2025, is serving a two-year term on the JAC, from Nov 15, 2025 to Nov 14, 2027. The JAC is a nine-member body responsible for recommending candidates for appointment to Malaysia's superior courts. The ex-AG's appointment drew brickbats from many quarters, with many highlighting that his selection departed from established practice by bypassing a more senior judge and could undermine perceptions of judicial independence. In the midst of this, the Bar filed the leave application on Feb 12, naming Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, the JAC, and the Malaysian government as respondents. Among the reliefs sought, the Bar is asking the court to quash Terrirudin's appointment, prohibit his appointment to any judicial office pending disposal of the proceedings, and compel the disclosure of minutes from a JAC meeting held on May 16, 2025. In her grounds of judgement, Norliza said that the Bar's argument that Terriruddin's appointment was irrational fails, as "nothing here is so deprived of logic or accepted moral standards that no sensible decision-maker could have reached it". She added that the Bar's argument that the decision contained illegality also failed. She added that the Bar also lacked locus standi to bring the action as they were not adversely affected by the appointment. "The JAC merely recommends," she said in her judgement, adding, "The power of appointment lies with the Yang di-Pertuan Agong on the prime minister's advice under [the law]. The alleged fear of bias from one of nine members of a body that decides nothing is remote, indirect, and speculative.” She ordered cost of RM3,000 to be paid to the Attorney General's Chambers (AGC). Former Bar presidents Zainur Zakaria, Steven Thiru and Datuk Ambiga Sreevenasan appeared for the Bar while senior federal counsel Datuk Shamsul Bolhassan led the team appearing for the AGC. title: 'Bolsonaro Beats Expectations in Brazil Presidential Vote, Will Face Lula in Run-off
body: 'BRASILIA/SAO PAULO/RIO DE JANEIRO (Oct 5): Right-wing Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro will face leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in a run-off of the presidential election later this month, after he exceeded expectations in Sunday's first-round vote with a slight lead over the incumbent. The election, which centred around the cost of living, corruption and insecurity in Brazilians' daily lives, follows a string of wins across Latin America by right-wing parties aligned with US President Donald Trump. Bolsonaro's stronger-than-expected performance, at 47% of votes versus Lula's 45%, is expected to buoy his campaign and may bolster Brazil's currency and stock market, which have risen on the prospects of the business-friendly challenger. Private surveys in the run-up to the election had forecast Lula leading the first-round vote by around three percentage points. "Brazil wants change and I am very happy with the results," Bolsonaro told reporters in Brasilia after nearly all tallies were reported, heralding "the end of the era of (Lula's) Workers' Party." title: 'Cara mengelola keuangan di tengah gaya hidup tanpa dompet
body: 'JawaPos.com - Gaya hidup tanpa dompet fisik semakin lekat dengan keseharian generasi muda. Berbagai kebutuhan, mulai dari transaksi hingga menyiapkan dana masa depan, kini dapat dilakukan melalui layanan digital.  Melihat trend ini,  PT Bank CIMB Niaga Tbk (CIMB Niaga) meluncurkan OCTO untuk Pejuang Mimpi, sebuah inisiatif yang dirancang untuk membantu generasi muda mengelola keuangan secara lebih mudah, praktis, dan relevan dengan gaya hidup digital masa kini.  Head of Marketing, Brand & Customers Experience CIMB Niaga Amir Widjaya mengatakan, di tengah berbagai peluang yang tersedia saat ini, kemampuan mengelola keuangan menjadi salah satu fondasi penting agar generasi muda dapat terus berkembang dan mencapai tujuan hidup mereka.  “Karena itu, CIMB Niaga ingin hadir sebagai partner yang membantu mereka mengambil langkah finansial yang tepat sejak dini,” ujar Amir Widjaya pada talkshow “OCTO Go Dompetless, Wear Pocketless” yang menjadi bagian dari rangkaian Kejar Mimpi FEST 2026 di Senayan City, Jakarta, Sabtu (3/10/2026).  Untuk menjawab kebutuhan tersebut, CIMB Niaga menghadirkan OCTO melalui pendekatan Jurus O-C-T-O, yaitu Olah Dana, Capai Mimpi, Tangkis Risiko, dan Optimalkan Keseruan.  Melalui OCTO, generasi muda dapat mengelola kebutuhan finansial sehari-hari, menabung, berinvestasi, mempersiapkan dana untuk masa depan, serta menikmati berbagai pengalaman hidup secara lebih bijak.  Generasi muda juga dapat membuka rekening secara digital hanya dalam beberapa menit dan menikmati berbagai kemudahan transaksi sehari-hari, mulai dari transfer, pembayaran, dan top up e-wallet hingga akses ke berbagai pilihan tabungan dan investasi. Kemudahan tersebut dihadirkan agar mereka dapat memulai perjalanan finansial dengan lebih praktis dan sesuai kebutuhan.  Adopsi OCTO terus menunjukkan tren positif. Pada semester I 2026, transaksi QRIS melalui OCTO meningkat 65% secara year-on-year (YoY), sementara pembukaan rekening pertama melalui OCTO tumbuh 89% YoY. Selain itu, transaksi reksa dana meningkat 48% YoY dan transaksi obligasi naik 112% YoY, mencerminkan semakin tingginya preferensi nasabah terhadap layanan perbankan digital yang praktis, mudah, dan terintegrasi.  Pada kesempatan yang sama, CIMB Niaga juga memperkenalkan kampanye Go Dompetless, Wear Pocketless yang merefleksikan perubahan gaya hidup generasi muda yang semakin mengandalkan teknologi digital dalam berbagai aktivitas sehari-hari, termasuk bertransaksi dan mengelola keuangan.  “Go Dompetless, Wear Pocketless bukan sekadar soal meninggalkan dompet fisik. Ini merupakan simbol gaya hidup yang lebih praktis, fleksibel, dan efisien. Ketika urusan finansial menjadi lebih mudah, anak muda memiliki lebih banyak ruang untuk fokus mengembangkan potensi, mengejar passion, dan mewujudkan mimpi yang ingin mereka capai,” kata Amir.  Sebagai bagian dari rangkaian acara, CIMB Niaga menghadirkan fashion show bertema Pocketless, sebuah kampanye dengan semangat “The New Fashion Movement in Jakarta” yang mengeksplorasi semangat generasi muda dalam mengekspresikan diri.  “Kami percaya setiap generasi memiliki cara sendiri untuk mengejar mimpi. Melalui OCTO, kami ingin membantu generasi muda mengambil keputusan finansial dengan lebih percaya diri dan memiliki lebih banyak ruang untuk fokus pada aspirasi yang ingin mereka wujudkan,” tutup Amir.

title: 'Bursa Malaysia ditutup tinggi susulan selera risiko bertambah baik
body: 'H: Bursa Malaysia ditutup tinggi susulan sentimen risiko bertambah baik KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia ditutup sedikit tinggi pada 5 Oktorber seiring pasaran serantau yang positif, susulan selera risiko bertambah baik berikutan data pekerjaan Amerika Syarikat (AS) yang lebih lemah, sekali gus mengurangkan jangkaan kenaikan kadar faedah lanjut oleh Rizab Persekutuan AS (Fed) dan meredakan tekanan terhadap hasil bon. Pada jam 5 petang, FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) meningkat 0.88 mata kepada 1,631.75 berbanding 1,630.87 pada penutupan Jumaat lalu. Indeks penanda aras itu dibuka 2.55 mata lebih tinggi pada 1,633.42 dan bergerak antara paras 1,630.95 hingga 1,640.46 sepanjang sesi dagangan. Bagaimanapun, di pasaran lebih meluas, kaunter rugi mengatasi kaunter untung dengan 599 berbanding 564, manakala 523 kaunter tidak berubah, 1,087 tidak diniagakan dan 24 kaunter digantung. Jumlah dagangan meningkat kepada 4.78 bilion unit bernilai RM2.89 bilion berbanding 4.23 bilion unit bernilai RM2.70 bilion pada Jumaat lalu. Naib Presiden Penyelidikan Ekuiti Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd, Thong Pak Leng, berkata saham teknologi antara yang mendapat manfaat utama daripada sentimen pasaran yang bertambah baik. Beliau berkata, di Wall Street pada Jumaat lalu, S&P 500 meningkat 0.73 peratus kepada 7,722.72 mata, manakala Nasdaq Composite menokok 1.19 peratus kepada 27,190.86 mata. "Bagi pasaran tempatan, kami kekal sedikit positif dalam tempoh terdekat kerana FBM KLCI masih berada dalam keadaan terlebih jual selepas pembetulan ketara minggu lalu, yang sepatutnya terus menarik aktiviti pembelian ketika harga rendah, khususnya dalam saham mewah terpilih. "Kecairan domestik juga kekal menyokong pasaran, dengan institusi tempatan merekodkan pembelian bersih RM352.4 juta minggu lalu, walaupun jualan berterusan oleh pelabur asing kekal sebagai cabaran," katanya kepada Bernama. Sehubungan itu, Thong menjangkakan indeks penanda aras akan mencatat pemulihan secara beransur-ansur, namun kekal tidak menentu, dengan FBM KLCI dijangka didagangkan dalam julat 1,620 hingga 1,650 mata minggu ini. Dalam kalangan saham berwajaran tinggi, Public Bank meningkat lima sen kepada RM4.71, CIMB menokok lapan sen kepada RM7.73, Tenaga Nasional naik empat sen kepada RM13.00, Maybank susut dua sen kepada RM10.00, manakala IHH Healthcare turun empat sen kepada RM7.76. Dalam dagangan aktif, V.S Industry meningkat tiga sen kepada 32 sen, Zetrix AI susut lima sen kepada 6.5 sen, Jaks Resources turun satu sen kepada 17 sen, Excel Force MSC merosot empat sen kepada 17 sen, manakala NationGate tidak berubah pada RM1.83. Antara kaunter untung utama, Malaysian Pacific Industries meningkat RM1.00 kepada RM43.40, UMS Integration melonjak 37 sen kepada RM9.40, Kelington menokok 49 sen kepada RM9.12, Nestle meningkat 48 sen kepada RM90.00, manakala Samaiden melonjak 35 sen kepada RM3.19. Kaunter rugi utama diketuai Batu Kawan yang merosot RM1.48 kepada RM18.98, diikuti United Plantations yang susut 32 sen kepada RM31.06, Hengyuan Refining Company turun 18 sen kepada RM3.46, manakala Kuala Lumpur Kepong dan YTL Power International masing-masing susut 14 sen kepada RM20.86 dan RM5.54. Di papan indeks, FBM Mid 70 meningkat 61.56 mata kepada 17,543.49, FBM Emas menokok 19.78 mata kepada 12,190.35, FBM Top 100 naik 15.70 mata kepada 11,973.38, FBM Emas Shariah meningkat 8.69 mata kepada 12,069.01, manakala FBM ACE melonjak 77.15 mata kepada 5,606.61. Mengikut sektor, Indeks Produk dan Perkhidmatan Perindustrian meningkat 0.45 mata kepada 178.97, Indeks Perkhidmatan Kewangan menokok 99.63 mata kepada 19,140.14, manakala Indeks Tenaga susut 3.09 mata kepada 829.94 dan Indeks Perladangan merosot 125.52 mata kepada 8,931.03. Jumlah dagangan di Pasaran Utama meningkat kepada 3.13 bilion unit bernilai RM2.41 bilion daripada 2.67 bilion unit bernilai RM2.34 bilion pada Jumaat lalu. Dagangan waran meningkat kepada 1.04 bilion unit bernilai RM208.20 juta berbanding 973.40 juta unit bernilai RM160.21 juta sebelumnya. Jumlah dagangan di Pasaran ACE meningkat kepada 611.02 juta unit bernilai RM267.66 juta daripada 593.05 juta unit bernilai RM205.21 juta pada Jumaat. Sementara itu, kaunter produk dan perkhidmatan pengguna mencatatkan 248.10 juta saham didagangkan di Pasaran Utama, produk dan perkhidmatan perindustrian (439.37 juta), pembinaan (183.56 juta), teknologi (1.76 bilion), perkhidmatan kewangan (49.02 juta), hartanah (106.95 juta), perladangan (22.08 juta), amanah pelaburan hartanah (10.76 juta), dana tertutup (152,900), tenaga (106.66 juta), penjagaan kesihatan (103.20 juta), telekomunikasi dan media (22.11 juta), pengangkutan dan logistik (40.92 juta), utiliti (38.48 juta) serta amanah perniagaan (162,200). --BERNAMA

title: 'Cover Story: Playing the long game at Forest City
body: 'Cover Story: Playing the long game at Forest City This article first appeared in City & Country, The Edge Malaysia Weekly on September 28, 2026 - October 4, 2026 It was a scorching afternoon when Country Garden Pacificview Sdn Bhd (CGPV) executive director and chief of regional industrial business development Kevin Li and regional vice-president Syarul Izam Sarifudin arrived at The Edge’s office in Petaling Jaya, Selangor. The pair had flown in from Johor Bahru to give an update on Forest City, a high-profile project in Johor that has dealt with some hot issues since its inception. “What we achieved [since 2015] up to 2025 was merely concentrating more on our operational stability, resource integration and preparing for our next phase of growth,” says Syarul. “In the early years, we were primarily viewed as a residential real estate developer. But we are now embarking into a new sector — managing townships and driving actual economic nodes of financial and industrial development in southern Johor.” The master developer of Forest City is a joint venture between China-headquartered developer Country Garden Holdings Co Ltd and Esplanade Danga 88 Sdn Bhd. Operating as an independent local management unit under Country Garden Malaysia’s executive umbrella, CGPV is responsible for Forest City’s master plan development and management, industrial park development and Special Financial Zone (SFZ) operation. Officially launched by the Malaysian government with duty-free island status in 2016, the 7,500-acre integrated development covers four reclaimed man-made islands over 5,000 acres and 2,500 acres on the mainland. Located in Iskandar Puteri, it sits along the Straits of Johor near the Malaysia-Singapore Second Link, just 2km across the water from Singapore. The ambitious development has made international headlines over the years, some of them for the wrong reasons, especially since it has fallen short of market expectations in terms of progress, sales and occupancy rates. These challenges were compounded by the Covid-19 pandemic and the well-documented financial restructuring of its parent company amid China’s broader real estate liquidity crisis. “When China’s property market faced a systemic downturn, amplified by global supply chain disruptions, macroeconomic shifts and strict pandemic controls, Country Garden — once China’s top property developer — was caught in the crossfire, just like many other big players in the country. However, late last year, our parent group successfully executed onshore and offshore debt restructurings in China,” says Li, who is also the chief financial officer of Country Garden Malaysia. Regardless of the situation faced by its parent company, he highlights that Country Garden Malaysia operates with complete operational and financial independence. “Since Country Garden entered Malaysia as its first overseas destination back in 2010 and 2011, the local operation has relied on an independent management team. For the past three years, our cash flow has been generated entirely within the country, allowing us to remain self-sustaining in terms of liquidity and debt servicing,” he says, adding that all five of its projects in the Klang Valley and Johor are performing steadily. According to Li, Country Garden Malaysia’s sales and cash collection was RM1.3 billion in 2023, more than RM1.1 billion in 2024, and RM1.3 billion in 2025. “More crucially, we utilised our local cash flows to fully settle bank borrowings and capital market obligations worth about RM2 billion over the past three years, including a RM1 billion sukuk … As at earlier this year, the remaining outstanding amount [of the sukuk] was only RM150 million. We pre-repaid them as our cash flow was comfortable.” With most of its debts cleared, local rating agency RAM upgraded Country Garden Malaysia’s outlook rating from negative to stable in March, reflecting its balance-sheet resilience despite global sector volatility. That financial stability has been supported by developments on the legal front. Malaysian courts have recently upheld the validity of sales and purchase agreements in favour of the developer. Dismissing buyer suits seeking to void contracts for reasons such as media portrayals of the project as a “ghost town”, the courts established that market downturns and post-purchase regret do not constitute grounds for breach. The decisions shield CGPV against speculative contract cancellations and protect its revenue base. “Forest City has completed and delivered 26,000 residential units so far. We understand that we cannot make every single person happy, and it is normal to receive feedback or complaints. We respect the buyers’ legal rights,” Li says. “But we also have our internal KPIs [key performance indicators] to meet. We are pleased to share that customer satisfaction consistently hits above 95% in our surveys and polls. Generally, the majority of our 20,000 residents are happy to live here, or they wouldn’t choose to continue staying. This is evidenced by our growing population.” A city waking up Today, Forest City is home to around 20,000 people living in 66 completed blocks, over 770 acres of the approved 5,000-acre reclaimed island land bank. “If you pass by from Iskandar Puteri towards Batam, you can see the lights on across the residential towers at night,” Syarul says. “It is a night-and-day difference compared with what people experienced immediately after the pandemic in early 2021.” Demographics have shifted significantly, he adds. While buyers were once predominantly mainland Chinese, the current resident base is largely local Malaysians, many of whom commute daily to Singapore or work in nearby industrial parks, as well as expatriates of different nationalities. “The township’s commercial pulse is also quickening,” says Syarul. “The Fisherman’s Wharf commercial street has seen steady footfall, with duty-free shops, eateries and premier banking facilities, including branches of Maybank and CIMB, with Affin Bank and AmBank joining the fold soon.” Forest City attracts between 1.5 million and two million tourists annually. Its crown jewel is Forest City Golf Resort, located on the mainland about 9km from the man-made islands. Featuring two 18-hole international championship courses, it draws golfers from Japan, South Korea and Singapore. There is also an affordable beachfront water park that offers weekend entertainment for visiting families. “Forest City is probably the only sandy beach in Johor Bahru. Otherwise, you have to go to Desaru, which is an hour away. To draw more visitors, we are also collaborating with some watersports academies on courses for adults and children. The beach and water park are very popular during school holidays and weekends, contributing to our growing annual tourist and visitor numbers,” Syarul says. Meanwhile, Network School, a start-up society and experimental community based on Silicon Valley entrepreneur Balaji Srinivasan’s book The Network State, was set up in the township in October 2024. Balaji’s private co-living and co-working hub at Marina Hotel drew hundreds of international digital nomads, crypto enthusiasts and tech workers. However, in July 2026, the Iskandar Puteri City Council (MBIP) revoked the Network School operator’s business licence for breaching local licensing conditions. The management of the school clarified that CGPV operates solely as a commercial landlord, and that the developer is fully cooperating with the local authorities to ensure all commercial tenants adhere to the regulatory framework. Strategic shift Li says while Forest City’s master plan is unchanged, CGPV is shifting its focus towards commercial and industrial developments, in alignment with the government’s broader economic development plan for the state. “We maintain the master plan as it is because, to us, it is still a very fantastic plan even after a decade. Of course, for such a mega development, you have to do it in phases, and there will be small twists and adjustments in between. But overall, we do not have plans to review the master plan. Now, we are embarking on the third phase of development. We foresee the entire master plan being completed only by 2040. It is now 12% to 13% developed,” says Syarul. The biggest “twists and adjustments” to the master plan were its integration into the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) and designation as an SFZ. In August 2023, the government announced that Forest City would be designated as an SFZ to boost foreign investment, with incentives such as a 15% income tax rate for skilled workers and lower business operating costs. A year later, the government launched the tax incentive framework for the SFZ, which includes a zero tax rate for single family offices (SFO), a 5% corporate tax rate for fintech and global business services, and concessionary income tax rates. In early 2025, Malaysia and Singapore signed a bilateral agreement to establish the JS-SEZ. Under the agreement, Forest City was formally incorporated as Flagship G, one of nine primary flagship zones within the 3,505 sq km economic zone. “We started [the master plan] with residential and, maybe, this made people misunderstand that Forest City is focusing on high-rise residential developments. The SFZ designation puts us right back on track to [industrial projects],” says Li. “Under the SFZ blueprint, the development is divided into two distinct functional zones, where the island component acts as a core financial services hub, focusing on single-family offices, fintech, foreign payment operating systems and back-office financial services. Meanwhile, the mainland focuses on smart logistics, high-tech manufacturing and global business services.” To encourage direct investments in Forest City, the Malaysian government established the Iskandar Malaysia Facilitation Centre Johor (IMFC-J) at Forest City’s 42-storey primary office tower, Menara Delima Satu, to streamline the investment process. The centre houses 18 government agencies under one roof and acts as a single processing point for foreign investors. “A key cornerstone of the SFZ is attracting family offices. The SC (Securities Commission) set an AUM (assets under management) threshold of RM30 million for family offices setting up in Forest City, a far more accessible entry point compared with Singapore’s S$15 million (RM47.9 million) requirement or Hong Kong’s HK$240 million (RM124.7 million) benchmark,” Li says. Syarul stresses, however, that Malaysia is not competing with Singapore or Hong Kong in the SFO segment but is instead complementing them. “It is about synergy. Under the SFZ rules, family offices in Forest City can invest up to 90% of their AUM globally. This means that investors can set up their operational base here in Forest City at one-third to one-fourth of the operational cost, while still leveraging Singapore’s capital markets just across the strait. It is very attractive to many family offices,” he explains. Under the SFO Incentive Scheme guidelines issued by the SC, it is mandatory to establish a physical office in Forest City to qualify for and maintain SC approval and the accompanying 0% tax incentive. According to Li, over 40 SFOs have secured physical office space in Forest City, with nine having formally received SC approval to date. “We are very positive about this, though we do not have an actual target of having many of them in Forest City in the near future because it is beyond our control and SC has its plan. But it is a strong catalyst in helping to add vibrancy to Forest City because when the offices come, they bring in their professional teams — accountants, lawyers and finance and investment experts,” he adds. Forest City is also targeting global business services. CGPV is in advanced discussions with two major international banking institutions — one looking to relocate its back-office operations from Singapore, and another expanding its operational footprint from Kuala Lumpur. Forest City 2.0 Despite the tailwinds from the SFZ, Li and Syarul acknowledge that transforming the mega project into a self-sustaining regional economy is not without immediate, real-world hurdles. The most pressing challenge currently is cross-border physical connectivity and accessibility. “While the project is geographically proximate to Singapore, seamlessly moving people, goods and daily commuters across borders remains a complex, multi-jurisdictional effort,” says Li. “Furthermore, regional competition from peers like Thailand, Indonesia and Vietnam means that Malaysia must continually sharpen its execution speed and policy delivery to stay ahead.” To close this connectivity gap, Country Garden is taking interim measures while lobbying government authorities for long-term infrastructure approvals. “Before all the major government infrastructure projects are completed, we are bridging the gap ourselves. We currently run daily direct shuttles transferring residents and workers to the Sultan Abu Bakar CIQ Second Link complex,” Li says. For the long term, the developer has submitted plans to the joint Malaysia-Singapore ministerial committee under the Iskandar Regional Development Authority (IRDA) for a dedicated ferry terminal. Once approved, ferry routes will connect Forest City directly to Raffles Marina in Singapore and Batam in Indonesia. “We are also asking the government for assistance to permit a direct highway connection linking straight to Tuas, and to integrate Forest City into upcoming regional rail routes like the RTS [Rapid Transit System], ART [Automated Rapid Transit] and transport corridors heading to Kulai and Senai,” he adds. “Moving people efficiently is crucial to unlocking the full value of the JS-SEZ but because these are country-to-country matters, we have to keep pushing and following up continuously.” Simultaneously, the master developer is pivoting to boosting population density and creating high-value local jobs, away from traditional residential property sales, towards what the team calls “Forest City 2.0”. “We are not launching any more residential projects in the near future, but focusing on clearing the inventory. We will advance commercial and industrial land development earlier than originally scheduled to inject immediate economic vibrancy,” Li says. “Our next focus is to bring in companies and industries to invest or establish their presence here.” Acknowledging the importance of generating sufficient jobs to increase Forest City’s population, CGPV is actively trying to draw data centres, logistics players and manufacturers to its upcoming 418-acre industrial park. “We need to create real economic dynamics. If you don’t generate jobs and economic substance, you cannot sustain a population,” Li stresses. The response to this industrial shift has been positive. In the first half of this year alone, the developer logged over 300 company enquiries and secured a 40-acre industrial land deal with a manufacturer in Phase 1 of the industrial park, paving the way for ready-built factory developments in Phase 2 should market demand sustain. In another strategic partnership, Country Garden recently signed a term sheet with Penang-based Oriental Holdings Bhd (KL:ORIENT) to develop a RM750 million healthcare hub in Forest City, anchored by a 500-bed hospital alongside comprehensive medical supply chain services. “Internationally, we are actively introducing Forest City to big-name [multinational corporations]. It is not so much for their name, but the entire supply chain. We are looking to bring in ‘queen bee’ investors,” Li says. “We have been doing roadshows, especially in China, to introduce the JS-SEZ and Forest City SFZ. We went to Shenzhen and Suzhou, which have some of the most successful industrial parks in China.” Apart from the industrial park, CGPV has also received enquiries from international investors interested in private island parcels. “It is something that we are looking at. Instead of standard residential towers, we can custom-reclaim approved island plots, such as 1.5 to two acres, based entirely on an investor’s specific operational or residential requirements. It’s about being adaptive to what the current market actually demands,” he says. Road to 2030 and beyond Apart from Forest City, Country Garden Malaysia has four other major developments in Johor and the Klang Valley, executed largely through JVs. “Out of our five projects in Malaysia, four are structured as JVs,” Li explains. “Only Danga Bay is 100% held by Country Garden Malaysia. We welcome JVs because local partners bring value to the table, though for master site design, we prefer to lead.” In Johor Bahru, Country Garden Central Park has completed three phases comprising over 3,000 residential units that are nearly fully sold. The developer is now planning subsequent sub-phases over a 10- to 12-year development cycle. In Kuala Lumpur, the initial two phases of township development Lake City in Taman Wahyu are completed and sold out, with Phase 3 scheduled for launch next year. The remaining four parcels have been earmarked for development over a 15-year period. In Semenyih, Selangor, residential development Diamond City launched its final landed parcel in September 2025, which is expected to wrap up construction within two years. With a substantial land bank in its existing portfolio, the developer will focus its resources on executing its active pipeline over the next decade. As the interview draws to a close, both Li and Syarul reflect on the long-term nature of master township development. “Rome was not built in a day,” Li says. “When we first came to this coastal area in Johor, it was completely rural. Today, the infrastructure is firmly established. Development never moves in a straight upward line; it moves in spirals, but it always moves forward. “We wish the public to know that since the first day Country Garden has been here in Malaysia, we have wanted to be here long term. Of course, there are twists and turns over the years, but we cannot deny the contribution of the company in Malaysia.” He says Country Garden has invested RM32 billion in Malaysia, including RM20 billion in Forest City alone. “We have created jobs, contributed to the country’s tax revenues and trained local skilled workers. Most importantly, after so many challenges and uncertainties, we were here, and we are still here today. The fundamentals are in place, and we have absolute faith in what Forest City will become.” Save by subscribing to us for your print and/or digital copy. In the first half of this year alone, the developer logged over 300 company enquiries and secured a 40-acre industrial land deal with a manufacturer in Phase 1 of the industrial park, paving the way for ready-built factory developments in Phase 2 should market demand sustain. In another strategic partnership, Country Garden recently signed a term sheet with Penang-based Oriental Holdings Bhd (KL:ORIENT) to develop a RM750 million healthcare hub in Forest City, anchored by a 500-bed hospital alongside comprehensive medical supply chain services. “Internationally, we are actively introducing Forest City to big-name [multinational corporations]. It is not so much for their name, but the entire supply chain. We are looking to bring in ‘queen bee’ investors,” Li says. “We have been doing roadshows, especially in China, to introduce the JS-SEZ and Forest City SFZ. We went to Shenzhen and Suzhou, which have some of the most successful industrial parks in China.” Apart from the industrial park, CGPV has also received enquiries from international investors interested in private island parcels. “It is something that we are looking at. Instead of standard residential towers, we can custom-reclaim approved island plots, such as 1.5 to two acres, based entirely on an investor’s specific operational or residential requirements. It’s about being adaptive to what the current market actually demands,” he says. Road to 2030 and beyond Apart from Forest City, Country Garden Malaysia has four other major developments in Johor and the Klang Valley, executed largely through JVs. “Out of our five projects in Malaysia, four are structured as JVs,” Li explains. “Only Danga Bay is 100% held by Country Garden Malaysia. We welcome JVs because local partners bring value to the table, though for master site design, we prefer to lead.” In Johor Bahru, Country Garden Central Park has completed three phases comprising over 3,000 residential units that are nearly fully sold. The developer is now planning subsequent sub-phases over a 10- to 12-year development cycle. In Kuala Lumpur, the initial two phases of township development Lake City in Taman Wahyu are completed and sold out, with Phase 3 scheduled for launch next year. The remaining four parcels have been earmarked for development over a 15-year period. In Semenyih, Selangor, residential development Diamond City launched its final landed parcel in September 2025, which is expected to wrap up construction within two years. With a substantial land bank in its existing portfolio, the developer will focus its resources on executing its active pipeline over the next decade. As the interview draws to a close, both Li and Syarul reflect on the long-term nature of master township development. “Rome was not built in a day,” Li says. “When we first came to this coastal area in Johor, it was completely rural. Today, the infrastructure is firmly established. Development never moves in a straight upward line; it moves in spirals, but it always moves forward. “We wish the public to know that since the first day Country Garden has been here in Malaysia, we have wanted to be here long term. Of course, there are twists and turns over the years, but we cannot deny the contribution of the company in Malaysia.” He says Country Garden has invested RM32 billion in Malaysia, including RM20 billion in Forest City alone. “We have created jobs, contributed to the country’s tax revenues and trained local skilled workers. Most importantly, after so many challenges and uncertainties, we were here, and we are still here today. The fundamentals are in place, and we have absolute faith in what Forest City will become.” Save by subscribing to us for your print and/or digital copy. title: 'Permohonan Shamsul Iskandar untuk dapat pasport secara kekal diketahui 8 Disember
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR - Mahkamah Sesyen di sini menetapkan 8 Disember ini bagi memutuskan permohonan Datuk Seri Shamsul Iskandar Mohd. Akin untuk mendapatkan semula pasportnya secara kekal bagi memudahkan beliau menghadiri beberapa program di luar negara.  Hakim Suzana Hussin menetapkan tarikh itu selepas mendengar permohonan peguam Yusmadi Yusoff yang mewakili pemohon yang juga bekas Setiausaha Politik Kanan Perdana Menteri.  Pasport tersebut berada dalam simpanan mahkamah sebagai syarat jaminan tambahan selepas beliau didakwa atas lima pertuduhan rasuah.  Pada prosiding hari ini, Yusmadi memaklumkan bahawa permohonan bagi mendapatkan pasport secara kekal, difailkan pada 30 September lalu.  Menurut beliau, anak guamnya juga memohon pasport secara sementara bagi membolehkan beliau menghadiri program di Frankfurt dan London, bulan ini.  Bagaimanapun, Timbalan Pendakwa Raya Julaila Jamaludin membantah permohonan Shamsul Iskandar untuk mendapatkan pasportnya secara kekal atas alasan dokumen yang dikemukakan hanya berupa surat jemputan dan terdapat perbincangan yang boleh dijalankan secara dalam talian.  Bagaimanapun, Julaila tidak membantah permohonan Shamsul Iskandar untuk mendapatkan pasport secara sementara.  Suzana kemudian membenarkan pasport Shamsul Iskandar diberikan secara sementara mulai hari ini dan perlu diserahkan semula kepada mahkamah pada atau sebelum 16 Oktober ini.  Selain itu, mahkamah memerintahkan pihak pendakwaan memfailkan afidavit balasan terhadap permohonan Shamsul Iskandar bagi mendapatkan pasport secara kekal pada atau sebelum 19 Oktober ini.  Menerusi afidavit bagi menyokong permohonannya, Shamsul Iskandar berkata, beliau memerlukan pasportnya untuk perjalanan ke empat buah negara iaitu Frankfurt, London, Ireland dan Bosnia Herzegovina, dalam masa terdekat.  Berdasarkan dokumen yang diperoleh antara program yang dihadiri ialah pesta buku, sidang kemuncak dan lawatan kerja penglibatan perniagaan strategik.  Katanya, beliau berhasrat untuk ke Frankfurt, Jerman bagi menghadiri pesta buku bertajuk 'Frankfurt Book Fair' yang dianjurkan oleh Rex Education dan dijadualkan berlangsung 7 Oktober hingga 11 November.  "Berdasarkan penglibatan saya dengan Akademi Kepimpinan Masyarakat Madani, penyertaan dalam pesta buku tersebut bertujuan untuk memupuk sinergi antara organisasi serta memberikan manfaat bersama kepada kedua-dua entiti," katanya.  Sementara itu, bagi lawatan di London, Shamsul Iskandar memaklumkan beliau mendaftar untuk Sidang Kemuncak AlBaraka kelima bertajuk Ethics in Action: Rebuilding Foundations and Advancing the Global Impact of the Islamic Economy' yang akan berlangsung dari 13 Oktober hingga 14 Oktober ini.  Menurutnya, objektif utama sidang kemuncak tersebut adalah untuk memberi tumpuan kepada pengukuhan asas etika yang autentik bagi institusi kewangan Islam dan institusi bukan kewangan, sistem tadbir urus serta amalan pasaran.  Dalam pada itu, perjalanan ke Ireland dijadual bermula 27 November hingga 4 Disember ini bagi memenuhi jemputan Perbincangan Lanjutan Mengenai Strategi Perniagaan di negara itu.  Selain itu, beliau turut dijemput ke Bosnia Herzegovina pada November dan Disember ini untuk menghadiri beberapa siri perbincangan kedua-dua negara dalam pelbagai lapangan termasuk keusahawanan, pembangunan ekonomi dan transformasi sosial.  Justeru beliau memohon supaya pasport antarabangsanya dilepaskan secara kekal daripada tarikh perintah mahkamah bagi memudahkannya melakukan perjalanan ke luar negara.  Shamsul Iskandar, 51, didakwa atas dua pertuduhan bersetuju menerima suapan untuk dirinya, iaitu wang tunai RM140,000 daripada ahli perniagaan Tei Jiann Cheing atau turut dikenali sebagai Albert Tei sebagai dorongan membantu syarikat milik Albert Tei untuk mendapatkan kelulusan lesen penerokaan mineral di Sabah.  Dia turut didakwa atas dua lagi pertuduhan iaitu memperoleh untuk dirinya satu suapan berupa kelengkapan perabot dan barangan elektrik bernilai RM14,580.03 dan RM22,249 daripada individu sama bagi tujuan sama.  Kesalahan itu didakwa dilakukan di premis di Jalan Medang Serai, Bukit Bandaraya; di tempat letak kereta sebuah hotel di Jalan Sultan Hishamuddin di sini; serta di Jalan P14A 1/1, Presint 14, Putrajaya, antara 7 Disember 2023 dan 31 Januari 2024, serta antara 24 November 2023 dan 5 Mac 2024.  Shamsul Iskandar turut didakwa atas satu pertuduhan memperoleh suapan berjumlah RM64,924 yang dimasukkan ke dalam akaun CIMB Bank milik Rahmalidya Buyong bagi tujuan pembayaran penyewaan sebuah rumah di Jalan Medang Serai, Bukit Bandaraya, di sini, daripada Albert Tei bagi membantu syarikat miliknya mendapatkan kelulusan lesen penerokaan mineral di Sabah. - MalaysiaGazette

title: 'Merah Bermaksud Bahaya? Berhenti? Amaran? Video Ini Bakal Mengubah Persepsi Tanggapan Rata-Rata Manusia | Oh! Media
body:
'

Artikel Tajaan · Apa maksudnya?

Bila nampak warna merah, otak kita automatik akan bertindak memberi isyarat pada badan kita untuk berjaga-jaga betul tak? 

Mana taknya, dari kecil lagi fikiran kita dah dipengaruh dengan konotasi negatif terhadap warna merah di mana ia menggambarkan amaran, bahaya, berhenti dan macam-macam lagi.

Jujur cakap, sampai ke hari ini, warna merah masih lagi terpalit dengan persepsi ini daripada rata-rata manusia di seluruh dunia. 

Sering Disalah Erti, Warna Merah Sebenarnya Lebih Daripada Itu?

Tak seperti warna lain yang sering dikenali dengan tanggapan yang lebih positif, warna merah seringkali disalah erti. 

“Ala, warna merah kan boleh melambangkan keberanian dan keyakinan? Positif lah tu?”

Betul, tapi tak mencukupi untuk membuatkan ramai orang ubah persepsi terhadap warna ini. Jadi, untuk mengubah pandangan kita, jom tonton video ini sampai habis. 

Bertenaga, Berani & Bersemangat, CIMB Beri Persepsi Baru

Menerusi video jenama yang dibawakan oleh CIMB ini jelas menunjukkan gambaran yang warna merah BOLEH jadi positif dan beri impak besar dalam diri kita. 

Apa yang digambarkan oleh CIMB menerusi video jenama mereka ini adalah warna merah sentiasa membawa makna yang jauh lebih besar, di mana mereka menggalakkan kita semua untuk melihat cabaran bukan sebagai halangan, tetapi sebagai satu peluang. 

Ia bukan saja menampilkan keberanian, malah ia juga memberi kita semangat dan keyakinan untuk terus maju ke hadapan, sama ada untuk mengejar impian, merebut peluang, mengatasi cabaran ataupun sekadar untuk terus melangkah.

Bagi CIMB, untuk terus maju ke hadapan, ia hanya perlu bermula dengan satu pilihan iaitu untuk terus berjalan.

CIMB yang juga sinonim dengan warna merah turut memberi kita jaminan yang mereka akan sentiasa menyokong kita, memudahkan perjalanan dan membantu merealisasikan impian. 

Jadi, korang yang tengah membaca ni perlu ingat dan tanam dalam fikiran, warna merah sebenarnya boleh memberi impak positif dalam kehidupan harian kita. 

Sebagai jenama yang juga mempunyai warna merah sebagai identiti mereka, CIMB berjanji yang mereka akan sentiasa ada bersama kita untuk terus memacu ke hadapan.

Maklumat lanjut, layari laman web rasmi CIMB, atau ikuti media sosial di Facebook dan Instagram untuk update terkini.

title: 'A record earnings run
body: 'This article first appeared in The Edge Malaysia Weekly on October 5, 2026 - October 11, 2026 CIMB Group Holdings Bhd Despite an increasingly challenging banking landscape, CIMB Group Holdings Bhd (KL:CIMB) has continued to set new earnings benchmarks, hitting a record net profit in 2024 before surpassing it with a fresh record in 2025. Net profit at the country’s second largest banking group and Asean’s fifth largest by assets rose 1.7% to RM7.86 billion in the financial year ended Dec 31, 2025 (FY2025), from RM7.73 billion a year earlier. That followed a 10.7% increase in FY2024 and a much sharper 28.3% jump in FY2023 to RM6.98 billion. The steady rise in earnings translated into a risk-weighted compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 19.6% over the three years — the highest among its peers. This made CIMB this year’s winner of The Edge Billion Ringgit Club (BRC) award for Highest growth in profit after tax over three years in the financial services sector, among banks that have a market capitalisation of at least RM10 billion. It also won in the BRC Super Big Cap category for companies with a market capitalisation of above RM40 billion. It is the third year running that CIMB has won in both categories, marking how far the group has come since the Covid-19 pandemic. Its return on equity (ROE) improved from 10.7% in 2023 to 11.2% in 2024 and 11.3% in 2025, from just 9% in 2022. Thanks to its strong share price appreciation and attractive dividends, CIMB also clinched this year’s award for highest returns to shareholders over three years in the Super Big Cap category for companies with a market cap of over RM40 billion. CIMB’s shareholder returns grew at a CAGR of 20.2% over the three years — ahead of the competition — as its share price shot up to RM7.55 on March 31, 2026, from RM4.35 on March 31, 2023. The returns reflect the higher dividends that shareholders received as profits grew. CIMB increased its dividend per share from 43 sen in 2023 to 47 sen in 2024, before declaring 47.1 sen for FY2025. Each year’s payout included a special dividend of seven sen per share. The latest payout amounted to a record of about RM5.1 billion. Supporting its share price is the fact that the group has committed to returning up to RM2 billion of additional capital to shareholders by 2027 through special dividends and/or share buybacks, subject to market conditions and regulatory approvals. This year, given a more challenging macroeconomic backdrop, including a prolonged conflict in the Middle East macroeconomics, CIMB’s 1HFY2026 financial performance softened from the previous corresponding period. Net profit for the period fell a marginal 0.2% year on year (y-o-y) to RM3.85 billion, while revenue slid to RM10.97 billion from RM11.10 billion. Be that as it may, it delivered an annualised ROE of 11%, in line with its target of 11% to 11.5% for the full year. It announced an all-cash first interim dividend of 19.65 sen per share, based on a consistent payout ratio of 55.5%, which translated into a total dividend payout of RM2.1 billion. Notably, asset quality remained broadly stable, with its gross impaired loan ratio at an all-time low of 1.6% at end-June, compared with 1.7% three months earlier. Group CEO Novan Amirudin said the execution momentum for Forward30 — the group’s six-year strategic programme that started running from last year — remained firmly on track. “Our destination is clear: to become the top-of-mind Asean bank by 2030. To get there, we must deliver a sustainable ROE of 12% to 13% by 2027 and compete consistently in the top quartile of our regional peers by 2030,” he said in the group’s latest annual report. Nevertheless, headwinds persist, and the group expects funding cost pressures in Indonesia and competition on loan repricing to weigh on its net interest margin (NIM) this year. CIMB’s NIM stood at 2.04% in 2QFY2026, down four basis points from the previous quarter and down 11bps on a y-o-y basis. A notable development this year is that CIMB’s Thai unit, CIMB Thai Bank, was delisted from the Stock Exchange of Thailand on Sept 12, more than 2½ years after a regulatory process triggered by stricter free-float requirements. CIMB Thai remains a core subsidiary and the delisting is not expected to have a material impact on the lender. The Thai unit is profitable, having posted more than a fivefold y-o-y increase in net profit to THB886.3 million in 2QFY2026. As at Aug 28, CIMB’s share price closed at RM7.96, giving the company a market value of RM86.05 billion. Bloomberg data shows 15 “buy” and five “hold” recommendations on the stock, with no “sell” calls. Net profit at the country’s second largest banking group and Asean’s fifth largest by assets rose 1.7% to RM7.86 billion in the financial year ended Dec 31, 2025 (FY2025), from RM7.73 billion a year earlier. That followed a 10.7% increase in FY2024 and a much sharper 28.3% jump in FY2023 to RM6.98 billion. The steady rise in earnings translated into a risk-weighted compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 19.6% over the three years — the highest among its peers. This made CIMB this year’s winner of The Edge Billion Ringgit Club (BRC) award for Highest growth in profit after tax over three years in the financial services sector, among banks that have a market capitalisation of at least RM10 billion. It also won in the BRC Super Big Cap category for companies with a market capitalisation of above RM40 billion. It is the third year running that CIMB has won in both categories, marking how far the group has come since the Covid-19 pandemic. Its return on equity (ROE) improved from 10.7% in 2023 to 11.2% in 2024 and 11.3% in 2025, from just 9% in 2022. Thanks to its strong share price appreciation and attractive dividends, CIMB also clinched this year’s award for highest returns to shareholders over three years in the Super Big Cap category for companies with a market cap of over RM40 billion. CIMB’s shareholder returns grew at a CAGR of 20.2% over the three years — ahead of the competition — as its share price shot up to RM7.55 on March 31, 2026, from RM4.35 on March 31, 2023. The returns reflect the higher dividends that shareholders received as profits grew. CIMB increased its dividend per share from 43 sen in 2023 to 47 sen in 2024, before declaring 47.1 sen for FY2025. Each year’s payout included a special dividend of seven sen per share. The latest payout amounted to a record of about RM5.1 billion. Supporting its share price is the fact that the group has committed to returning up to RM2 billion of additional capital to shareholders by 2027 through special dividends and/or share buybacks, subject to market conditions and regulatory approvals. This year, given a more challenging macroeconomic backdrop, including a prolonged conflict in the Middle East macroeconomics, CIMB’s 1HFY2026 financial performance softened from the previous corresponding period. Net profit for the period fell a marginal 0.2% year on year (y-o-y) to RM3.85 billion, while revenue slid to RM10.97 billion from RM11.10 billion. Be that as it may, it delivered an annualised ROE of 11%, in line with its target of 11% to 11.5% for the full year. title: 'Bursa Sheds 2.4% For Week As Yields, Foreign Selling Hit Sentiment
body: 'Bursa Malaysia ended the Sept 28-Oct 2 week sharply lower, with the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) losing 40.75 points, or 2.4%, to 1,630.87 from the previous Friday’s 1,671.62, as rising global bond yields, elevated oil prices and persistent foreign selling weighed on sentiment.  The benchmark started the week marginally lower, slipping 0.09% to 1,670.02 on Sept 28, as investors remained cautious amid a lack of fresh catalysts and continued external headwinds.  Selling intensified the next day, when the FBM KLCI tumbled 26.06 points, or 1.56%, to 1,643.96, pressured by surging bond yields and Brent crude prices around US$107 a barrel, which reignited inflation concerns and dampened risk appetite.  The market rebounded 0.43% to 1,651.17 on Sept 30 as bargain hunters returned following the sharp sell-off, although broader sentiment remained cautious ahead of key US inflation data.  That recovery proved short-lived, with the index plunging another 1.26% to 1,630.36 the following day, dragged by selling in heavyweights including Maybank, Public Bank, CIMB, TNB and IHH Healthcare. Weak domestic manufacturing activity and continued foreign outflows added to the pressure.  Bursa eked out a 0.03% gain to 1,630.87 to close out the trading week as bargain hunting cushioned the recent sell-off, but the rebound remained muted amid weakness across regional markets and caution ahead of US labour data.  Overall, the FBM KLCI recorded losses in three of the five sessions, with external rate and inflation concerns dominating trading despite intermittent bargain hunting.

title: 'Laws alone will not shield our children online
body: 'AI and the relentless subscription to social media pose many new challenges to ordinary people, not just in Malaysia but around the world. The government deserves credit for introducing laws to safeguard the young from AI manipulation and social media abuse. New laws, new duties The Online Safety Act 2025 came into force on 1 January. This landmark law gives the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) sweeping powers to enforce safety standards on digital services. The laws aim to protect children from AI-generated child sexual abuse material, deepfakes, online grooming and voice cloning. They also shift responsibility from parents as watchdogs to digital platforms, which must have strict built-in accountability features. The Child Protection Code and the Risk Mitigation Code came into force on 1 June. They require platforms to build in ‘child-by-design’ safeguards. Platforms must also label AI-generated synthetic media, such as deepfakes, so young users and parents can spot manipulative or misleading content. Those that do not comply face fines of up to RM10m. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member There are also mandatory age-verification checks to stop children under 16 from registering for social media or high-risk content accounts. The Cybercrimes Bill 2026, passed in July, targets synthetic and AI-generated threats to children. Section 23 criminalises the use of deepfake technology to produce and spread harmful, malicious material. Section 24 outlaws the sharing of non-consensual intimate images. This extends protection to minors from AI that digitally alters school photos and similar images. The government has also set out seven key principles for responsible AI, focusing on reliability, safety, control, privacy and data security. These help protect children from AI tools that track data and use biased algorithms. The aim is a transparent, ethical system that acts as a shield for our most vulnerable – our children. Awareness must follow Other initiatives due in the months ahead include national digital literacy programmes. These aim to build resilience in children rather than rely on bans. The laws will need strong public awareness campaigns. They must reach not only consumers but also the AI back-end developers and social media programmers. Other ministries, including education and trade and economics, will need to work with the MCMC. Each should run campaigns covering the parts of the laws that apply to them. Only then can we hope for the vigilance needed to make these laws work. The video above, in which a mother describes how she lost her teenage son to the dangers of AI and social media, should send shivers down the spine. It is also a timely reminder to governments, leaders, parents, teachers and anyone else who helps protect the digital lives of children. However, given Malaysia’s track record of enthusiastic, knee-jerk reactions to new ideas that are quickly forgotten, there is much to worry about. The views expressed in Aliran's media statements and the NGO statements we have endorsed reflect Aliran's official stand. title: 'Ibu janji ambil kami di sekolah, tapi dia pergi selamanya'
body: 'GUA MUSANG: Hancur hati dua beradik apabila ibu dinanti untuk menjemput pulang dari sekolah tidak kunjung tiba, sebaliknya berita duka diterima apabila insan tersayang itu meninggal dunia akibat kemalangan. Nur Arissa Najla Mohd Shazuam, 13, dan Nur Amani Nuwairah Mohd Shazuam, 15, menanti penuh sabar selepas ibunya, Nor Hasyikim Daud, 34, berjanji mengambil mereka pulang dari Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan (SMK) Bandar Chiku. Nur Arissa Najla berkata, dia menerima berita kemalangan itu daripada seorang rakan ketika menunggu pada 1.40 tengah hari. "Ibu ada maklumkan akan ke Gua Musang dengan rakannya dan berjanji mengambil saya serta kakak dari sekolah. "Pada hari kejadian, saya menduduki tiga kertas peperiksaan dan sangat teruja untuk memberitahu ibu yang saya boleh jawab semua soalan subjek Sejarah. "Lebih setengah jam menanti ibu, namun tidak kunjung tiba, sebaliknya saya terima berita ibu kemalangan. "Saya nampak bapa saudara datang menjemput kami," katanya ketika ditemui di Felda Chiku 5 di sini. Dalam kejadian Ahad lalu, Nor Hasyikim maut di lokasi kejadian apabila kenderaan dipandunya bertembung dengan lori 10 tan di Kilometer 40 Jalan Gua Musang-Kuala Krai. Mangsa meninggal dunia akibat tersepit, manakala rakannya di tempat duduk penumpang hadapan cedera parah. Allahyarham turut meninggalkan seorang bayi Nur Aireen Nisrina berusia 11 bulan. Sementara itu, kakak kepada Nor Hasyikim, Siti Noraeshah Daud, 39, berkata, tiga beradik itu akan dijaga ibunya dengan bantuan adik-beradik lain. "Sejak setahun lalu arwah membesarkan tiga anaknya dengan bekerja di kantin asrama SMK Bandar Chiku. "Selepas ini kami akan bersama-sama menjaga dan membesarkan tiga anak perempuan arwah," katanya. Orang ramai yang ingin memberi sumbangan boleh menyalurkan ke akaun Bank CIMB milik Siti Noraeshah Daud bernombor 7601845122.

title: 'DNB completes RM5.2b financing, unlocking next phase of 5G growth in Malaysia - Newswav
body: 'PETALING JAYA: Digital Nasional Bhd (DNB) has completed a RM5.2 billion syndicated Islamic term financing exercise, a transaction that ranks among the largest syndicated loan facilities ever arranged for an unlisted company in Malaysia. DNB CEO Datuk Azman Ismail said, “The successful completion of this RM5.2 billion financing exercise marks a significant milestone for DNB and reflects strong confidence in our business fundamentals, operational track record and long-term role in Malaysia’s digital economy. “This financing provides DNB with a sustainable platform to operate on its own, continue investing in network enhancement and capacity expansion, and leverage our expanded spectrum assets. “As Malaysia progresses under the dual network framework, DNB remains committed to providing world-class digital infrastructure that supports our shareholders, customers, enterprises and government agencies. “With strong financing, enhanced spectrum resources and a proven nationwide 5G platform, DNB is well positioned to support the government’s AI Nation aspirations and help power Malaysia’s next phase of digital growth.” Maybank Investment Bank Bhd acted as mandated lead arranger, bookrunner and coordinating arranger with AmInvestment Bank Bhd, CIMB Islamic Bank Bhd, RHB Islamic Bank Bhd and United Overseas Bank (Malaysia) Bhd as joint mandated lead arrangers. AmInvestment Bank acted as financial adviser to DNB. This significant step marks DNB’s evolution as Malaysia transitions to the next phase of its dual 5G network framework. The financing strengthens DNB’s long-term financial position and facilitates the planned exit of Minister of Finance Incorporated (MOFInc) as an ordinary shareholder and the transition to equal ownership among its mobile network pperator shareholders, namely CelcomDigi Bhd through Infranation Sdn Bhd, Maxis Broadband Sdn Bhd and YTL Power International Bhd, expected in the early fourth quarter of 2026. MOF Inc will retain a special share in DNB to safeguard national interests, ensuring continued stewardship of key strategic matters while enabling the company to advance its next phase of development. The syndicated financing exercise includes the refinancing of DNB’s Government Guarantee Revolving Credit Facility, which expired on Sept 29, and establishes a sustainable long-term funding structure to support the company’s future growth. The completion of the financing coincides with the award of the full 100 MHz of the 3.3–3.4GHz spectrum and the conversion of DNB’s entire 240MHz spectrum holding to a spectrum assignment. Following the issuance of the spectrum assignment by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), the assignment took effect yesterday, providing greater regulatory certainty and strengthening DNB’s ability to support Malaysia’s evolving 5G connectivity needs. The 240 MHz spectrum block will enhance network capacity, efficiency, and performance, enabling faster speeds, lower latency, and an improved customer experience. It also supports the deployment of advanced technologies, including Massive MIMO, carrier aggregation, 5G Advanced and AI-driven network capabilities, further strengthening DNB’s leadership in next-generation connectivity. Together, the financing and the spectrum assignment strengthen DNB’s ability to enhance network quality and resilience, support future demand, and advance Malaysia’s digital economy ambitions.

title: 'Tenaga Nasional Tells Analysts Extra Subsidy Is One-off, Mulls Permanent Solutions
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 23): Tenaga Nasional Bhd (KL:TENAGA) said the extra subsidy earmarked for households is a one-off measure, and the national electric utility is mulling tweaks to its charges to better shield consumers. The initial estimate of up to RM150 million in costs to subsidise consumers from rising electricity bills is conservative and the actual cost may be lower for the company, according to several analysts that attended an investor briefing by Tenaga Nasional on Tuesday. Tenaga Nasional stressed that “this is a one-off corporate contribution outside the regulatory framework, rather than a change to the revenue-cap or price-cap mechanism”, BIMB Securities said in a post-briefing note. The briefing follows a decline in Tenaga Nasional’s share price as investors priced in earnings impact after the company agreed to absorb the impact from the electricity tariff fuel surcharge exemption that has been expanded to more households up until the end of this year. Consumers are seeing relatively higher electricity bills from soaring temperatures and work-from-home policy and other seasonal factors. Last week, the government announced that households consuming 800 kilowatt-hour of power or less monthly will now be spared from surcharges under the automatic fuel adjustment. The exemption is previously provided only to those using under 600 kilowatt-hour each month. More importantly, Tenaga Nasional and the government are working on a more permanent solution for 2027 onwards to address elevated fuel price, CIMB Securities said. One possible approach could be differentiated rates versus the current uniform rate, and similar to how the imbalance cost pass-through, or ICPT, was previously implemented with residential users paying a lower rate against large-scale commercial users, the house noted. While there is no clarity on the new structure, the previous framework under ICPT mechanism allowed “cross subsidisation and potentially greater protection” for residential consumers and even small and medium enterprises, TA Securities added. Under the previous mechanism that was replaced in June 2025 with the automatic fuel adjustment system, the final tariff to be paid by consumers was adjusted every six months in the form of rebates or surcharges on top of the base tariff.
