'Tenaga Nasional Tells Analysts Extra Subsidy Is One-off, Mulls Permanent Solutions

'KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 23): Tenaga Nasional Bhd (KL:TENAGA) said the extra subsidy earmarked for households is a one-off measure, and the national electric utility is mulling tweaks to its charges to better shield consumers. The initial estimate of up to RM150 million in costs to subsidise consumers from rising electricity bills is conservative and the actual cost may be lower for the company, according to several analysts that attended an investor briefing by Tenaga Nasional on Tuesday. Tenaga Nasional stressed that “this is a one-off corporate contribution outside the regulatory framework, rather than a change to the revenue-cap or price-cap mechanism”, BIMB Securities said in a post-briefing note. The briefing follows a decline in Tenaga Nasional’s share price as investors priced in earnings impact after the company agreed to absorb the impact from the electricity tariff fuel surcharge exemption that has been expanded to more households up until the end of this year. Consumers are seeing relatively higher electricity bills from soaring temperatures and work-from-home policy and other seasonal factors. Last week, the government announced that households consuming 800 kilowatt-hour of power or less monthly will now be spared from surcharges under the automatic fuel adjustment. The exemption is previously provided only to those using under 600 kilowatt-hour each month. More importantly, Tenaga Nasional and the government are working on a more permanent solution for 2027 onwards to address elevated fuel price, CIMB Securities said. One possible approach could be differentiated rates versus the current uniform rate, and similar to how the imbalance cost pass-through, or ICPT, was previously implemented with residential users paying a lower rate against large-scale commercial users, the house noted. While there is no clarity on the new structure, the previous framework under ICPT mechanism allowed “cross subsidisation and potentially greater protection” for residential consumers and even small and medium enterprises, TA Securities added. Under the previous mechanism that was replaced in June 2025 with the automatic fuel adjustment system, the final tariff to be paid by consumers was adjusted every six months in the form of rebates or surcharges on top of the base tariff. title: 'Malaysia-Myanmar: The repatriation question
body: 'A group of 1,476 people have been returned to Myanmar from Malaysia earlier this week, as part of a wider repatriation programme that could eventually involve up to 5,000 people. title: 'DNB lengkapkan pembiayaan RM5.2 bilion bagi menyokong fasa seterusnya pertumbuhan 5G - Newswav
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR 1 Okt - Digital Nasional Bhd (DNB) melengkapkan pembiayaan berjangka Islam secara sindiket bernilai RM5.2 bilion, sekali gus mengukuhkan kedudukan pembiayaan jangka panjang syarikat ketika Malaysia memasuki fasa pertumbuhan seterusnya dwirangkaian 5G . DNB dalam kenyataan berkata pembiayaan itu akan memudahkan perancangan keluar Menteri Kewangan Diperbadankan (MOF Inc) sebagai pemegang saham biasa dan peralihan kepada pemilikan sama rata dalam kalangan pemegang saham pengendali rangkaian mudah alihnya, iaitu CelcomDigi Bhd, Maxis Broadband Sdn Bhd dan YTL Power International Bhd. Peralihan pemilikan tersebut dijangka berlaku pada awal suku keempat 2026, manakala MOF Inc akan mengekalkan saham khas dalam DNB bagi melindungi kepentingan negara. Pembiayaan berkenaan turut merangkumi pembiayaan semula kemudahan kredit pusingan DNB yang dijamin kerajaan dan tamat tempoh pada 29 September, selain mewujudkan struktur pembiayaan jangka panjang bagi menyokong pertumbuhan syarikat. Penyempurnaan pembiayaan itu bertepatan dengan pemberian penuh spektrum 100MHz dalam jalur 3.3–3.4GHz serta penukaran keseluruhan pegangan spektrum 240MHz DNB kepada penetapan spektrum. Penetapan oleh Suruhanjaya Komunikasi dan Multimedia Malaysia (MCMC) itu berkuat kuasa mulai 1 Oktober. Menurut DNB, blok spektrum 240MHz tersebut akan meningkatkan kapasiti, kecekapan dan prestasi rangkaian, selain menyokong teknologi termasuk Massive MIMO, pengagregatan pembawa, 5G Advanced dan keupayaan rangkaian dipacu kecerdasan buatan. Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif DNB, Datuk Azman Ismail berkata pembiayaan berkenaan menyediakan platform mampan untuk syarikat beroperasi secara bebas sambil meneruskan pelaburan dalam peningkatan rangkaian dan peluasan kapasiti. “Penyempurnaan pembiayaan RM5.2 bilion ini merupakan pencapaian penting bagi DNB dan mencerminkan keyakinan kukuh terhadap asas perniagaan, rekod operasi serta peranan jangka panjang kami dalam ekonomi digital Malaysia,” katanya. Maybank Investment Bank Bhd bertindak sebagai pengatur utama yang diberi mandat, pengurus buku dan pengatur penyelaras bagi pembiayaan itu. AmInvestment Bank Bhd, CIMB Islamic Bank Bhd, RHB Islamic Bank Bhd dan United Overseas Bank (Malaysia) Bhd pula merupakan pengatur utama bersama yang diberi mandat, manakala AmInvestment Bank bertindak sebagai penasihat kewangan DNB. - DagangNews.com

title: 'DNB completes RM5.2bil financing to support next phase of 5G growth
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Digital Nasional Bhd (DNB) has completed a RM5.2bil syndicated Islamic term financing, strengthening its long-term funding position as Malaysia moves into the next phase of its dual 5G network framework. In a statement, DNB said the financing will facilitate the planned exit of Minister of Finance Inc (MOF Inc) as an ordinary shareholder and the transition to equal ownership among its mobile network operator shareholders, namely CelcomDigi Bhd, Maxis Broadband Sdn Bhd and YTL Power International Bhd. The ownership transition is expected in the early fourth quarter of 2026, while MOF Inc will retain a special share in DNB to safeguard national interests. The syndicated financing also includes the refinancing of DNB's government-guaranteed revolving credit facility, which expired on Sept 29, and establishes a longer-term funding structure to support the company's growth. DNB said the completion of the financing coincided with the award of the full 100 MHz of the 3.3–3.4 GHz spectrum and the conversion of its entire 240 MHz spectrum holding to a spectrum assignment. The assignment by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) takes effect from Oct 1. DNB said the 240 MHz spectrum block would enhance network capacity, efficiency and performance and support technologies including Massive MIMO, carrier aggregation, 5G Advanced and artificial intelligence-driven network capabilities. Chief executive officer Datuk Azman Ismail said the financing would provide DNB with a sustainable platform to operate independently while continuing to invest in network enhancement and capacity expansion. “The successful completion of this RM5.2bil financing exercise marks a significant milestone for DNB and reflects strong confidence in our business fundamentals, operational track record and long-term role in Malaysia’s digital economy,” he said. Maybank Investment Bank Bhd acted as mandated lead arranger, bookrunner and coordinating arranger for the financing. AmInvestment Bank Bhd, CIMB Islamic Bank Bhd, RHB Islamic Bank Bhd and United Overseas Bank (Malaysia) Bhd were joint mandated lead arrangers, while AmInvestment Bank was DNB's financial adviser.

title: 'Bursa Malaysia dibuka rendah, dipengaruhi faktor luaran
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia dibuka rendah pada Khamis, menjejaki prestasi bercampur-campur Wall Street berikutan hasil bon Perbendaharaan AS yang lebih tinggi serta ketegangan berterusan di Asia Barat menjejaskan minat belian. Pada 9.10 pagi, FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) susut 3.74 mata atau 0.22 peratus kepada 1,647.43 daripada paras 1,651.17 ketika ditutup pada Rabu. Indeks penanda aras itu dibuka 1.30 mata lebih rendah pada 1,649.87. Di pasaran meluas, kaunter rugi mengatasi kaunter untung sebanyak 200 berbanding 142, manakala 307 kaunter tidak berubah, 2,124 kaunter tidak diniagakan dan 12 kaunter digantung. Jumlah dagangan sebanyak 246.59 juta saham bernilai RM118.14 juta. Naib Presiden Penyelidikan Ekuiti Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd, Thong Pak Leng, berkata Wall Street ditutup bercampur-campur apabila inflasi yang lebih rendah mengurangkan jangkaan terhadap satu lagi kenaikan kadar faedah oleh Rizab Persekutuan AS, meskipun hasil bon yang kekal tinggi terus menjejaskan sentimen. Di peringkat domestik, beliau berkata, indeks penanda aras pasaran mungkin cenderung diniagakan berhati-hati, dengan sentimen keseluruhan pasaran yang lemah dan jualan asing baru-baru ini menunjukkan pelabur terus mengambil pendekatan berhati-hati. "Justeru, bagi hari ini, kami menjangkakan indeks kekal dalam mod pengukuhan dalam julat 1,640-1,660, dengan aktiviti pembelian ketika harga rendah dijangka mengehadkan penurunan," katanya kepada Bernama. Dalam kalangan saham wajaran tinggi, Maybank dan IHH Healthcare masing-masing tidak berubah pada RM9.90 dan RM7.83. Public Bank susut tiga sen kepada RM4.67, CIMB berkurangan satu sen kepada RM7.78 dan Tenaga Nasional turun dua sen kepada RM12.94. Dalam dagangan aktif, saham yang baru disenaraikan di Pasaran ACE, GB Bond susut setengah sen kepada 24.5 sen, manakala VS Industry tidak berubah pada 28 sen. Astro Malaysia menambah setengah sen kepada enam sen, Jaks Resources meningkat satu sen kepada 21.5 sen dan Divfex menokok dua sen kepada 11 sen. Antara kaunter untung utama, Keck Seng meningkat 11 sen kepada RM5.14 dan Petron Malaysia menambah tujuh sen kepada RM3.47. Hengyuan Refining dan Spritzer masing-masing naik enam sen kepada RM3.62 dan RM3.67, manakala Jati Tinggi mengukuh lima sen kepada RM1.44. Kuala Lumpur Kepong mendahului kaunter rugi apabila susut 18 sen kepada RM22.02. UWC pula berkurangan 15 sen kepada RM6.92, manakala Insights Analytics dan MISC masing-masing turun sembilan sen kepada RM1.20 dan RM7.55. Petronas Dagangan susut lapan sen kepada RM19.20. Di papan indeks, Indeks FBM Mid 70 susut 42.26 mata kepada 17,532.41, Indeks FBM Emas berkurangan 26.32 mata kepada 12,265.69, manakala Indeks FBM Top 100 turun 27.82 mata kepada 12,056.62. Indeks FBM Emas Shariah susut 22.09 mata kepada 12,154.26, manakala Indeks FBM ACE berkurangan 6.31 mata kepada 5,527.97. Mengikut sektor, Indeks Produk dan Perkhidmatan Perindustrian susut 0.10 mata kepada 180.31, manakala Indeks Tenaga meningkat 1.41 mata kepada 847.11. Indeks Perkhidmatan Kewangan turun 27.47 mata kepada 19,189.02, manakala Indeks Perladangan merosot 33.34 mata kepada 9,163.33.

title: 'Mateen perlu RM8,000 beli ‘stroller’ khas
body: 'PETALING JAYA – Bayi hidrosefalus, Muhammad Mateen Aryan Muhammad Hanif, 15 bulan, dari Sungai Petani, Kedah, kini semakin aktif namun pergerakannya terbatas disebabkan kepalanya yang berat. Bapanya, Muhammad Hanif Zakaria, 32, berkata, Mateen kini cuba menggerakkan badan dan memusingkan badan, tetapi sukar berbuat demikian dengan kepala yang mencecah ukuran 90 sentimeter (cm). “Perkembangan dia okey. Dia pun cuba bergerak, nak pusing badannya, tetapi tak boleh sebab kepala dia berat,” katanya ketika dihubungi Kosmo!. Menurut Muhammad Hanif, keadaan Mateen kini semakin baik apabila sawan yang dialaminya semakin berkurang, namun apabila serangan berlaku, saiz kepala anaknya boleh kembali membesar. “Sejak kami mendapatkan rawatan alternatif, Mateen semakin kurang diserang sawan dan saiz kepala dia turun sedikit ke 89cm. Tapi apabila kena sawan, automatik saiz tu boleh naik balik,” ujarnya. Muhammad Hanif berkata, keperluan asas Matten kini mencukupi dan berterima kasih kepada pihak yang pernah membantu, namun dia dan isteri kini merancang untuk mendapatkan kereta sorong (stroller) khas bagi memudahkan pergerakan Mateen. Bagaimanapun dia menjelaskan, ia perlu ditempah khas mengikut keperluan Mateen, dengan anggaran kos sebanyak RM8,000 dan akan berbuat demikian apabila jumlah itu mencukupi. Orang ramai yang ingin membantu keluarga itu mendapatkan kereta sorong berkenaan, boleh menyalurkan sumbangan ke akaun bank CIMB bernombor 7632966954 di atas nama Muhammad Hanif. Terdahulu Kosmo! melaporkan, Muhammad Hanif yang bekerja sebagai pemandu lori bersyukur kerana anak bongsu daripada tiga beradik itu tidak pernah menangis kesakitan sejak lahir. Dia dan isteri, Habidah Nasruddin, 31, bagaimanapun berdepan kesukaran mengangkat Mateen disebabkan kepalanya yang makin membesar.

Bapanya, Muhammad Hanif Zakaria, 32, berkata, Mateen kini cuba menggerakkan badan dan memusingkan badan, tetapi sukar berbuat demikian dengan kepala yang mencecah ukuran 90 sentimeter (cm). “Perkembangan dia okey. Dia pun cuba bergerak, nak pusing badannya, tetapi tak boleh sebab kepala dia berat,” katanya ketika dihubungi Kosmo!. Menurut Muhammad Hanif, keadaan Mateen kini semakin baik apabila sawan yang dialaminya semakin berkurang, namun apabila serangan berlaku, saiz kepala anaknya boleh kembali membesar. “Sejak kami mendapatkan rawatan alternatif, Mateen semakin kurang diserang sawan dan saiz kepala dia turun sedikit ke 89cm. Tapi apabila kena sawan, automatik saiz tu boleh naik balik,” ujarnya. Muhammad Hanif berkata, keperluan asas Matten kini mencukupi dan berterima kasih kepada pihak yang pernah membantu, namun dia dan isteri kini merancang untuk mendapatkan kereta sorong (stroller) khas bagi memudahkan pergerakan Mateen. Bagaimanapun dia menjelaskan, ia perlu ditempah khas mengikut keperluan Mateen, dengan anggaran kos sebanyak RM8,000 dan akan berbuat demikian apabila jumlah itu mencukupi. Orang ramai yang ingin membantu keluarga itu mendapatkan kereta sorong berkenaan, boleh menyalurkan sumbangan ke akaun bank CIMB bernombor 7632966954 di atas nama Muhammad Hanif. Terdahulu Kosmo! melaporkan, Muhammad Hanif yang bekerja sebagai pemandu lori bersyukur kerana anak bongsu daripada tiga beradik itu tidak pernah menangis kesakitan sejak lahir. Dia dan isteri, Habidah Nasruddin, 31, bagaimanapun berdepan kesukaran mengangkat Mateen disebabkan kepalanya yang makin membesar.

title: 'Bursa Malaysia Opens Lower Amid US Yield Increase and Regional Tensions
body: 'Kuala Lumpur:Bursa Malaysia began the trading day on a lower note, reflecting Wall Street's mixed performance as higher US Treasury yields and ongoing tensions in West Asia affected investor sentiment. According to BERNAMA News Agency, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) dropped 3.74 points, or 0.22 percent, to 1,647.43 at 9.10 am on Thursday, down from the previous day's close of 1,651.17. The index had opened 1.30 points lower at 1,649.87. The broader market saw 200 decliners outpacing 142 gainers, with 307 counters unchanged, 2,124 untraded, and 12 suspended. The turnover was 246.59 million shares, valued at RM118.14 million. Thong Pak Leng, Vice-President of Equity Research at Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd, noted that Wall Street's mixed close was influenced by softer inflation, which eased the expectations of another US Federal Reserve rate hike, although elevated bond yields still weighed on market sentiment. Domestically, Thong indicated that the market may trade cautiously due to weak market breadth and recent foreign selling, suggesting continued investor caution. He anticipates the index to consolidate within the 1,640-1,660 range, with bargain hunting providing some support. Among the heavyweights, Maybank and IHH Healthcare remained unchanged at RM9.90 and RM7.83, respectively. Public Bank decreased by three sen to RM4.67, CIMB fell one sen to RM7.78, and Tenaga Nasional dropped two sen to RM12.94. In more active trading, new ACE Market entrant GB Bond fell half a sen to 24.5 sen, while VS Industry remained steady at 28 sen. Astro Malaysia increased by half a sen to six sen, Jaks Resources gained one sen to 21.5 sen, and Divfex rose two sen to 11 sen. Top gainers included Keck Seng, which advanced 11 sen to RM5.14, and Petron Malaysia, which rose seven sen to RM3.47. Hengyuan Refining and Spritzer each gained six sen to RM3.62 and RM3.67, respectively, while Jati Tinggi strengthened five sen to RM1.44. Leading the decliners, Kuala Lumpur Kepong dropped 18 sen to RM22.02, UWC decreased 15 sen to RM6.92, and both Insights Analytics and MISC fell nine sen to RM1.20 and RM7.55, respectively. Petronas Dagangan lost eight sen to RM19.20. On the index board, the FBM Mid 70 Index fell 42.26 points to 17,532.41, the FBM Emas Index declined 26.32 points to 12,265.69, and the FBM Top 100 Index shed 27.82 points to 12,056.62. The FBM Emas Shariah Index weakened 22.09 points to 12,154.26, while the FBM ACE Index decreased by 6.31 points to 5,527.97. Sector-wise, the Industrial Products and Services Index slipped 0.10 point to 180.31, the Energy Index gained 1.41 points to 847.11, the Financial Services Index fell 27.47 points to 19,189.02, and the Plantation Index retreated 33.34 points to 9,163.33.

title: 'Bursa Malaysia Closes Lower Amid Cautious Wall Street Influence
body: 'Kuala Lumpur:Bursa Malaysia ended the trading session lower on Thursday due to persistent selling pressure, influenced by a mixed and cautious performance on Wall Street overnight. According to BERNAMA News Agency, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) dropped 20.81 points, or 1.26 percent, closing at 1,630.36, down from the previous day's close of 1,651.17. The index opened slightly weaker at 1,649.87 and fluctuated between 1,630.10 and 1,649.87 throughout the day. The market trend showed a negative breadth, with 750 decliners outpacing 342 gainers, while 495 counters remained unchanged, 1,186 were untraded, and 12 were suspended. Turnover decreased to 3.1 billion units valued at RM2.7 billion, compared to 3.63 billion units worth RM3.62 billion on Wednesday. Mohd Sedek Jantan, the director of investment strategy and country economist at IPPFA Sdn Bhd, noted that the sentiment was cautious, exacerbated by weaker domestic manufacturing activity and continued foreign selling. He highlighted that softer manufacturing momentum and global portfolio rotation exerted pressure on the benchmark index, despite domestic institutional demand providing some balance against foreign outflows. The S and P Global Malaysia Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) slightly dipped below the neutral 50.0 mark, reaching 49.9 in September from 50.2 in August. This marks the first decline in four months following a period of improvement. Regionally, the S and P Global ASEAN Manufacturing PMI decreased to 52.1 in September from 52.3 in August. In terms of specific stocks, Maybank fell four sen to RM9.95, Public Bank lost three sen to RM4.67, and CIMB dropped 10 sen to RM7.69. Tenaga Nasional declined six sen to RM12.90, while IHH Healthcare erased 13 sen to RM7.70. Among active trades, Zetrix AI firmed half a sen to 16.5 sen, VS Industry dipped one sen to 27 sen, and Jaks Resources slipped 2.5 sen to 18 sen. ACE Market debutant GB Bond slumped 4.5 sen to 20.5 sen, with HHRG gaining half a sen to 16.5 sen. Top gainers included Malaysian Pacific Industries, which surged 72 sen to RM41.12, Ayer Holdings rising 20 sen to RM7.70, and Riverview Rubber Estates advancing 12 sen to RM3.02. Dutch Lady Malaysia Industries added 10 sen to RM30, while Vitrox gained nine sen to RM10. Among the biggest losers, Kuala Lumpur Kepong dropped 78 sen to RM21.42, Allianz Malaysia gave up 62 sen to RM21.00, and United Plantations fell 60 sen to RM30.96. Fraser and Neave, along with Hong Leong Industries, both slipped 32 sen to RM21.42 and RM16.14, respectively.

title: 'Bursa Malaysia Rises Amid Bargain Hunting
body: 'Kuala Lumpur:Bursa Malaysia's key index rose on Wednesday, rebounding from recent losses as oversold conditions prompted bargain hunting. According to BERNAMA News Agency, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) increased by 7.21 points, or 0.43 percent, ending at 1,651.17 compared to Tuesday's close of 1,643.96. The index opened 2.53 points higher at 1,646.49, fluctuating between 1,645.03 and 1,657.41 throughout the session. Market breadth was negative, with 703 decliners surpassing 413 gainers, while 572 counters remained unchanged, 1,167 were untraded, and 95 were suspended. Turnover improved, reaching 3.63 billion units valued at RM3.62 billion, up from 3.31 billion units worth RM2.95 billion on Tuesday. Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd's vice-president of equity research, Thong Pak Leng, noted that the local market's recovery was tentative as investors awaited the August US Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index. This key inflation gauge could influence further movements in bond yields. Domestically, a cautious stance is maintained due to the elevated US 10-year Treasury yield and ongoing geopolitical tensions in West Asia. Thong remarked that the recent market correction has made selected blue-chip valuations more attractive, potentially providing downside support and encouraging more bargain hunting. He anticipates a gradual return of buying interest in fundamentally strong stocks, though a sustained recovery may require a more favorable external backdrop. The FBM KLCI is expected to trend within the 1,640-1,670 range for the remainder of the week. Among the heavyweights, Maybank remained at RM9.99, Public Bank dropped two sen to RM4.70, CIMB increased by one sen to RM7.79, Tenaga Nasional rose by 24 sen to RM12.96, and IHH Healthcare decreased by four sen to RM7.83. In active trading, Zetrix AI fell half a sen to 16 sen, V.S Industry rose 4.5 sen to 28 sen, Jaks Resources increased by 1.5 sen to 20.5 sen, Gamuda gained 20 sen to RM5.18, and Aimax was unchanged at 0.5 sen. Top gainers included Nestle, which rose RM1.00 to RM90.00, Allianz Malaysia, which added 76 sen to RM21.62, UWC, which increased 27 sen to RM7.07, United Plantations, which firmed 24 sen to RM31.56, and Petronas Gas, which advanced 22 sen to RM17.40. On the losing end, Hengyuan Refining dropped 78 sen to RM3.56, Malaysian Pacific Industries fell 40 sen to RM40.40, Kuala Lumpur Kepong decreased 30 sen to RM22.20, Genting Plantations declined 24 sen to RM5.53, and Eurospan fell 23 sen to RM3.01. On the index board, the FBM Mid 70 Index lost 35.42 points to 17,574.67, while the FBM Emas Index gained 26.55 points to 12,292.02, and the FBM Top 100 Index increased 32.90 points to 12,084.44. The FBM Emas Shariah Index rose 48.73 points to 12,176.35, and the FBM ACE Index added 5.70 points to 5,534.28. title: 'BernamaBiz - Malaysia Entering More Supportive Water Investment Cycle  -- CIMB Securities
body: 'Malaysia Entering More Supportive Water Investment Cycle -- CIMB Securities KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 (Bernama) -- Malaysia is entering a more supportive water investment cycle as ageing infrastructure, high water losses and rising industrial and data centre demand, as well as greater climate variability are increasing the urgency to improve water efficiency, reliability, and resilience. In a note today, CIMB Securities said the federal government had approved RM1.7 billion under the 13th Malaysia Plan to replace about 1,800 kilometres of critical pipes from 2026 to 2030, alongside a multi-year National Non-Revenue Water (NRW) Programme. It said sizeable projects including Langat 2 Phase 2, Rasau Phase 2, and the Northern Perak Water Supply Scheme should further strengthen water security and provide a visible pipeline for contractors, pipe manufacturers and ancillary solution providers. CIMB Securities said Malaysia’s NRW rate stood at 37.1 per cent in 2024. “Persistently high NRW, ageing distribution networks, and rising climate variability result in unnecessary raw water extraction, higher treatment and pumping requirements, weaker utility economics, and supply disruption risks. “Concurrently, population growth, industrialisation, and rapid data centre development are driving structural water demand, particularly across economic corridors in Selangor, Johor, and Penang,” it added. The stockbroking company said Malaysia’s water transition is seen broadening from purely building new infrastructure towards using existing water resources and assets more efficiently. It said sustainable NRW reduction requires physical rehabilitation alongside smart metering, leak detection, pressure management, telemetry, analytics, and intelligent asset-management systems. “These technologies can make water networks more visible, measurable, and manageable, improving the effectiveness of every ringgit spent on water infrastructure. “This is aligned with the Water Sector Transformation 2040 (WST2040), which promotes digitalisation, climate resilience, integrated water-resource management, and stronger sector governance,” it said. From an investment perspective, CIMB Securities said it favours companies positioned at either the efficiency or infrastructure-enablement layers of Malaysia’s water transition. “Insight Analytics Bhd is among the most direct listed proxies to water digitalisation and NRW management, while Gamuda Bhd offers exposure to large-scale treatment, transmission, and water security projects. “The key near-term risk remains the pace at which funding and policy commitments translate into tenders, project awards, and, ultimately, earnings,” it said. -- BERNAMA

title: 'Indonesia land reform raises uncertainty for Malaysian planters with exposure there — CIMB Securities
body:
'

KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 25): Malaysian plantation companies with sizeable operations in Indonesia face greater regulatory uncertainty following the country’s new agrarian reform law, with SD Guthrie Bhd (KL:SDG), Genting Plantations Bhd (KL:GENP) and Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd (KL:KLK) among those with the largest exposure, according to CIMB Securities.

The potential impact, however, remains unclear as key details — including maximum landholding limits for companies and affiliated entities, and how a provision requiring at least 20% of certain land to be made available for agrarian reform and redistribution — have yet to be finalised through implementing regulations.

As such, CIMB has not made any adjustments to its earnings forecasts or the land banks of plantation companies under its coverage, saying it sees higher regulatory uncertainty rather than an immediate loss of land or earnings.

“We do not expect an across-the-board 20% cut in existing land,” the research house said in a note on Friday.

Indonesia’s parliament approved the Agrarian Reform Law on Tuesday, creating a broader framework to address land ownership concentration, redistribution and longstanding agrarian conflicts. The law also provides for a dedicated body under the president to oversee implementation, supervision and conflict resolution.

However, the Indonesian government still needs to draw up implementing rules that will, among other matters, determine minimum and maximum landholding limits. Agrarian Affairs and Spatial Planning Minister Nusron Wahid said such details would be provided through subsequent regulations.

The development was reported earlier this week, including by Bloomberg, which highlighted broader risks to Indonesia’s plantation and property sectors. CIMB’s latest assessment focuses on the potential implications for Malaysian-listed plantation companies.

Among CIMB’s Malaysian plantation coverage, SD Guthrie, Genting Plantations and KLK have the largest absolute plantation exposure to Indonesia. IOI Corp Bhd (KL:IOICORP) has a smaller relative exposure, while Johor Plantations Group Bhd (KL:JPG), Ta Ann Holdings Bhd (KL:TAANN) and Hap Seng Plantations Holdings Bhd (KL:HSPLANT) have plantation operations entirely in Malaysia.

CIMB said the impact will depend on the final land limits, whether the 20% rule applies to existing plantations and how it will be implemented.

Bloomberg consensus as at Friday showed analysts remaining broadly positive on SD Guthrie and Genting Plantations, while views on KLK were more mixed.

For SD Guthrie, 17 analysts had "buy" calls and three had "hold" calls, with a 12-month target price of RM7.68. Genting Plantations had 10 "buy" calls and two "hold" calls, with a target price of RM6.81. KLK had nine "buy" calls, 10 "hold" calls, and one "sell", with a target price of RM24.57.

Separately, India’s decision to lower import duties on major edible oils could provide some support for crude palm oil (CPO) demand, although CIMB expects the benefit to Malaysian planters to be modest.

India cut the basic customs duty on crude palm oil and crude soybean oil to 5% from 10%, while eliminating the 10% duty on crude sunflower oil, effective Thursday. The Indian government said the move was aimed at reducing import costs and easing domestic edible oil prices.

CIMB said the lower CPO duty should reduce landed costs and support Indian palm oil imports, although the larger tariff reduction for sunflower oil could make it more competitive against palm oil and limit the increase in demand.

India accounted for about 17% of Malaysia’s palm oil export volume in 2025. CIMB said the main benefit for Malaysian planters would likely come through firmer CPO prices rather than a significant direct increase in export volumes.

CIMB maintained its CPO price forecasts at RM4,450 per tonne for 2026 and RM4,550 per tonne for 2027.

'Indonesia land reform raises uncertainty for Malaysian planters with exposure there — CIMB Securities '

KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 25): Malaysian plantation companies with sizeable operations in Indonesia face greater regulatory uncertainty following the country’s new agrarian reform law, with SD Guthrie Bhd (KL:SDG), Genting Plantations Bhd (KL:GENP) and Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd (KL:KLK) among those with the largest exposure, according to CIMB Securities.

The potential impact, however, remains unclear as key details — including maximum landholding limits for companies and affiliated entities, and how a provision requiring at least 20% of certain land to be made available for agrarian reform and redistribution — have yet to be finalised through implementing regulations.

As such, CIMB has not made any adjustments to its earnings forecasts or the land banks of plantation companies under its coverage, saying it sees higher regulatory uncertainty rather than an immediate loss of land or earnings.

“We do not expect an across-the-board 20% cut in existing land,” the research house said in a note on Friday.

Indonesia’s parliament approved the Agrarian Reform Law on Tuesday, creating a broader framework to address land ownership concentration, redistribution and longstanding agrarian conflicts. The law also provides for a dedicated body under the president to oversee implementation, supervision and conflict resolution.

However, the Indonesian government still needs to draw up implementing rules that will, among other matters, determine minimum and maximum landholding limits. Agrarian Affairs and Spatial Planning Minister Nusron Wahid said such details would be provided through subsequent regulations.

The development was reported earlier this week, including by Bloomberg, which highlighted broader risks to Indonesia’s plantation and property sectors. CIMB’s latest assessment focuses on the potential implications for Malaysian-listed plantation companies.

Among CIMB’s Malaysian plantation coverage, SD Guthrie, Genting Plantations and KLK have the largest absolute plantation exposure to Indonesia. IOI Corp Bhd (KL:IOICORP) has a smaller relative exposure, while Johor Plantations Group Bhd (KL:JPG), Ta Ann Holdings Bhd (KL:TAANN) and Hap Seng Plantations Holdings Bhd (KL:HSPLANT) have plantation operations entirely in Malaysia.

CIMB said the impact will depend on the final land limits, whether the 20% rule applies to existing plantations and how it will be implemented.

Bloomberg consensus as at Friday showed analysts remaining broadly positive on SD Guthrie and Genting Plantations, while views on KLK were more mixed.

For SD Guthrie, 17 analysts had "buy" calls and three had "hold" calls, with a 12-month target price of RM7.68. Genting Plantations had 10 "buy" calls and two "hold" calls, with a target price of RM6.81. KLK had nine "buy" calls, 10 "hold" calls, and one "sell", with a target price of RM24.57.

Separately, India’s decision to lower import duties on major edible oils could provide some support for crude palm oil (CPO) demand, although CIMB expects the benefit to Malaysian planters to be modest.

India cut the basic customs duty on crude palm oil and crude soybean oil to 5% from 10%, while eliminating the 10% duty on crude sunflower oil, effective Thursday. The Indian government said the move was aimed at reducing import costs and easing domestic edible oil prices.

CIMB said the lower CPO duty should reduce landed costs and support Indian palm oil imports, although the larger tariff reduction for sunflower oil could make it more competitive against palm oil and limit the increase in demand.

India accounted for about 17% of Malaysia’s palm oil export volume in 2025. CIMB said the main benefit for Malaysian planters would likely come through firmer CPO prices rather than a significant direct increase in export volumes.

CIMB maintained its CPO price forecasts at RM4,450 per tonne for 2026 and RM4,550 per tonne for 2027.

title: 'Malaysia’s First Nuclear Power Plant Could Come Online By 2040-2046, CIMB
body: 'Malaysia could potentially commission its first nuclear power plant between 2040 and 2046, as the country begins the lengthy process of assessing nuclear energy as a firm, low-carbon source of electricity amid rising power demand and energy security concerns, according to CIMB Securities.  In a sector report assessing Malaysia’s nuclear option, CIMB said the country has recently restarted Phase 1 of the International Atomic Energy Agency’s (IAEA) Milestones Approach, with MyPOWER Corp appointed to coordinate the feasibility assessment. The process requires the government to complete feasibility studies and establish a national position before making a knowledgeable commitment to a nuclear programme.  The IAEA estimates that all three phases required to develop nuclear power infrastructure could take 10 to 15 years, although there is no fixed timeline. Assuming Malaysia completes Phase 1 and formally decides to adopt nuclear power by 2030-2031, CIMB estimates another three to four years would be required for regulatory preparation, site assessment, vendor selection and commercial negotiations before construction or fabrication begins.  CIMB said renewed interest in nuclear power comes as the West Asia conflict highlights vulnerabilities in Malaysia’s energy supply while electricity demand is accelerating, partly due to investments in data centres.  Nuclear Offers Firm, Low-Carbon Power  According to CIMB, nuclear energy could provide Malaysia with firm and relatively clean baseload electricity, while using less land than solar photovoltaic projects and reducing exposure to volatile fossil fuel prices.  However, nuclear is neither the cheapest nor fastest new-build clean energy option, given the extensive planning, regulatory requirements and capital involved. Public acceptance also remains an important challenge.  From an ESG perspective, CIMB said Malaysia would need to balance the potential benefits of reliable low-carbon electricity against issues including affordability, safety, radioactive waste, water use, public acceptance and long-term government accountability.  The research house’s readiness assessment shows several areas remain unresolved. No project cost, electricity tariff model or site has been determined, while the owner and financing structure remain undecided. Commercial spent-fuel and disposal arrangements have also yet to be established, alongside funding mechanisms for waste management and eventual decommissioning.  TNB Could Play Key Role  Malaysia has, however, already identified several important institutional players.  MyPOWER has been appointed as the country’s nuclear energy programme implementing organisation, while Atom Malaysia would serve as the nuclear and radiation licensing regulator. Nuklear Malaysia would provide technical expertise and workforce development, while the Energy Commission would oversee electricity market-related matters.  The owner-operator has yet to be determined, but CIMB views Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) as the most logical anchor operator for a future baseload nuclear asset because of its balance sheet and control of the grid. An independent power producer with nuclear expertise could alternatively be involved to reduce project risk.  CIMB said private-sector participation during the initial stages would likely remain limited, apart from TNB’s potential role as the commercial delivery vehicle for a pioneering nuclear project. The research house maintained its BUY call on TNB with a target price of RM15.90, against RM13.90 at the time of the report.  Large Reactors, SMRs And Floating Plants Among Options  Malaysia has yet to settle on a reactor technology, with CIMB identifying conventional large-scale reactors, small modular reactors (SMRs) and floating nuclear power plants as possible options under evaluation.  Conventional reactors offer proven technology and economies of scale above 1,000MW but require substantial upfront investment and lengthy development. SMRs potentially offer lower initial capital requirements and modular expansion, although CIMB noted there are currently no proven commercially viable units demonstrating replicable economics.  Floating nuclear plants could reduce land constraints by locating reactors offshore, but may face complications involving international maritime law.  On ownership, CIMB considers full foreign control unlikely given Malaysia’s established government-linked entities. It suggested a structure similar to the UAE’s Barakah nuclear project could be more suitable, with TNB or another Malaysian project company retaining control while an experienced foreign nuclear supplier takes minority equity and provides turnkey construction and operating support.  CIMB said the ultimate decision should hinge not only on reactor technology but also on who bears the risks of construction cost overruns, delays, operating performance, fuel and waste obligations and long-term electricity tariffs.  For now, Malaysia remains at the assessment stage. CIMB noted that the next major milestones would be a formal commitment to a nuclear programme, followed by development of the regulatory framework, selection of reactor technology and finalisation of ownership and financing models.

title: 'CIMB Securities lifts 2026 GDP growth forecast to 5pct on domestic strength
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: CIMB Securities Research has raised its forecast for Malaysia's 2026 gross domestic product (GDP) growth to five per cent from 4.8 per cent previously, backed by stronger-than-expected domestic activity. "Following the weaker-than-expected July Industrial Production Index (IPI) outturn, the third quarter (Q3) 2026 GDP nowcast has edged down to 5.0 per cent from 5.2 per cent," it said in a note. However, CIMB Securities said the weakening in domestic manufacturing assumed in its house forecast has so far not materialised. The firm noted that domestic-oriented production outside the motor vehicle segment strengthened in July, while overall manufacturing output continued to expand sequentially. "We therefore raise our Q3 2026 GDP growth forecast to 4.5 per cent from 4.0 per cent previously, and our full-year 2026 forecast to 5.0 per cent from 4.8 per cent previously. "This reflects stronger-than-expected resilience in domestic activity," it said. On the overnight policy rate, CIMB Securities said its outlook remained unchanged, with the inflation trajectory the key factor in determining the timing of a rate hike. Nevertheless, the firm said renewed escalation in the Middle East remained a downside risk to growth, while prospective US semiconductor tariffs could weigh on electrical and electronics manufacturing and exports if introduced.

title: 'Fire safety managers, officers mandatory for 9,451 buildings from April 2027
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: From April 1, 2027, owners of 9,451 buildings across the country designated under the Fire Services Act will be required to appoint Fire Safety Managers (FSMs) and Fire Safety Officers (FSOs) at their premises. Fire and Rescue Department director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said the requirement was in line with Section 27A of the Fire Services (Amendment) Act 2025, which requires owners of designated premises to establish a Fire Safety Organisation (OKK). "From April 1, 2027, any building that we inspect within the next one or two years and which is required to obtain a Fire Certificate will have to appoint an FSM and FSO and establish a Fire Safety Organisation at the premises," he told reporters after the launch of the FSM and FSO programme at Menara Merdeka Maybank today. Nor Hisham said a preparation period of between six and 18 months would be given to building owners before full enforcement begins, depending on the expiry date of their existing certificates and the Fire Certificate inspection schedule. He said the enforcement was a strategic approach to reduce the department's workload, particularly in conducting annual inspections of premises. "In future, the annual inspection reports prepared by FSMs will be assessed by the department for the renewal of Fire Certificates without requiring physical inspections to be conducted by the Fire and Rescue Department every year," he said. To meet industry needs from 2026 to 2030, the department expected 6,000 FSMs and 18,000 FSOs to be appointed nationwide, he said. He said the fire department currently had 13 registered training providers and had issued a tender to increase the number of training providers and instructors. A total of 174 FSMs and 324 FSOs who formed the first group to complete the training received their certificates at the ceremony.

title: 'Axis REIT ‘well positioned’ against rate risks amid RM250 mil deal pipeline — analyst
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Longer-term financing secured much earlier is now providing Axis REIT (KL:AXREIT) cushion against rising interest rates as the real estate investment trust pursues deals, an analyst said. A 25-basis-point increase in policy rate would potentially raise its cost of borrowings by just 0.1 percentage-point to 4.06%, Maybank Investment Bank said, noting that Axis REIT has locked in 10-year and seven-year financing facilities over the past 12 months when rates were more favourable. “With the completion of signed acquisitions, gearing is expected to rise to around 39%, still having ample headroom before any equity raising is required,” the research house said. Axis REIT owns and manages more than 70 office and industrial assets worth over RM5 billion in Klang Valley, Penang, Johor, Pahang, Negeri Sembilan and Kedah. The trust is in the midst of acquiring a distribution centre, a warehouse, and an industrial complex for RM193 million combined. The stated aim is to nearly double the asset under management to RM10 billion by 2030, driven by high-growth sectors and key industrial hubs throughout Peninsular Malaysia. In the near term, Axis REIT has a RM250 million acquisition pipeline currently under negotiation, of which one or two transactions could be announced before year-end, Maybank Investment said and maintained its “buy” call on the trust. “We believe its acquisition pipeline should provide further income visibility” with most ongoing transactions fully occupied and carrying weighted average lease expiry of five years or longer, the research house said. Axis REIT has rebounded from its September lows when the US Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the first time in three years, sending global bond yields higher and triggering concerns of rising borrowing costs. title: 'MARC Ratings affirms PNB Merdeka Ventures’ sukuk at AAA
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: MARC Ratings has affirmed its AAAIS rating on PNB Merdeka Ventures Sdn Bhd’s (PNBMV) Merdeka Sukuk Wakalah Programme of up to RM6bil, with a stable outlook. The rating agency, in a statement, said the rating is equalised with the AAA/Stable corporate credit rating of Permodalan Nasional Bhd (PNB), based on publicly available information. It said the equalisation reflects PNB’s unconditional and irrevocable rolling guarantee to cover any shortfall in principal and profit payments under the sukuk programme. PNBMV, a wholly owned subsidiary of PNB, is undertaking the 40-acre Merdeka 118 development in Kuala Lumpur. The development includes the 118-storey Menara Merdeka Maybank, a retail mall and sites earmarked for two residential towers and a serviced apartment building. PNBMV is also the landowner and custodian of Stadium Merdeka and Stadium Negara, both of which are listed as National Heritage sites. MARC Ratings said PNBMV has leased all 84 floors of office space in the tower to PNB under a triple net master lease agreement, under which PNB bears property-related expenses in addition to rental and service charges. About 70% of the office tower's 1.6 million sq ft of net lettable area has been sub-leased, comprising 40% or 33 floors to Maybank, 20% to PNB and about 10% to other tenants. Occupancy is expected to rise to about 90% over the next five years, while the office tower is projected to generate annual net property income of about RM137mil. For the 750,324 sq ft retail mall, lease agreements covering 81% of its net lettable area have either been signed or are under negotiation, at an indicative average rental rate of RM11.92 per sq ft. The mall is expected to open in November. Meanwhile, two residential apartment buildings with a combined estimated gross development value (GDV) of RM2bil are targeted for launch in the first half of 2027. A serviced apartment component, with an estimated GDV of RM745mil, is planned for a later launch. MARC Ratings noted that the residential and serviced apartment components are exposed to demand risk due to competing developments in Kuala Lumpur. The Merdeka 118 development has incurred RM10.6bil in development costs to date, while the upcoming residential projects are expected to require another RM1.4bil, funded through a combination of borrowings and equity injections. MARC Ratings said recurring income from the completed development could reach RM500mil to RM600mil annually over the medium term.

body: '马股半天微升1.84点 科技指数涨1.69% （吉隆坡5日讯）美国非农就业数据放缓，降低联储局加息的概率，带动区域股市普遍上涨，马股周一在部分蓝筹股获得趁低吸纳下，一度攀升至1640点。 富时综指开盘涨2.55仙，至1633.42点，随后一度升至1640.46点之后回吐部分涨幅，午休上涨1.84点，至1632.71点，上周五收盘报1630.87点。  反映大盘走势的富时全股指数上扬27.99点，至12198.56点，创业板指数也起53.92点，至5583.38点。 马股主要指数起落不一，科技指数半日上涨1.69%，是表现最出色。另外，电讯媒体指数半日下挫2.12%，为表现最差。 场内有560只下跌股，超过477只上升股，另有473只平盘。全场成交量达29亿3086万零800股，总值13亿9406万零525令吉。 有16只综指股上涨、13只下跌和1只没有起落。上涨的股项包括马电讯(TM,4863,主板电讯媒体组)上涨16仙，至7令吉99仙；国际船务(MISC,3816,主板交通物流组)起9仙，收于7令吉62仙；99迷你超市(99SMART,5326,主板消费产品服务组)起7仙，收报3令吉13仙。 部分银行股走稳，丰隆银行(HLBANK,5819,主板金融服务组)起26仙，收报22令吉90仙；大马银行(AMBANK,1015,主板金融服务组)涨11仙，收于6令吉50仙；大众银行(PBBANK,1295,主板金融服务组)升高4仙，至4令吉70仙；但马来亚银行(MAYBANK,1155,主板金融服务组)却下挫2仙，至10令吉。 杨忠礼双雄双双走低，杨忠礼电力(YTLPOWR,6742,主板公用事业组)收报5令吉59仙，下跌9仙；杨忠礼机构(YTL,4677,主板公用事业组)收于2令吉19仙，下滑5仙。 ZETRIX公司(ZETRIX,0138,主板科技组)成为今天的市场焦点，该公司遭陆路交通局（JPJ）暂停代收服务之后，周一暂停交易一个小时，复牌之后股价应声下挫。 ZETRIX公司今早发文告证实，JPJ收款服务将于今日起暂停，该公司正在讨论解决此问题。 ZETRIX公司恢复交易后先跌至8仙，下滑3.5仙或30.43%，盘中最低跌至6.5仙，下挫5仙或43.48%，午休收于8仙，半天下滑3.5仙或30.43%，成交量更是突破8亿股，达到8亿6840万2700股成交，为全场最大热门股。  热门新闻 百格视频

title: 'UOB Malaysia, RHB Banking and Maybank execute landmark MYOR-based transaction
body: 'PETALING JAYA: UOB Malaysia, RHB Banking Group and Malayan Banking (Maybank) recently executed the first Malaysia Overnight Rate-based three-month interbank money market transaction in the country, incorporating a two-day lookback calculation convention through an interbank money market broker.   The landmark transaction was anchored by UOB Malaysia and executed with RHB and Maybank, marking a significant milestone in the evolution of Malaysia’s money market and supporting industry efforts towards the adoption of risk-free rate-based market conventions.

title: 'PMCK Expands Beyond Hospitals as Maybank Maintains BUY With RM0.35 Target Price
body: 'PMCK Bhd is entering a new phase of growth as the healthcare group expands beyond its core hospital operations into the medical consumables business. Maybank Investment Bank remains positive on the company, maintaining its BUY recommendation with an unchanged target price of RM0.35, compared with PMCK’s share price of RM0.195 in the report, implying potential upside of about 79%. A major highlight is PMCK’s proposed RM52.8 million acquisition of Marpoliq Sdn Bhd and Derberg Sdn Bhd, two medical consumables suppliers. The acquisition will broaden PMCK’s healthcare ecosystem from hospital services into sourcing and distribution of disposable medical devices, respiratory and airway products, feeding supplies, incontinence pads and other hospital and home-care accessories. Completion is targeted by 1Q27. Maybank views the deal positively because medical consumables provide recurring and higher-margin income while giving PMCK exposure to both government and private hospitals. Importantly, the acquisition comes with a RM3 million annual profit-after-tax guarantee for FY27E and FY28E. The deal is valued at just 7.2x P/E and 4.9x EV/EBITDA, significantly below the average valuations of Bursa-listed medical supply peers. The earnings impact could also be meaningful. Maybank estimates the acquisitions could increase PMCK’s FY27E core net profit from RM13.0 million to RM16.8 million, representing a 29.4% uplift after accounting for the acquired companies’ earnings contribution and additional interest expenses. Both businesses also enjoy stronger profitability, with FY26 PAT margins of 21.6% for Marpoliq and 29.1% for Derberg, compared with PMCK’s existing margin of around 12%. Beyond the acquisition, PMCK has an established healthcare footprint in northern Malaysia. It has operated PMC Alor Setar since 1995, while Kedah and Perlis remain relatively underserved in terms of private hospital beds. Another major catalyst is the upcoming 90-bed PMC Kulim hospital, targeted for 1QCY28, which should expand capacity and increase patient throughput. Maybank Investment Bank remains positive on the company, maintaining its BUY recommendation with an unchanged target price of RM0.35, compared with PMCK’s share price of RM0.195 in the report, implying potential upside of about 79%. A major highlight is PMCK’s proposed RM52.8 million acquisition of Marpoliq Sdn Bhd and Derberg Sdn Bhd, two medical consumables suppliers. The acquisition will broaden PMCK’s healthcare ecosystem from hospital services into sourcing and distribution of disposable medical devices, respiratory and airway products, feeding supplies, incontinence pads and other hospital and home-care accessories. Completion is targeted by 1Q27. Maybank views the deal positively because medical consumables provide recurring and higher-margin income while giving PMCK exposure to both government and private hospitals. Importantly, the acquisition comes with a RM3 million annual profit-after-tax guarantee for FY27E and FY28E. title: '石隆门女子遭假贷款群组连环套 汇款3次始觉受骗向警方求助
body: '（古晋3日讯）意图通过网上个人贷款缓解经济，学校保洁掉入网上诈骗陷阱，3次汇款共6400令吉给老千后，老千继续各种理由要求汇款、保洁才如梦初醒被骗并来到石隆门警局报案求助。  上述欺骗案是发生在石隆门警区，受害者是现年40岁来自石隆门甘榜瑟吉邦的女子，在石隆门某间政中任职保洁工作。  受害者是昨午5时15分来到石隆门警局报案求助，商业犯罪调查查案官已着手展开调查工作。  石隆门警区主任莫哈默海德今早向媒体发布有关讯息。  受害者是在9月28在工作地点游览面子书时，看到名为“myringgitcash”的个人贷款广告，并有意申请1万令吉的个人贷款。  受害人点击广告链接填写了申请人的个人信息，随后被添加到一个名为“myringgit10k”的WhatsApp群组。  加入该WhatsApp群组后，受害人与3名自称是群组管理员的人员联系，联系电话号码分别为011-11236641、011-21097126和011-28589136。  在与3个人交涉后，受害人于 9 月 29 日通过“myringgit10k”WhatsApp 群组被告知，其申请的贷款已获批准，并要求投诉人预先支付几笔款项，据称是为了将贷款资金存入受害人的账户。  因此，投诉人向2个不同的账户进行了三笔交易，具体如下：  2026年9月30日，向Muhammad Nurzaidi Bin Nazri名下的Maybank账户（151342200688）汇款1,100.00令吉 2026年10月1日，向Kannan A/L Gagendran名下的Maybank账户（362405001788）汇款2,200.00令吉 2026年10月1日，向Kannan A/L Gagendran名下的Maybank账户（362405001788）汇款3,140.00令吉  付款后，受害人仍被要求支付额外款项，但由于他认为自己受到了欺骗且未收到任何款项，因此没有继续支付并火速来道警局报案求助。

title: 'Nelly Korda's Deliberate Golf Break Costs Her as She Becomes Ineligible for LPGA Award - Report
body: 'Nelly Korda's Deliberate Golf Break Costs Her as She Becomes Ineligible for LPGA Award - Report Nelly Korda had a chance to settle her LPGA Hall of Fame future on the course this year. Victories at the Chevron Championship and U.S. Women's Open left her at 25 points, two short of induction. Given her early-season form, she was widely expected to earn those two points by the end of 2026. A single major win would have done it, but she has not won another major since June. Now, despite leading the tour in scoring average, Korda is set to miss another Hall of Fame point. This time, it has nothing to do with her performance or scores. Korda is ineligible for the Vare Trophy, the LPGA's award for lowest scoring average, due to insufficient rounds played, though she remains on track for Player of the Year. Golfweek's senior writer Beth Ann Nichols notes that the World No. 1 "currently leads the Vare Trophy race for low scoring at 69.38." However, she is not playing enough golf to win it. Had she earned the Vare Trophy, she would have received a Hall of Fame point. Paired with the Player of the Year award, which is worth one more point, that would have put her at 27. But the Vare Trophy has two key eligibility requirements. First, the golfer must play at least 60 individual-scoring rounds, or 60% of the applicable official rounds, whichever is lower. If Nelly Korda makes the cut at The ANNIKA and plays all four rounds of the CME Group Tour Championship, she will have played 61 rounds. However, she won't meet the second eligibility criterion, which is playing at least 70 rounds, or 70% of the applicable official rounds, whichever is lower. Counting the four rounds of the Dow Championship she played this summer, Korda finishes at 65 rounds. Thus, she falls five rounds shy of the eligibility criterion. She missed out on the Vare Trophy and the Hall of Fame point for the same reason in 2021. She could have become eligible if she had played two more events during the season. Her last event was the Solheim Cup, which Charley Hull & co. won. In total, she has made only 15 starts so far in 2026. She is now on a break that includes the ongoing Lotte Championship, which she is not playing. Golfweek reports that she will also be skipping the Asia swing, which includes the Buick LPGA Shanghai, the BMW Ladies Championship, the Maybank Championship, and the TOTO Japan Classic. This brings her total break to around two months. This isn't the first time she has missed the Asia swing. In fact, some fans have been outraged by her habit of skipping it. Korda has not played a fall Asian event since 2023. She skipped the 2024 stops after a neck injury sustained in practice. "I'm disappointed to miss these events and am especially sorry to my fans who were looking forward to seeing me play," she wrote in 2024. She also skipped last year's swing because of injury. After a top-five finish in Hawaii, Korda withdrew from the International Crown in October 2025 with an unspecified injury, and she was expected to sit out the Asia swing that followed. It came in a winless 2025 in which neck problems cost her time. Korda said after the Hawaii event that her body is "definitely worn down" by that point in the year, and she has stressed the need to be as close to 100 percent as possible before teeing it up. But despite the reduced schedule, the 28-year-old has a chance to win the remaining two points by the end of the season. She leads Haeran Ryu in the Player of the Year race by 75 points. So that is one possible point. In addition, she can win either The ANNIKA or the CME Group Tour Championship to earn the last point. Korda is a three-time winner at The ANNIKA and can do it again this year. Nelly Korda's shortened schedule has cost her another opportunity to add an LPGA Hall of Fame point, but her season is far from over. title: 'Syed Saddiq, Bella Astillah anjur 'Kenduri Rakyat' rai perkahwinan
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Bakal mempelai, Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman dan tunangnya, Bella Astillah menjemput orang ramai menghadiri majlis 'Kenduri Rakyat' di Muar, Johor dan Kota Kinabalu, Sabah, selepas mereka diijabkabulkan di sini, pada 10 Oktober ini. 'Kenduri Rakyat' meraikan perkahwinan Syed Saddiq dan Bella akan diadakan di Muar, Johor pada 25 Oktober, diikuti Kota Kinabalu, Sabah, pada 31 Oktober. Syed Saddiq yang juga Ahli Parlimen Muar berkata, kedua-dua majlis resepsi dirancang dalam tempoh kurang dua bulan dan mereka berdepan kekangan masa serta kesukaran mendapatkan lokasi majlis perkahwinan. "Majlis kahwin kami nanti bertemakan rewang. Kalau sebelum ini, sambutan Hari Raya yang saya anjurkan di Muar sudah mencecah 10,000 orang, jadi, kita jangka untuk kenduri kami lebih ramai yang akan datang. "Jadi, majlis itu nanti berkonsepkan 'siapa cepat dia dapat' (nikmati juadah). Jika makanan habis sekalipun, kami akan berada di sana untuk bersama dengan tetamu," katanya pada majlis Walimatulurus Bella Astillajh & Syed Saddiq di sini, hari ini. Difahamkan, sebanyak 10,000 cenderahati istimewa disediakan untuk tetamu. Sebelum ini, Syed Saddiq dan Bella dilapor mengesahkan bakal disatukan sebagai suami isteri pada 10 Oktober ini. Majlis pernikahan mereka akan berlangsung di aras 118, Menara Merdeka Maybank, di sini, dengan konsep serba putih disulami elemen Arab atau Islamik atas permintaan keluarga. Syed Saddiq dan Bella dilapor mula berkenalan dengan lebih rapat pada 2025 sebelum mengikat tali pertunangan pada 28 Mac lalu.

title: '马股随隔夜美股反弹，但投资者仍保持谨慎，综指仅微幅收高
body: '马股周五随隔夜美股反弹，由于市场对美债收益率和油价的担忧挥之不去，投资者仍保持谨慎并采取选择性投资策略，综合指数收盘仅微幅走高。 截至下午闭市，综合指数涨0.51点或0.03%，至1,630.87点。 市场整体表现平衡，全场上涨股592只，下跌股554只，562只平盘，另1041只股无交易。全天成交量42.59亿股，总成交额27.11亿令吉。 综指成分股涨跌互见，IHH医疗保健集团（IHH，5225，主板保健股）涨10仙至7.80令吉，国油贸易（PETDAG，5681，主板能源股）、PPB集团（PPB，4065，主板消费股）和国油石化（PCHEM，5183，主板工业股）各涨8仙，分别收在19.20令吉、9.15令吉和4.21令吉。 下跌股，雀巢（NESTLE，4707，主板消费股）跌48仙至89.52令吉，吉隆坡甲洞（KLK，2445，主板种植股）跌42仙至21.00令吉，马国际船务（MISC，3816，主板交通与物流股）跌15仙至7.53令吉，国油气体（PETGAS，6033，主板公用事业股）跌12仙至17.20令吉。 银行股，马银行（MAYBANK，1155）涨7仙至10.02令吉，大众银行（PBBANK，1295）跌1仙4.66令吉，联昌国际（CIMB，1023）跌4仙至7.65令吉，兴业银行（RHBBANK，1066）跌4仙至7.43令吉，丰隆银行（HLBANK，5819）跌20仙至22.64令吉，大马银行（AMBANK，1015）持平于6.30令吉。 热门股方面，Zetrix AI（ZETRIX，0138，主板科技股）跌5仙至11.5仙，捷硕科技（JAKS，4723, 主板建筑股）持平于18仙，JCY国际（JCY，5161，主板科技股）涨10.5仙至66仙，威铖（VS，6963，主板工业股）涨2仙至29仙，迪耐（DNEX，4456，主板科技股）涨2仙至51.5仙。 其他重要股项，马太平洋（MPI，3867，主板科技股）涨1.28令吉至42.40令吉，UWC公司（UWC，5292，主板科技股）涨47仙至7.57令吉；ENRA集团（ENRA，8613，主板产业股）跌25.5仙至72.5仙，安联保险（ALLIANZ，1163，主板金融股）跌20仙至20.80令吉。 亚太主要股指，新加坡海峡时报指数跌 0.58% 至 5,634.83 点，香港恒生指数跌 2.60% 至 23,972.29 点，日本日经指255数跌 0.94% 至 68,309.46 点，韩国首尔综合指数起 0.46% 至 7,003.74 点。中国股市适逢国庆长假期休市。

title: 'New Hilux catches fire after 40 days, son and mother awarded RM427,000
body: 'KUALA KUBU BARU: The Sessions Court has awarded more than RM427,000 in damages to a man and his mother after their new Toyota Hilux caught fire 40 days after it was registered, with the blaze spreading to their house.   Judge Norhayati Johar found that the fire was caused by electrical arcing at the vehicle's battery terminal connection and ruled that the Hilux did not meet the safety, durability and quality reasonably expected of a new vehicle.   She ruled in favour of plaintiffs V. Thiagarajan and V.C. Kamalam in their suit against Maybank Islamic Bhd and Toyota dealer Telagamas Motors Sdn Bhd.

title: 'Anak syarikat ES Sunlogy tuntut RM1.17 juta daripada Ecolectric, Maybank terlibat prosiding garnisi | DagangNews - Berita Bisnes Anda
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR 2 Okt - Anak syarikat milik penuh ES Sunlogy Berhad, Savelite Engineering Sdn Bhd sedang mengambil tindakan untuk menguatkuasakan penghakiman mahkamah bernilai RM1.17 juta terhadap Ecolectric Engineering Sdn Bhd selepas Mahkamah Tinggi membenarkan prosiding garnisi melibatkan Malayan Banking Berhad (Maybank). Mahkamah Tinggi Kuala Lumpur membenarkan permohonan Savelite bagi Perintah Garnisi Tunjuk Sebab terhadap Maybank, yang dinamakan sebagai garnisi pertama Ecolectric, dalam pendengaran ex parte pada 30 September lalu, menurut pemakluman ES Sunlogy kepada Bursa Malaysia. Mahkamah menetapkan 21 Oktober 2026 bagi pendengaran tunjuk sebab. Perintah Garnisi atau Garnishee Order merupakan proses undang-undang yang membolehkan pihak yang memperoleh penghakiman mahkamah memohon mendapatkan bayaran daripada wang milik pihak yang berhutang di bawah penghakiman tetapi dipegang oleh pihak ketiga, seperti bank. Dalam kes ini, Maybank dinamakan sebagai garnisi dan perlu menunjukkan sebab kepada mahkamah sebelum mahkamah memutuskan sama ada wang yang mungkin dipegang bagi pihak Ecolectric boleh digunakan untuk memenuhi penghakiman tersebut. Savelite akan mendapatkan Perintah Garnisi Tunjuk Sebab itu dan mengatur penyerahannya kepada Maybank mengikut arahan mahkamah. Prosiding itu menyusuli penghakiman ingkar pembelaan yang direkodkan terhadap Ecolectric pada 17 Ogos 2026 berhubung pertikaian kerja pemasangan elektrik bagi projek pembangunan kediaman di Damansara Heights. Pertikaian projek Damansara Heights Menerusi penghakiman itu, Ecolectric diperintahkan membayar RM1,174,327.72 kepada Savelite dalam tempoh 14 hari. Jumlah itu merupakan RM1,234,551.27 yang diputuskan mahkamah selepas ditolak wang tahanan RM60,223.55 yang dipegang Savelite. Pertikaian itu berpunca daripada surat anugerah bernilai kira-kira RM1.65 juta bertarikh 25 April 2022, apabila Savelite melantik Ecolectric sebagai subkontraktor untuk membekalkan tenaga kerja bagi pemasangan perkhidmatan elektrik untuk projek pembangunan kediaman 54 unit di Damansara Heights. Savelite mendakwa Ecolectric gagal atau enggan menempatkan tenaga kerja yang mencukupi atau berkemahiran di tapak, menyebabkan kerja tidak dapat dilaksanakan mengikut program yang dipersetujui. Savelite memfailkan writ saman dan penyata tuntutan terhadap Ecolectric pada Julai 2026. Menurut pemakluman ES Sunlogy, Ecolectric tidak memasukkan kehadiran dalam tempoh 14 hari selepas writ saman dan penyata tuntutan diserahkan serta gagal memfail dan menyerahkan pembelaannya dalam tempoh ditetapkan. Mahkamah Tinggi kemudian merekodkan penghakiman ingkar pembelaan terhadap Ecolectric pada 17 Ogos 2026. Selain bayaran RM1.17 juta, mahkamah memerintahkan ganti rugi am ditaksir dan kos RM528 dibayar oleh Ecolectric kepada Savelite. ES Sunlogy sebelum ini berkata Savelite telah membuat rosot nilai penuh sebanyak RM3.17 juta ke atas jumlah terhutang daripada Ecolectric berkaitan projek Damansara Heights dan Old Klang Road, mencerminkan penilaian kumpulan terhadap kebolehkutipan jumlah tersebut. - DagangNews.com

title: 'AHB kekal agihan pendapatan 5.00 sen seunit
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Amanah Hartanah Bumiputera (AHB) mengekalkan agihan pendapatan sebanyak 5.00 sen seunit bagi tahun kewangan berakhir 30 September 2026, membabitkan pembayaran keseluruhan RM236.41 juta kepada lebih 82,000 pemegang unit. Agihan itu merangkumi agihan pendapatan akhir sebanyak 2.10 sen seunit bagi tempoh enam bulan berakhir 30 September 2026, selain edaran bonus 0.40 sen seunit yang diumumkan oleh Pelaburan Hartanah Bhd (PHB) selaku penaja dana. Edaran bonus berkenaan diberikan bagi pegangan sehingga satu juta unit pertama bagi setiap pemegang unit, menjadikan jumlah keseluruhan agihan bagi tempoh enam bulan itu sebanyak 2.50 sen seunit. Jumlah berkenaan adalah tambahan kepada agihan interim sebanyak 2.50 sen seunit yang diumumkan pada April lalu, sekali gus menjadikan keseluruhan agihan bagi tahun kewangan 2026 sebanyak 5.00 sen seunit. Pengarah Urusan Kumpulan PHB, Mazuki Abdullah @ Muhammad, berkata prestasi itu mencerminkan daya tahan AHB serta kekuatan portfolio hartanahnya yang disokong pendekatan pengurusan aset dan pelaburan berdisiplin. Beliau berkata, pengumuman penawaran tambahan sebanyak 400 juta unit AHB baru-baru ini juga turut mencerminkan usaha pihaknya dalam memperluas peluang kepada lebih ramai pelabur Bumiputera untuk mengambil bahagian dalam pelaburan hartanah komersial utama. "Kami percaya AHB akan terus memainkan peranan penting dalam menyokong pembentukan kekayaan jangka panjang Bumiputera, di samping menjana nilai mampan kepada pemegang unit. "Kami akan terus memperkukuh kedudukan AHB sebagai instrumen pelaburan pilihan Bumiputera menerusi pengurusan modal berhemat, strategi pelaburan dinamik dan pengoptimuman portfolio secara berterusan bagi memastikan pertumbuhan mampan serta penciptaan nilai jangka panjang," katanya. Mazuki berkata, komitmen itu turut selaras dengan aspirasi Pelan Transformasi Ekonomi Bumiputera 2035 (PUTERA35) yang bertujuan memperkukuh penyertaan ekonomi, pemilikan aset dan pembentukan kekayaan Bumiputera. Sementara itu, Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif PHB Asset Management Bhd (PHBAM), Zulkifli Ishak, berkata pihaknya kekal komited menguruskan AHB secara bertanggungjawab bagi memastikan dana berkenaan terus menjadi pilihan pelaburan yang mudah diakses oleh pelabur Bumiputera. PHB turut berkata, menerusi agihan akhir tahun kewangan 2026, sebanyak RM120.13 juta akan diagihkan kepada pemegang unit dan dikreditkan dalam bentuk unit AHB ke akaun masing-masing selewat-lewatnya pada 13 Oktober ini. "Agihan berkenaan akan dilaburkan semula secara automatik bagi membolehkan pemegang unit meningkatkan pegangan pelaburan serta berpotensi menikmati manfaat pertumbuhan jangka panjang menerusi pengkompaunan," katanya. Pelabur Bumiputera boleh melanggan AHB pada harga tetap RM1 seunit, dengan pelaburan minimum RM100 dan maksimum RM1 juta. Sejak penubuhannya, dana itu sudah mengagihkan sejumlah RM2.7 bilion kepada pemegang unit Bumiputera. Langganan boleh dibuat melalui cawangan pengedar yang sah di seluruh negara, iaitu Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank), AmBank Bhd, AmBank Islamic Bhd, Bank Islam Malaysia Bhd dan Bank Kerjasama Rakyat Malaysia Bhd.

title: 'Daily Market Commentary - 29 Sep 2026
body: 'The local stock market traded sideways with slight downward bias on Monday, as subdued domestic catalysts and heightened global uncertainty weighed on investor sentiment. The FBM KLCI inched down by 1.60 points to close at 1,670.02, off an low of 1,668.61 and high of 1,674.11, as losers led gainers 748 to 388, on total turnover of 3.11bn shares worth RM2.40bn. Uncertainty surrounding Middle East tensions and persistent inflationary pressures is likely to continue clouding the outlook for the local market. Immediate support for the index stays at the June 2026 low (1,655), with stronger support coming from the 76.4%FR (1,610) and 61.8%FR (1,564). Meanwhile, immediate resistance is maintained at the June 2026 high (1,722), followed by tougher upside hurdles at the 123.6%FP (1,759) and 138.2%FP (1,805) ahead. Any weakness on Maybank shares towards the 38.2%FR (RM9.74) or the 23.6%FR (RM9.27) should encourage buying on weakness ahead of recovery upside towards the 76.4%FR (RM10.96) with next resistance coming from the 25/02/26 high (RM11.71). Sime Darby shares remain in base building mode pending recovery to the 123.6%FP (RM2.67), with a confirmed breakout to aim for the 138.2%FP (RM2.82) and 150%FP (RM2.94), while immediate chart supports are from the 30-day ma (RM2.45) and 76.4%FR (RM2.19). title: 'F1 Singapore Grand Prix value proposition still strong after 18 years
body: 'SINGAPORE – For 18 years, Singapore has marketed its Formula 1 Grand Prix not just as a motor race, but as a showcase of what the Lion City can do when it turns several kilometres of floodlit roads along the waterfront at dusk into a global stage.  Since September 2008, the Marina Bay Street Circuit has become one of the most iconic events on the F1 calendar, offering something no other city did – the first-ever night race.  The spectacle helped establish Singapore as a distinctive stop on the F1 calendar, while giving the city-state a high-profile platform to promote its hospitality industry, infrastructure, business environment and ability to stage a complex international event.  Now, a few countries in the region are seeking to replicate Singapore’s success and join the F1 bandwagon in hopes of global attention and attracting high-spending visitors.  After a nine-year hiatus, Malaysia is set to host an F1 race in Sepang again in October, while Thailand is targeting a street race in Bangkok’s Chatuchak area as early as 2028.  The emergence of new Asian contenders raises questions about whether the Singapore Grand Prix can continue to distinguish itself or if fans will be drawn away to rival races.  Market observers and economists believe it can.  “F1 is still delivering benefits to Singapore that outweigh the cost of hosting the event,” said Brian Lee, an economist at Maybank.  “While the direct tourism benefits may face diminishing returns, the race remains valuable as a platform for attracting high-spending visitors, business events and global capital,” he added.  He noted that the 2025 F1 race weekend drew a sell-out crowd of more than 300,000 fans. That was the second-highest attendance in the event’s history and an almost 12 per cent jump from 2024, suggesting the novelty remained.  Guy Llewellyn, academic director for Asia-Pacific at EHL Hospitality Business School, said it would be hard for other cities to replicate Singapore’s experience after it has run the event for 18 years, coordinating different stakeholders and building a strong international reputation.  “Singapore’s strategy has gradually evolved from hosting a sporting event to hosting a citywide festival. The concerts, entertainment zones, dining experiences, and new Barge Stage programming mean that visitors can spend an entire day in Marina Bay without focusing exclusively on racing,” the assistant professor said.  The Barge Stage waterfront amphitheatre will be unveiled in 2026 along with a line-up of international DJs.  “Few destinations can offer a Formula 1 circuit, internationally branded hotels, fine dining, nightlife and entertainment venues all within walking distance of one another,” Llewellyn said.  However, while being the first night race was once a powerful differentiator, the novelty naturally fades over time, making the broader ecosystem increasingly important in setting the experience apart, he added.  Faizal Yahya, senior research fellow at the Institute of Policy Studies at NUS’ Lee Kuan Yew School of Public Policy, also believes the race should go on.  The returns have been “a massive net positive”, as Singapore has gained a lot economically, strategically, and in terms of its global image, Yahya said.  From the inaugural night race in 2008 until 2024, the event generated around $2.2 billion in incremental tourism receipts, mostly for accommodation, attraction tickets, food and beverage, shopping and airfares. It also attracted more than 720,000 visitors over the period.  Lee said that this is equivalent to $129 million a year in incremental spending from tourists attending the race. That is 0.4 per cent of Singapore’s 2025 aggregate tourism receipts.  While this may be close to the $140 million annual cost of organising the race, there are other beneficiaries that are not captured by the tourism receipt figures.  These include companies involved in the track and venue setup, advertising and others that support the event, ranging from raw material suppliers, equipment rental, logistics and even laundry and cleaning services, Lee said.  Beyond grandstand ticket sales, F1’s ripple effect extends to drawing other high-profile events around the race period.  Every year, about 25 to 30 international conferences – including the Forbes Global CEO Conference, the Milken Institute Asia Summit and TOKEN2049 – have been held around race week, bringing in around 90,000 C-suites to Singapore.  High-net-worth travellers, who make up 30 per cent of F1 visitors, account for 40 per cent of tourist spending during race week, pushing up occupancy rates and hotel room rates even outside the race vicinity.  A large share of the race’s contracts is subcontracted to Singapore-based small and medium-sized enterprises, including firms in engineering, construction and hospitality, the Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry (METI) said.  About 30,000 staff, contractors and stakeholders work on each race. More than 1,000 students from the Institute of Technical Education and polytechnics are also trained each year for roles around the circuit, giving them exposure to the organisation of a major international event.  “This creates temporary employment for over 30,000 workers and students across logistics, advanced engineering, hospitality and specialised event staging,” Yahya said. Regional travel partnerships can encourage onward trips across ASEAN, while digital matchmaking connects delegates with local businesses. Hosting networking events in Marina Bay and Orchard Road can further showcase Singapore’s commercial ecosystem.  The Singapore Grand Prix was never just a sporting event from the start. It is being used as a tourism draw, a business-networking platform, a showcase for local companies and a recurring global advertisement for the city.  “The issue is less about whether Singapore should continue hosting F1, and more about whether it can continue extracting scarcity value from the event as competing cities replicate the street-race model,” Lee said.

The spectacle helped establish Singapore as a distinctive stop on the F1 calendar, while giving the city-state a high-profile platform to promote its hospitality industry, infrastructure, business environment and ability to stage a complex international event. title: '周四亚洲股市淡静、马股低开低走，综指收盘大幅下挫
body: '美国就业数据前市场谨慎，周四亚洲股市淡静，马股综合指数低开，午后跌势加深，闭市重挫近21点。 截至下午闭市，综合指数跌20.81点或1.26%，至1,630.36点。 市场整体表现偏软，全场下跌股750只，上涨股342只，495只平盘，另1174只股无交易。全天成交量30.99亿股，总成交额27.29亿令吉。 30只综指成分股有·27只·下跌，仅2只微涨，另外一只平盘。吉隆坡甲洞（KLK，2445，主板种植股）跌78仙至21.42令吉，齐力工业（PMETAL，8869，主板工业股）跌29仙至7.16令吉，国油贸易（PETDAG，5681，主板能源股）和马电讯（TM，4863，主板电讯与媒体股）各跌16仙，分别收在19.12令吉和7.85令吉。 此外，杨忠礼电力（YTLPOWR，6742，主板公用事业股）和SD牙直利（SDG，5285，主板种植股）跌各跌15仙，分别收在5.72令吉和6.05令吉，IHH医疗保健集团（IHH，5225，主板保健股）跌13仙至7.70令吉，99迷你市场集团（99SMART，5326 ，主板消费股）跌11仙至3.04令吉。 银行股，马银行（MAYBANK，1155）跌4仙至9.95令吉，大众银行（PBBANK，1295）跌3仙4.67令吉，联昌国际（CIMB，1023）跌10仙至7.69令吉，兴业银行（RHBBANK，1066）跌3仙至7.47令吉，丰隆银行（HLBANK，5819）跌30仙至22.84令吉，大马银行（AMBANK，1015）涨1仙至6.30令吉。 热门股方面，今天首日上市的GB联合（GBBOND，0475，创业板工业股）跌4.5仙（比IPO价低18%）至20.5仙，Zetrix AI（ZETRIX，0138，主板科技股）涨0.5仙至16.5仙，威铖（VS，6963，主板工业股）跌1仙至27仙，捷硕科技（JAKS，4723, 主板建筑股）跌2.5仙至18仙，迪耐（DNEX，4456，主板科技股）涨1仙至495仙 其他重要股项，马太平洋（MPI，3867，主板科技股）涨72仙至41.12令吉，亚逸控股（AYER，2305，主板产业股）涨20仙至7.70令吉；安联保险（ALLIANZ，1163，主板金融股）跌62仙至21.00令吉，联合种植（UTDPLT，2089，主板种植股）跌60仙至30.96令吉。 亚太主要股指，新加坡海峡时报指数跌 0.14% 至 5,667.68 点，日本日经指255数起 3.30% 至 68,958.72 点，韩国首尔综合指数起 1.95% 至 6,971.35 点。香港和中国股市适逢中国国庆日假期休市。
