title: 'Inside the UN tunnel
body: 'Guillermo R Barreto In September, like every year, the UN General Assembly commences. Heads of state take the floor to send messages to the world. These messages are broadcast on TV, transcribed, and recorded in official documents and the press. We have heard denunciations of violations of international law, calls for peace and coexistence, and also cynical remarks from leaders of genocidal entities. It is a month of speeches that surely generates revenue for the media and benefits the local economy of New York City. It is month that also entails significant expenses for the delegations of the 193 UN member nations, in addition to the numerous NGO delegations present at or around the event. The UN was founded in 1945 following the end of the Great Anti-Fascist War, referred to as World War Two, by the Eurocentric narrative. Its purposes, principles and structure are set forth in the UN Charter, signed on 26 June 1945, in San Francisco and enforced since 24 October of that same year. As stated in Article 1, its purpose is to maintain international peace and security and to promote friendly relations among nations, based on respect for the principle of equal rights and the self-determination of peoples. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member Fundamental freedoms, respect for human rights, and universal peace – these are legitimate principles worth fighting for. The history of the UN, however, does not show that it has been capable of defending the principles for which it was created. Let’s look at three examples of this. In 1993 amid the war in the former Yugoslavia, the UN Security Council adopted resolution 819, which required the parties to the conflict (in this case, Serbia and Bosnia and Herzegovina) to treat the city of Srebrenica and its surrounding areas as safe areas, free from armed attacks or any other hostile acts. At that time, Bosnian Serb forces were carrying out an operation to displace and exterminate the Muslim population of Bosnia, thousands of whom sought refuge in Srebrenica, where they expected protection from the UN through its protection force Unprofor. This protection never materialised, and the Bosnian Serb army attacked, resulting in the massacre of 8,372 people. Even today, hundreds of bodies have not been located. Rwanda is another tragic case. There, the United Nations Assistance Mission (Unamir) was established to mediate the conflict that had been brewing and that led, in 1994, to the massacre of the Tutsi population by the Hutu army and militias. The reality is that, while the Security Council debated whether to use the term ‘genocide’ to describe what was happening, Unamir’s blue helmets were restricted in their actions, their personnel reduced to 250 troops, and the slaughter continued, leaving hundreds of thousands of people unprotected; they were ultimately murdered before the eyes of a world that watched without reacting. The words of the peacekeeping force commander, Romeo Dellaire, speak volumes: “I know that the mourning for all those Rwandans who placed their faith in us and believed that the UN Peacekeeping Force was there to stop the extermination, to stop the killings, and to guide them toward peace will never end. That mission, Unamir, failed.” Another UN failure is reflected in the United Nations Stabilisation Mission in Haiti (Minustah). A blue helmet intervention was launched to “maintain peace and security and support a political process leading to elections in 2010”. The mission remained in place until 2017, when its continued presence was deemed unsustainable. The conduct of Minustah soldiers has been heavily criticised, with numerous cases of rape and abuse of women and children. The introduction of a cholera epidemic (due to negligence in the management of wastewater from the blue helmets’ camps), caused some 9,792 deaths and affected about 820,000 people between 2010 and 2019. To date, the UN has not provided any form of compensation, and there has been no restorative justice for these cases. These are just three examples. The reality is that the UN was born with fundamental flaws: - A General Assembly where all parties have a voice and a vote and pass resolutions that are merely deliberative in nature and not legally binding - A Security Council composed of five permanent members with veto power and 10 non-permanent members – five of whom are elected each year for a two-year term – who, although they can make decisions, are severely limited by the veto power of the permanent members This is a self-perpetuating structure that, day by day, seems to be turning into an empty shell, powerless to transform an increasingly cruel reality. Twenty years ago, in an iconic speech before the UN General Assembly, the then-president of Venezuela, Hugo Chávez, said: “The United Nations system that emerged after World War Two has collapsed, shattered, it does not work anymore.” In that speech, Chávez called for the re-founding of the UN and put four proposals on the table: - The expansion of the Security Council in both the permanent and non-permanent categories - The implementation of effective methods for addressing and resolving conflicts - The immediate abolition of the veto power - The strengthening of the role and powers of the secretary-general Chávez added that it was necessary to move the organisation’s headquarters to another country that, unlike the US, would respect the host country’s norms by not imposing visa restrictions on delegations that are entitled to participate in the General Assembly and in the organisation’s own meetings and activities. For this year’s 2026 Assembly, the State Department is preventing the Palestinian delegation from attending. The General Assembly reminded the US government of its commitment to respect the host country agreement and voted in favour of Palestine’s participation. President Mahmoud Abbas will, however, have to participate via videoconference. Thus, we are currently witnessing increasingly aggressive and shameless actions by the US administration. This is an administration led by a narcissist surrounded by religious fanatics for whom international law holds no value and who act consistently to weaken the UN system and the principles of multilateralism. This is an administration that relies solely on military might to impose its will and uses unilateral coercive measures (neither contemplated nor endorsed by the UN) to force countries to submit to US influence. “The devil came here yesterday. Yesterday, the Devil was here in this very place. This rostrum still smells like sulphur.” This is how Hugo Chávez began his speech before the UN General Assembly exactly 20 years ago, on 20 September, one day after the speech by US President George W Bush – a phrase that echoed through the halls of the UN and made its way around the entire world. In that speech, Chávez unequivocally denounced the US’ ambitions to dominate the world, to install a ‘world dictatorship”, and to impose a “very original” democracy “through explosions, bombings, invasions and bombs”. Without hesitation, he labelled Bush a cynic for speaking to nations with hypocrisy while expressing his desire to control everything. Today, the US imposes its will even on its allies, wields a deadly military apparatus, and has no qualms about expressing its expansionist and controlling ambitions. The UN, on the other hand, appears to be an organisation incapable of curbing those ambitions or stopping the genocide of the Palestinian people, the massacres in Sudan, or the imperialist aggressions against Venezuela, Cuba or Iran. Can we expect anything from this 81st UN General Assembly? In his speech, Chávez spoke of the need to rebuild the UN. This need remains more relevant than ever. He also left room for hope by expressing reasons to be optimistic: “Streams, alternative thoughts and movements, youths with different ideas are rising.” That is where hope lies – in the capacity of organised peoples fighting for a different future – and not, for now, in the hallways and rostrums of the UN, where the air still reeks of sulphur. – Globetrotter Guillermo R Barreto is Venezuelan and holds a PhD in science from the University of Oxford). A retired professor at Simón Bolívar University in Venezuela, he served as the country’s deputy science and technology minister, president of the National Fund for Science and Technology, and ecosocialism and water minister. He is currently a researcher at the Tricontinental Institute for Social Research and a visiting scholar at the Center for the Study of Social Transformations-Ivic. The views expressed in Aliran's media statements and the NGO statements we have endorsed reflect Aliran's official stand. Views and opinions expressed in other pieces published here do not necessarily reflect Aliran's official position.

Twenty years ago, in an iconic speech before the UN General Assembly, the then-president of Venezuela, Hugo Chávez, said: “The United Nations system that emerged after World War Two has collapsed, shattered, it does not work anymore.” In that speech, Chávez called for the re-founding of the UN and put four proposals on the table: - The expansion of the Security Council in both the permanent and non-permanent categories - The implementation of effective methods for addressing and resolving conflicts - The immediate abolition of the veto power - The strengthening of the role and powers of the secretary-general Chávez added that it was necessary to move the organisation’s headquarters to another country that, unlike the US, would respect the host country’s norms by not imposing visa restrictions on delegations that are entitled to participate in the General Assembly and in the organisation’s own meetings and activities. For this year’s 2026 Assembly, the State Department is preventing the Palestinian delegation from attending. The General Assembly reminded the US government of its commitment to respect the host country agreement and voted in favour of Palestine’s participation. President Mahmoud Abbas will, however, have to participate via videoconference. Thus, we are currently witnessing increasingly aggressive and shameless actions by the US administration. This is an administration led by a narcissist surrounded by religious fanatics for whom international law holds no value and who act consistently to weaken the UN system and the principles of multilateralism. This is an administration that relies solely on military might to impose its will and uses unilateral coercive measures (neither contemplated nor endorsed by the UN) to force countries to submit to US influence. “The devil came here yesterday. Yesterday, the Devil was here in this very place. This rostrum still smells like sulphur.” This is how Hugo Chávez began his speech before the UN General Assembly exactly 20 years ago, on 20 September, one day after the speech by US President George W Bush – a phrase that echoed through the halls of the UN and made its way around the entire world. In that speech, Chávez unequivocally denounced the US’ ambitions to dominate the world, to install a ‘world dictatorship”, and to impose a “very original” democracy “through explosions, bombings, invasions and bombs”. Without hesitation, he labelled Bush a cynic for speaking to nations with hypocrisy while expressing his desire to control everything. Today, the US imposes its will even on its allies, wields a deadly military apparatus, and has no qualms about expressing its expansionist and controlling ambitions. The UN, on the other hand, appears to be an organisation incapable of curbing those ambitions or stopping the genocide of the Palestinian people, the massacres in Sudan, or the imperialist aggressions against Venezuela, Cuba or Iran. Can we expect anything from this 81st UN General Assembly? In his speech, Chávez spoke of the need to rebuild the UN. This need remains more relevant than ever. He also left room for hope by expressing reasons to be optimistic: “Streams, alternative thoughts and movements, youths with different ideas are rising.” That is where hope lies – in the capacity of organised peoples fighting for a different future – and not, for now, in the hallways and rostrums of the UN, where the air still reeks of sulphur. – Globetrotter Guillermo R Barreto is Venezuelan and holds a PhD in science from the University of Oxford). title: 'AirAsia’s Hunt for Cheaper Debt Won’t be Easy With US$100 Oil
body: '(Sept 24): AirAsia Group Bhd’s (KL:AAGB) Tan Sri Tony Fernandes is fed up with private credit and the exorbitant interest rate they charge. “I don’t want to take any more private credit debt because it’s expensive,” the co-founder of one of the biggest Southeast Asian budget carriers said at a briefing last week. “I don’t want more debt. I don’t like debt.” While Fernandes is seeking to reduce interest payments — some as high as 11% — through a US$1 billion (RM4.09 billion) refinancing package, it may be tough for a company that sells cheap flight tickets to make money when oil prices are above US$100 a barrel. AirAsia’s finances are so strained that it loses money, has more liabilities than assets, and has a cash-to-revenue ratio that’s well below the industry standard. “AirAsia likely needs either a real improvement in operating cash flow or credit enhancement,” said Linus Benjamin Bauer, founder of aviation consultancy BAA & Partners. “Without that, cheaper money is difficult to justify.” Like most airlines, the Iran war hit AirAsia hard but the carrier, which doesn’t hedge its fuel costs, has been grappling with soaring prices to such extent that it went through two straight quarterly losses. Its total debt had surged to a record US$4.1 billion at the end of June, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. While the jump largely reflected Fernandes’ consolidation of all its airline businesses into AirAsia from sister firm Capital A Bhd (KL:CAPITALA), AirAsia’s liabilities exceeded assets by RM606 million as of end-June, according to the company’s first-half financial report. It also shows it had RM954 million in cash and RM18.4 billion in current liabilities due over the next 12 months, suggesting coverage of only 5%. The cash represents 4.3% of AirAsia’s annualized revenue of RM22 billion and “normal airline practice is to have cash and facilities of at least 10%-20% of annualized revenue”, said independent aviation analyst Andrew Light. Fernandes has received an offer for US$1 billion of financing from Middle East banks to refinance existing debt, but he’s holding off on a final sign-off while he searches for cheaper alternatives. AirAsia, which is also seeking RM700 million in local credit facilities, aims to complete the refinancing by December or January. AirAsia declined to comment on its recent fundraising efforts and whether talks with creditors reflected liquidity pressures or raised concerns about its ability to meet obligations without additional financing. “Unless Tony can present a credible business plan to get the airline back to positive cash flow, raising the money AirAsia needs on commercial terms will become increasingly difficult,” said Gerry Soejatman, an independent aviation analyst based in Jakarta. “That challenge will only get harder if oil prices stay elevated or rise further.” Highlighting its financial strain, AirAsia fell behind on dues to some suppliers and asked lessors to defer rental payments on more than 16 aircraft after fuel costs surged, Bloomberg reported in June. It had also asked private-credit lenders Ares Management Corp and Indies Capital Partners Pte Ltd to allow aircraft lessors to share revenue from routes pledged to their US$200 million facility. And since the start of 2025, it sold six brand new Airbus planes without ever putting them into service. Fernandes denied renegotiating with Ares, and said the jet sale reported by Bloomberg was inaccurate, adding the company was returning planes it didn’t need “in this crisis”. The planned US$1 billion in refinancing debt would save AirAsia around RM200 million a year in interest expense if it’s able to lower the interest rate on debt raised during the Covid pandemic and private credit to 7%-8% from around 11%, said Samuel Yin, associate director for equity markets research at Maybank Investment Bank. “The debt isn’t maturing this year, but the airline wants to prepare ahead of upcoming obligations. Given the rise in fuel prices, the costs are increasing,” said Yin, who said he met with AirAsia management earlier this month. Behind its fundraising efforts is a business that isn’t generating enough cash. AirAsia’s operations consumed RM582 million in the first half of 2026, according to its financial statement. Citigroup Inc downgraded its rating on AirAsia stock to sell from buy in a report this week, saying that its limited cash and equity buffers leave little room for another fuel-price shock. “We see jet fuel prices as the key determinant of future liquidity and profitability as balance sheet constraints remain,” Citigroup said. The Iran conflict has hit budget airlines particularly hard because they have less ability than full-service carriers to pass on higher fuel costs to passengers. The industry’s biggest casualty so far has been US low-cost carrier Spirit Aviation Holdings Inc, which collapsed in May amid soaring fuel prices and the failure of a government bailout. Fernandes has said his airline doesn’t need to be rescued by the Malaysian government, dismissing the idea of an intervention as “the most ludicrous statement I have seen in 25 years”. “AirAsia survived the pandemic without a government bailout and the brand has shown demand resilience,” said Bauer from BAA & Partners. “But with liquidity this tight, the margin for execution error remains limited.” Uploaded by Chng Shear Lane Source: TheEdge - 25 Sep 2026 Oct 01, 2026 Former Felda chief Faizoull Ahmad pleads not guilty to a 2014 cheating charge tied to 16 land plots and Synergy Promenade; court sets bail at RM70,000. title: 'Lelaki bebas tuduhan tipu RM108,500
body: 'Kota Kinabalu: Seorang lelaki bekerja sendiri berusia 50 tahun dilepas dan dibebaskan daripada pertuduhan menipu seorang lelaki membabitkan RM108,500 berkaitan beberapa projek di Kinabatangan dan Semporna. Majistret Wan Farrah Farriza Wan Ghazali memutuskan demikian selepas mendapati pihak pendakwaan gagal membuktikan kes prima facie terhadap Abdillah Hamzah. Abdillah dilepas dan dibebaskan tanpa dipanggil membela diri. Abdillah didakwa menipu Chong Kong Fah dengan memperdayakannya sehingga mempercayai bahawa tertuduh mengurus beberapa projek iaitu pembinaan jalan konkrit ke SMK Bukit Garam, Kinabatangan; menaik taraf sistem perparitan di Taman Perumahan Bukit Permata, Kinabatangan; membaiki jeti terapung di Dataran Lepa-Lepa, Semporna; menaik taraf jalan di kawasan Dolton Town, Semporna; dan membaiki rumah di Semporna. Pertuduhan menyatakan Chong memasukkan wang berkenaan ke dalam akaun syarikat bernama Dilwani Enterprise, yang tidak akan dilakukannya sekiranya tidak diperdayakan sedemikian. Kesalahan itu didakwa dilakukan antara 23 Jun 2016 dan 5 Disember 2018 di Maybank cawangan Semporna. Pertuduhan mengikut Seksyen 420 Kanun Keseksaan memperuntukkan hukuman penjara sehingga 10 tahun dan sebatan serta boleh didenda jika sabit kesalahan. Pihak pendakwaan memanggil enam saksi sepanjang perbicaraan. Timbalan Pendakwa Raya (TPR) Noor Hafizah Anggu hadir bagi pihak TPR Arfa Anchal Khan manakala peguam Nurul Rafeeqa Afdul Mutolip mewakili Abdillah. Sementara itu seorang lelaki berusia 64 tahun mengaku bersalah menyebabkan kecederaan parah terhadap seorang lelaki menggunakan parang. Bagaimanapun Hakim Mahkamah Sesyen Marlina Ibrahim menangguhkan hukuman terhadap Paul Akang ke 28 Oktober ini sementara menunggu laporan perubatan dan forensik. Sementara menunggu tarikh berkenaan, Paul direman lanjut. Paul didakwa menyebabkan kecederaan serius terhadap lelaki berusia 45 tahun itu menggunakan senjata berkenaan pada jam 5 petang, 21 September lalu di hadapan sebuah rumah di Kampung Kelansatan, Kuala Penyu. TPR Ronnie Antony mengendalikan pendakwaan kes berkenaan. Lelaki bebas tuduhan tipu RM108,500 Daily Express Daily Express Online (Malaysia) is Sabah's top-ranked & most viewed English news site. It is also Sabah's leading & most circulated daily English newspaper.

title: 'Mahkamah Tinggi kekal keputusan timbang tara anugerah RM77 juta kepada SUJV
body: 'Kuala Lumpur: Mahkamah Tinggi mengekalkan keputusan Tribunal Timbang Tara menganugerahkan RM77 juta kepada kontraktor utama Menara Merdeka Maybank (sebelum ini dikenali Menara Merdeka 118).   Keputusan tribunal menghendaki Global Wall (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd (GWM) membayar RM77,022,327.67 kepada Samsung C&T Corporation UEM Construction JV Sdn Bhd (SUJV) membabitkan pertikaian kerja fasad bagi projek mercu tanda berkenaan.   Pesuruhjaya Kehakiman, Rajes Raghavuji menolak permohonan GWM mencabar keputusan itu, dengan memutuskan isu dibangkitkan sama ada secara individu atau kumulatif, gagal melepasi syarat bagi membolehkan keputusan tribunal diketepikan mengikut Akta Timbang Tara.

title: 'Tengku Ampuan Pahang rasmi Kejohanan Golf Wanita, The Ladies 2026
body: 'PETALING JAYA: Kejohanan golf wanita, The Ladies 2026 rasmi membuka tirai kelmarin menerusi acara Pro-Am Diraja yang dirasmikan oleh Tengku Ampuan Pahang, Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah Almarhum Sultan Iskandar Al-Haj di The Mines Resort and Golf Club.   Kejohanan yang berlangsung selama tiga hari itu menyaksikan penyertaan seramai 50 pemain merangkumi kelompok profesional dan amatur termasuklah kemunculan semula juara bertahan, Liyana Durisic serta atlet Olimpik negara, Kelly Tan.   Menurut The Mines Resort & Golf Club, matlamat utama kejohanan itu adalah untuk melahirkan lebih ramai pemain berwibawa tempatan selain bertindak sebagai batu loncatan penting sebelum saingan bertaraf antarabangsa menjelang kejohanan Maybank Championship tidak lama lagi.

body: '户头解冻遭速提1165万 投资者迎追讨曙光 轰动全国的黄金投资骗局金玉华（Genneva Gold）私人有限公司，已被高庭正式颁布清盘令！ 马来西亚高庭于2026年9月30日正式批准清盘申请，此举为数以千计的受害投资者通过法律清盘程序、向该公司追讨多年血汗钱铺平了道路。法庭也同时确认黄荣富（译音）正式担任该公司的清盘人。 高庭法官旺法蒂拉诺在宣读判词时指出，法庭下令清盘基于三大理由：第一，该公司此前因非法吸收存款被定罪，证明其曾被用于非法用途；第二，公司停运多年，目前缺乏合法执照和准证恢复业务；第三，公司管理极度混乱，不仅未妥善保存秘书记录，更没有一个正常运作的董事会。 户头刚解冻 1165万遭“闪电”转移 此项清盘申请是由持有金玉华75万股的董事黄婉瑜（译音）于2024年8月提出。而促使她急切向法庭申请清盘的导火线，正是涉及一笔高达1165万令吉的银行资金被迅速提走的惊人内幕。 根据法庭文件，地庭于2024年6月下令撤销国家银行此前的资产扣押令，解冻了金玉华在马银行（Maybank）及大众银行（Public Bank）的户头资金。然而，款项解冻后，金玉华董事局随即批准将1165万9661令吉20仙的款项，迅速转入其长期法律顾问律师楼的客户托管账户。 更令人震惊的是，黄婉瑜声称，在资金移至律师楼账户后，其中竟有高达到1026万令吉，以“专业服务费（律师费）”的名义被转出。由于担心公司剩余资产沦为某些人的“私人利益”而非用于偿还投资者，她决定通过法律清盘，由独立清盘人介入展开深入调查。 清盘人接管 全面追查非法资产转移 已被法庭正式确认为清盘人的黄荣富表示，初步调查显示，金玉华的资产在过去确实曾被不当且违法地转移。 随着高庭正式下达清盘令，清盘人现已获得法律授权，全面接管并清查金玉华遗留的所有资产。接下来的核心工作将包括追查这笔被“速提”的千万资金去向、追讨不当转移的资产，并在稍后开放受害者索赔登记程序。受害投资者受促密切关注官方清盘资产申报流程，以保障自身权益。 清盘是投资者的“迟来正义”，但“能拿回多少”仍是残酷的未知数 虽然高庭颁布清盘令、委任独立清盘人全面追查是法律的胜利，但受害者切勿盲目乐观： 金玉华当年席卷的资金高达数十亿令吉，涉及数万名受害者。如今独立清盘人去追查的，只是这区区一千多万令吉的冰山一角。 清盘人黄荣富虽然誓言追讨，但要从律师楼的口袋里、从已定罪的高层资产中把钱“吐出来”，还需要经历无数轮的法律诉讼与资产清算。即便最终追回，在扣除清盘行政费、法律费及优先债权后，普通投资者能分到的数额恐怕也只是象征性的巴仙率（%）。 金玉华案跨越十余年，从高调吸金、国行取缔、漫长诉讼，到如今解冻后的“临终分赃”与强行清盘，它是一部活生生的大马金融血泪史。它再次敲响警钟：在崩盘的庞氏骗局面前，不仅骗子的承诺不可信，连高喊合法合规的“内部人”也随时准备在废墟上刮骨吸髓。 【金玉华案前因后果：从吸金数十亿到内部“闪电分赃”】 高调吸金（2009—2012年）： 金玉华打着“伊斯兰合规黄金买卖”旗号，以高于市价20%卖金并承诺每月给2%至3%高额回扣，吸引全马数万名投资者砸入数十亿令吉棺材本。 国行取缔（2012—2020年）： 2012年10月，国家银行突击查封该公司，大盘轰然倒塌。历经多年诉讼，上诉庭于2020年做出终审定罪，判定多名核心高层非法吸收存款及洗黑钱罪成，判监并重罚4.5亿令吉。 解冻速提（2024年）： 2024年6月，地庭撤销当年的资产扣押令，其银行户头重新解冻。不料，控制权派系董事随即采取“闪电操作”，将1165万令吉现金转入合作的律师楼户头，更将其中1026万令吉以“律师费”名义转出分赃。 内讧清盘（2026年9月30日）： 另一名董事黄婉瑜因不满千万资金被内部蚕食，愤而“掀桌子”申请清盘。高庭最终宣判金玉华正式破产清盘，由独立清盘人接管。 图取自中国报 【免责声明】 《风采》网站欢迎读者/网民留言，创造友好交流空间；唯网民留言皆不代表本网站立场。本网站有权删除任何人身攻击、鼓吹种族宗教隔阂、诽谤造谣、网络霸凌等煽动性留言。 想要买《风采》，网购最方便！ 👉 https://s.lazada.com.my/s.xqJTn (西马) 👉 https://s.lazada.com.my/s.xqJ58 (东马) 👉 https://my.shp.ee/urmN2pCX (西马) 👉 https://my.shp.ee/K9R1Es9m (东马) 👉订阅《风采》纸本杂志： https://shop.enanyang.my/product/feminine/

title: 'Wacana PTKP dan PPh 21 DTP belum cukup, PPN perlu turun jadi 8%
body: 'KONTAN.CO.ID-JAKARTA. Wacana pemerintah menaikkan batas Penghasilan Tidak Kena Pajak (PTKP) dan memperluas insentif PPh 21 Ditanggung Pemerintah (DTP) belum cukup untuk menggankat kesejahteraan hidup masyarakat yang masih tertekan.  Maklum, pemerintah belum mengubah besaran PTKP sebesar Rp 54 juta per tahun selama satu dekade.  Sementara itu, insentif PPh 21 DTP yang sebelumnya terbatas pada sektor padat karya dan pariwisata akan diperluas ke seluruh sektor bagi pekerja dengan gaji di bawah Rp 10 juta.  Kepala Ekonom Bank Maybank Indonesia Juniman menilai, kenaikan PTKP dan perluasan insentif PPh 21 DTP dapat memberikan ruang pendapatan lebih besar bagi masyarakat untuk meningkatkan konsumsi.  Namun, pemerintah tidak bisa hanya mengandalkan kedua kebijakan tersebut untuk mengerek daya beli.  "Kalau kita lihat, peningkatan PTKP itu memang menjadi keinginan pemerintah, terutama untuk meningkatkan daya beli masyarakat, khususnya kelas menengah ke bawah," ujar Juniman kepada Kontan, Rabu (30/9/2026).  Menurutnya, kenaikan PTKP akan membuat sebagian masyarakat yang sebelumnya mulai masuk sebagai wajib pajak menjadi tidak lagi terbebani pajak penghasilan. Dengan demikian, terdapat tambahan pendapatan yang bisa digunakan untuk konsumsi.  Namun, Juniman mengingatkan pemerintah agar tidak melihat kenaikan PTKP hanya dari sisi peningkatan daya beli. Pemerintah juga harus menghitung konsekuensinya terhadap penerimaan pajak.  "Hal ini harus dikalkulasi dengan betul-betul," jelasnya.  Menurut Juniman, persoalan daya beli masyarakat tidak akan selesai hanya dengan menaikkan PTKP. Kebijakan tersebut hanya menjadi salah satu instrumen untuk memberikan tambahan ruang konsumsi bagi masyarakat.  Terlebih, dalam kondisi ketika pertumbuhan pendapatan masyarakat tidak mampu mengejar kenaikan biaya hidup, pemerintah perlu menyiapkan kebijakan yang lebih luas.  "Dalam kondisi sekarang, ketika pendapatan masyarakat tidak meningkat secepat kenaikan biaya hidup, tentu ini akan menjadi masalah kalau pemerintah hanya berkutat pada PTKP," ujarnya.  Karena itu, Juniman mendorong pemerintah tidak hanya mengandalkan kenaikan PTKP dan insentif PPh 21 DTP. Pemerintah dapat mempertimbangkan penyesuaian tarif pajak, sembari memperluas basis penerimaan melalui ekstensifikasi pajak.  Salah satu opsi yang dapat dipertimbangkan adalah menurunkan tarif Pajak Pertambahan Nilai (PPN). Menurut Juniman, kebijakan tersebut dapat mengurangi beban masyarakat sekaligus mendorong konsumsi domestik yang saat ini mulai melambat.  "Kalau sekarang PPN 11%, dengan kondisi saat ini ketika konsumsi mulai melambat, paling tidak pemerintah bisa mempertimbangkan untuk menurunkan tarif PPN. Itu bisa mengurangi beban masyarakat dan pada akhirnya mendongkrak penjualan serta aktivitas ekonomi domestik," katanya.  Juniman bahkan menyarankan opsi penurunan tarif PPN hingga menjadi 8%. Namun, ia menekankan bahwa pemerintah harus menghitung secara cermat dampaknya terhadap volume transaksi dan penerimaan negara.  "Kalau misalnya 8%, volume-nya naik berapa, nanti kan ada datanya. Bisa naik atau turun. Paling enggak bisa sama," jelas Juniman.  Menurutnya, penurunan tarif pajak tidak selalu berarti penerimaan negara akan turun. Jika penurunan tarif mampu mendorong peningkatan volume transaksi dan konsumsi, penerimaan yang hilang dari sisi tarif dapat dikompensasi oleh kenaikan basis pajak.  "Peningkatan volume konsumsi sebenarnya secara langsung juga bisa meningkatkan penerimaan pajak. Jadi yang hilang dari tarif bisa dikompensasi dengan kenaikan volume yang ada," ujarnya.  Karena itu, pemerintah perlu melakukan analisis sensitivitas sebelum mengubah tarif PPN.  Perhitungan tersebut penting untuk melihat seberapa besar kenaikan volume transaksi yang diperlukan agar penerimaan pajak tetap terjaga.  Juniman menilai kombinasi kebijakan tersebut diperlukan lantaran perekonomian Indonesia masih sangat bergantung pada konsumsi domestik. Sementara itu, dorongan dari sektor eksternal relatif sulit diandalkan di tengah kondisi ekonomi global.  "Jadi, kalau tarif pajak bisa diturunkan terlebih dahulu, kemudian ketika ekonomi sudah tumbuh cepat, tarif bisa dinaikkan kembali secara perlahan. Istilahnya, ada trade off di situ," pungkasnya.

Dengan demikian, terdapat tambahan pendapatan yang bisa digunakan untuk konsumsi.  Namun, Juniman mengingatkan pemerintah agar tidak melihat kenaikan PTKP hanya dari sisi peningkatan daya beli. Pemerintah juga harus menghitung konsekuensinya terhadap penerimaan pajak.  "Hal ini harus dikalkulasi dengan betul-betul," jelasnya.  Menurut Juniman, persoalan daya beli masyarakat tidak akan selesai hanya dengan menaikkan PTKP. Kebijakan tersebut hanya menjadi salah satu instrumen untuk memberikan tambahan ruang konsumsi bagi masyarakat.  Terlebih, dalam kondisi ketika pertumbuhan pendapatan masyarakat tidak mampu mengejar kenaikan biaya hidup, pemerintah perlu menyiapkan kebijakan yang lebih luas.  "Dalam kondisi sekarang, ketika pendapatan masyarakat tidak meningkat secepat kenaikan biaya hidup, tentu ini akan menjadi masalah kalau pemerintah hanya berkutat pada PTKP," ujarnya.  Karena itu, Juniman mendorong pemerintah tidak hanya mengandalkan kenaikan PTKP dan insentif PPh 21 DTP. Pemerintah dapat mempertimbangkan penyesuaian tarif pajak, sembari memperluas basis penerimaan melalui ekstensifikasi pajak.  Salah satu opsi yang dapat dipertimbangkan adalah menurunkan tarif Pajak Pertambahan Nilai (PPN). Menurut Juniman, kebijakan tersebut dapat mengurangi beban masyarakat sekaligus mendorong konsumsi domestik yang saat ini mulai melambat.  "Kalau sekarang PPN 11%, dengan kondisi saat ini ketika konsumsi mulai melambat, paling tidak pemerintah bisa mempertimbangkan untuk menurunkan tarif PPN. Itu bisa mengurangi beban masyarakat dan pada akhirnya mendongkrak penjualan serta aktivitas ekonomi domestik," katanya.  Juniman bahkan menyarankan opsi penurunan tarif PPN hingga menjadi 8%. Namun, ia menekankan bahwa pemerintah harus menghitung secara cermat dampaknya terhadap volume transaksi dan penerimaan negara.  "Kalau misalnya 8%, volume-nya naik berapa, nanti kan ada datanya. Bisa naik atau turun. Paling enggak bisa sama," jelas Juniman.  Menurutnya, penurunan tarif pajak tidak selalu berarti penerimaan negara akan turun. Jika penurunan tarif mampu mendorong peningkatan volume transaksi dan konsumsi, penerimaan yang hilang dari sisi tarif dapat dikompensasi oleh kenaikan basis pajak.  "Peningkatan volume konsumsi sebenarnya secara langsung juga bisa meningkatkan penerimaan pajak. Jadi yang hilang dari tarif bisa dikompensasi dengan kenaikan volume yang ada," ujarnya.  Karena itu, pemerintah perlu melakukan analisis sensitivitas sebelum mengubah tarif PPN.  Perhitungan tersebut penting untuk melihat seberapa besar kenaikan volume transaksi yang diperlukan agar penerimaan pajak tetap terjaga.  Juniman menilai kombinasi kebijakan tersebut diperlukan lantaran perekonomian Indonesia masih sangat bergantung pada konsumsi domestik. Sementara itu, dorongan dari sektor eksternal relatif sulit diandalkan di tengah kondisi ekonomi global.  "Jadi, kalau tarif pajak bisa diturunkan terlebih dahulu, kemudian ketika ekonomi sudah tumbuh cepat, tarif bisa dinaikkan kembali secara perlahan. Istilahnya, ada trade off di situ," pungkasnya.

title: 'Maybank Upgrades HEGROUP to Buy After RM124m Johor Data-Centre Contract Win
body: 'Maybank Investment Bank analyst Thong Kei Jun upgraded HE Group to “Buy” from “Hold” and raised his target price to RM1.35 from RM0.96, implying 25% upside. The upgrade followed a RM124 million electrical subcontract for a Johor data centre, lifting HE Group’s 2026 year-to-date contract wins to RM416.6 million—already above Maybank’s initial RM350 million full-year assumption. Its outstanding order book now stands at RM441 million. Thong Kei Jun does not yet have a one-year expert rating on StockTipRatings, based on data since 2023, due to insufficient qualifying one-year performance data. Over the three months following his calls, the stocks he covered recorded an average return of 24% and a 55% success rate. Thong expects further data-centre work to support growth, with such projects accounting for about 80% of HE Group’s RM1 billion tender pipeline. He also anticipates a pickup in semiconductor tenders in the first half of 2027. Reflecting the stronger contract momentum, he raised his 2026–2028 core-profit forecasts by 3%–48% and now projects RM19.1 million, RM33.1 million and RM37.3 million, respectively. As of 9:40 a.m. on September 25, HE Group's share price rose 3.7% to RM1.12. Disclaimer: All content is AI-aggregated from public sources for informational and educational purposes only. title: 'Maybank finalises RM2.5bil sukuk
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) has completed the issuance of RM2.5bil additional tier 1 (AT1) sukuk mudharabah under its sukuk programme. In a Bursa Malaysia filing, the banking group said the perpetual sukuk comprises three series with nominal amounts of RM750mil, RM1.1bil and RM650mil, respectively. The RM750mil tranche carries a fixed distribution rate of 4.85% per annum until its first call date on Sept 29, 2031, while the RM1.1bil tranche carries a rate of 5.11% until its first call date on Sept 28, 2033. Meanwhile, the RM650mil tranche has a fixed distribution rate of 5.15% per annum until its first call date on Sept 26, 2036. The proceeds will be used for syariah- compliant purposes, including investments in ringgit- and foreign currency-denominated Islamic financial instruments approved by the syariah advisory councils of Bank Negara Malaysia or the Securities Commission. — Bernama Thank you for your report!

title: 'Maybank completes RM2.5bil AT1 sukuk mudharabah issuance
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) has completed the issuance of RM2.5 billion additional tier 1 (AT1) sukuk mudharabah under its sukuk programme. In a Bursa Malaysia filing today, the banking group said the perpetual sukuk comprises three series with nominal amounts of RM750 million, RM1.10 billion and RM650 million, respectively. The RM750 million tranche carries a fixed distribution rate of 4.85 per cent per annum until its first call date on Sept 29, 2031, while the RM1.10 billion tranche carries a rate of 5.11 per cent until its first call date on Sept 28, 2033. Meanwhile, the RM650 million tranche has a fixed distribution rate of 5.15 per cent per annum until its first call date on Sept 26, 2036. "The relevant reset distribution rates for the three tranches are based on the prevailing five-year, seven-year and 10-year Malaysian Government Securities rates, respectively, plus their respective initial spreads for fixed rates of 0.98 per cent, 0.97 per cent and 0.98 per cent per annum," said Maybank. The proceeds would be used for shariah-compliant purposes, including investments in ringgit- and foreign currency-denominated Islamic financial instruments approved by Bank Negara Malaysia's Shariah Advisory Council or the Securities Commission Malaysia's Shariah Advisory Council. It would also be used to fund the Islamic business activities of Maybank's subsidiaries and overseas branches, as well as other shariah-compliant business activities, said Maybank. The returns from the investments would be used for the periodic distributions of the AT1 sukuk mudharabah, which are payable semi-annually. The sukuk has been assigned an AA3 rating by RAM Rating Services Bhd.

title: 'Maybank’s MAE App Now Checks Your Phone For More Scam Risks
body: 'Maybank has upgraded Malware Shielding, the security check built into its MAE app. According to Maybank’s announcement, the new version is rolling out in stages from 26 September 2026. The upgrade lets it spot more kinds of risk on your phone.  If it finds a risk, MAE will tell you what’s wrong and how to fix it. For more serious risks, it may stop you from using the app until the problem is gone.  Malware Shielding Checks Your Phone Every Time You Open MAE  Malware is harmful software that scammers trick people into installing. They often send a link to an app file instead of pointing people to an official app store. Once malware is on a phone, it can read the TAC or OTP codes your bank sends you, or let a scammer control the phone from far away and approve transfers.  Malware Shielding looks for these dangers each time you launch MAE. In 2024, the Association of Banks in Malaysia (ABM) said this kind of check only runs when you open a banking app. It doesn’t keep running in the background all day. Maybank says the feature doesn’t collect or store the personal content on your phone, such as your photos, messages, or contacts.  The Phone Settings And Apps MAE Now Looks Out For  Some of the risks on Maybank’s list are clearly dangerous, such as scam apps. Others are everyday tools. Maybank says a VPN or a keyboard app from an unknown developer may expose your password, your TAC, or other banking details to people you don’t know.  Several of these have normal uses. People use VPNs for work or to watch shows from other countries, and some use screen recording to show a family member how to pay a bill. Maybank’s list doesn’t make exceptions for these, so switch them off before you open MAE.  A Warning Or A Lockout Depends On The Risk  Malware Shielding may warn you, show you steps to fix the problem, or block MAE until it’s fixed. Maybank’s FAQ says this depends on how serious the risk is.  Maybank doesn’t say which risks only bring up a warning and which lock the app. Because the check runs every time you open MAE, a setting you switch on later, such as screen recording, can still trigger it the next time you log in.  Other banks run similar checks. Members of ABM and the Association of Islamic Banking and Financial Institutions Malaysia (AIBIM) began adding malware shielding to their apps in August 2024. Banks that had switched it on by then included CIMB, Public Bank, RHB, and UOB, so you may see similar warnings in their apps too.  In June 2026, ABM reported that malware shielding helped stop more than 60,000 malware-related scam attempts in 2025, involving about RM22 million in potential losses.  A Malware Shielding Alert Can Affect Whether You Get Your Money Back  Bank Negara Malaysia’s (BNM) SEFT policy sets out when banks compensate victims of unauthorised transactions, including money taken through malware. However, BNM’s 2025 Annual Report says some victims may be held fully responsible and get no compensation at all. One example it gives is a victim who downloads a harmful app even after the bank has warned them about the risk.  So if you tap past a Malware Shielding alert and carry on, it could be harder to get compensation if a scammer later takes money from your account.  Update MAE And Tap Agree To Keep Using It  To get added Malware Shielding protection, update MAE to the latest version from Google Play, the App Store, or Huawei AppGallery. After the update, MAE will ask you to read and agree to the Malware Shielding terms and conditions. This step is compulsory, so you can’t keep using the app until you tap “Agree”.  If MAE blocks you, follow the steps on your screen. You may be asked to delete a suspicious app, turn off a setting such as Developer Mode, stop screen sharing or recording, switch to a supported phone, or reinstall MAE from an official app store. Once that’s done, close MAE and open it again.  If you’re still locked out, call Maybank Group Customer Care on 1-300-88-6688, or +603-7844 3696 from overseas. If you think money has already left your account, turn on your bank’s kill switch and call the National Scam Response Centre on 997. The line is open 24 hours, and your call counts as a police report.

title: 'Maybank Turned Its Cash Back Card Perks Into A Playground At Mid Valley
body:
'

Last week, we dropped by Mid Valley Megamall to check out the Maybank Cash Back Mastercard Platinum showcase. Held at Centre Court from 23 to 27 September, the five-day event had a little bit of everything, from interactive activities to a closer look at the card’s features.

A Station For The Card’s Benefits

The showcase was set up like a stamp-card journey. We picked up a journey card at the start and worked our way through five stations. The first four were More To Discover, Stream For More, More To Enjoy and More To Unwind. Once we had collected all four stamps, we could head to the final stop, Maybank Cafe, and redeem either a ZUS Coffee or a Krispy Kreme doughnut.

The activities at each station were also designed around the card’s benefits. One had a touchscreen game where you had to catch groceries in a basket, a playful take on the card’s 8% cash back on digital lifestyle spending. There were also photo spots with airplane window backdrops featuring destinations like Singapore, Thailand, Japan and South Korea, which are among the countries where the card charges no foreign exchange mark-up fee.

Visitors who applied for the card on-site could unlock three additional activities. These included a Flight Simulator and a Merchandise Redemption station with goodies such as a Maybank tumbler and Lilo & Stitch tote bag. Applicants could also try their luck at a giant Gashapon machine for prizes including a Nintendo Switch 2, Setel vouchers and Grab vouchers.

Card Benefits At A Glance

The Event Has Ended, But You Can Still Win

If you missed the showcase, you can still catch Maybank’s upcoming contest for cardholders, which runs from 1 October to 31 December 2026. 

You’ll earn entries by spending at least RM1,000 a month on the card, giving you a chance to win one of these prizes:

Full contest details are available on Maybank’s contest page. 

To find out more about the Maybank Cash Back Mastercard Platinum and see how it compares with other cashback cards, visit our credit card page.

Follow us on our official WhatsApp channel for the latest money tips and updates.

title: 'Penangan BTS! Army Sanggup Beratur Awal Pagi Di Cawangan Maybank Untuk Dapatkan Kad Debit Edisi Terhad
body: 'Sekilas  Peminat BTS sanggup beratur awal pagi di cawangan terpilih Maybank untuk mendapatkan kad debit edisi terhad kumpulan itu. Hanya 60 keping kad ditawarkan setiap hari, tetapi Maybank juga menyediakan permohonan secara dalam talian bermula 28 September. Kad debit ini adalah sebahagian daripada kerjasama Maybank dengan siri jelajah dunia BTS, WORLD TOUR ARIRANG.  Penangan kumpulan terkenal Korea Selatan iaitu BTS memang tidak dapat disangkal apabila peminat kumpulan itu dilihat sanggup beratur dari awal pagi di beberapa cawangan Maybank bagi mendapatkan kad debit edisi terhad kumpulan berkenaan.  Meskipun hanya 60 keping kad ditawarkan setiap hari di cawangan terpilih, namun itu tidak menghalang golongan Army dari mendapatkan kad edisi terhad tersebut.  Bagi yang tidak berkesempatan untuk beratur, Maybank turut menyediakan pilihan permohonan secara dalam talian yang akan dibuka mulai 28 September ini.  Kad debit edisi terhad tersebut merupakan sebahagian daripada kerjasama Maybank bersempena siri jelajah dunia BTS yang akan datang, WORLD TOUR ARIRANG.  Kerjasama tersebut sekali gus memberi peluang kepada peminat BTS untuk memiliki kad debit khas yang menampilkan elemen berkaitan kumpulan tersebut.

title: 'Maybank Lancar Kad Debit Visa Edisi Terhad BTS ‘Arirang’, Peminat Boleh Dapatkan Di 12 Cawangan Terpilih
body: 'Suami isteri meninggal selang sehari, terpisah di dunia hanya beberapa jam. Sehidup semati, jodoh hingga ke syurga. Ungkapan itu cukup dekat dengan Allahyarham Alias bin Panjang Aris dan isterinya, Allahyarhamah Roezah binti Abdul Hamid apabila kedua-duanya dijemput Ilahi dalam tempoh tidak sampai 24 jam. Setelah puluhan tahun hidup bersama, membina keluarga dan melalui susah senang sebagai suami isteri, tiada siapa menyangka perpisahan hanya berlaku seketika buat suami isteri ini. Arwah Roezah sempat menghantar arwah suami ke tanah perkuburan sebelum mengikut jejak suami dikasihinya itu. Kisah kehilangan dua insan tersayang ini dikongsikan cucu mereka, Haziq Azmin menerusi Threads. Jelasnya, arwah datuk dan Opah cukup dekat di hatinya kerana sejak kecil, insan inilah yang menjaganya di saat ibu bapanya keluar bekerja mencari rezeki. Malah dia akui bukan mudah menerima hakikat perpisahan ini dan mengambil masa untuk berkongsi kisah duka ini. “Baru ada kekuatan nak buat post ni.” tulis Haziq Azmin. Membuka cerita tentang kedua-duanya, Haziq berkongsi bahawa arwah atuk dan Opah dilahirkan dalam bulan yang sama iaitu pada bulan Mei. Arwah atuk dilahirkan pada 28 Mei 1942 sementara arwah Opah pula pada 13 Mei 1948. Tarikh mereka meninggal dunia juga berdekatan. Arwah atuk meninggal pada 26 Ogos 2026, manakala arwah Opah sehari selepas itu iaitu pada 27 Ogos 2026. Menurut Haziq, keadaan kesihatan arwah atuknya sudah lama uzur malah doktor ada memaklumkan hal ini kepada keluarga. “Arwah atuk menghembuskan nafas terakhir kira-kira pukul 7.56 malam. Kami sekeluarga dah terima atuk pergi, sebab doktor memang bagitahu keadaan atuk dah kritikal. Namun kami semua tidak menyangka akan menerima satu lagi berita duka dalam masa terdekat, selang sehari. Mengimbas kembali pagi terakhir dirinya diuji kehilangan dua insan kesayangan, Haziq memaklumkan Opahnya turut berada di tanah perkuburan ketika jenazah atuk dikebumikan sekitar pukul 11 pagi. “Opah ada bersama kami di tanah perkuburan. Saksikan arwah atuk sampai siap dimasukkan ke liang lahat. Siap siram kubur atuk lagi dan sempat berbual dengan saudara-mara yang hadir. “Tak ada pun tanda-tanda Opah sakit. Balik dari tanah perkuburan, Opah berehat seketika. Sehinggalah jam 3.50 itu, Opah bangun mahu mandi tapi badannya tak larat bangun. Ibu saudara saya maklum yang Opah nampak lain dari kebiasaan. “Opah beritahu dia susah bernafas. Tanpa sempat kami beri bantuan apa-apa, Opah menyusul ikut arwah Atuk. Tak sangka, secepat itu opah pergi. Memang tak dijangka kami sekeluarga,” jelasnya. Selepas semuanya berlaku, Haziq teringat kembali kata-kata yang pernah dilontarkan arwah Opanya ketika mencium jenazah atuk buat kali terakhir. “Bila nak jumpa lagi ni bang, nanti kita jumpa ya.” Inilah kata-kata akhir Opah ketika mencium arwah atuk dan tak sangka, kata-katanya itu menjadi kenyataan. Keduanya hidup bersama di dunia dan pergi juga selang sehari. “Pasangan sehidup semati, insya-Allah pasangan syurga opah dan atuk.” Jelas anak muda ini lagi, hubungannya dengan arwah atuk dan nenek agak rapat kerana dua insan inilah yang menjaganya dari kecil. “Aku dijaga oleh opah dan atuk sejak kecil time mak ayah pergi kerja. Aku masih tak boleh proses apa yang berlaku,” kongsinya di threads. Jika 26 Ogos hari istimewa bagi sebahagian dari kita, berbeza buat diri Haziq. Pada tarikh yang sama juga iaitu 26 Ogos, ayahnya meninggal dunia 9 tahun lalu dan tarikh itu juga dikongsi dengan pemergian atuknya, Alias. “Semoga arwah opah dan atuk ditempatkan di kalangan orang yang beriman. Kita jumpa kat sana ye opah atuk,” tulisnya mengakhiri kisahnya di threads. Semoga Allah SWT mencucuri rahmat ke atas roh Allahyarham Alias bin Panjang Aris dan Allahyarhamah Roezah binti Abdul Hamid, mengampunkan segala dosa, melapangkan kubur serta menempatkan kedua-duanya dalam kalangan orang beriman dan beramal soleh. Bercinta di dunia, semoga dipertemukan kembali dan kekal berjodoh hingga ke syurga. Al-Fatihah. Lubuk konten tentang inspirasi, rumah tangga dan macam-macam lagi, MINGGUAN WANITA kini di download sekarang!

title: 'All You Need To Know About The BTS Arirang x Maybank Visa Card That’s Now Available In Malaysia
body:
'

BTS World Tour Arirang x Maybank Visa

It’s finally a Spring Day for Malaysian fans of BTS. Not literally – all we’ve got is summer over here – but fans can have a spring in their step after a drought of being left out of tour schedules and merch release lists.

Besides 2 concert dates scheduled in Malaysia, the latest merch drop from BTS on our shores comes in the form of an Arirang-themed Visa debit card, with the group’s name on a plastic card we can not leave home without.

What is the BTS World Tour Arirang Visa card for?

As the Worldwide Tour Sponsor for BTS World Tour Arirang – which unites the formidable 7-member group at 82 shows in 34 cities in five continents – Visa has been partnering with card issuers around the globe for limited-edition BTS Arirang debit cards. These cards are recognised as official merchandise by the group’s agency, HYBE, which means another merch item to cop and use in your daily life.

Each country gets its own special Arirang Visa card design, inspired by the colours and motifs of the BTS album and tour – it’ll feel a bit like getting your hands on an exclusive photocard, except this one carries your moolah.

How to get the card? 


Image credit: Lizzy

In Malaysia, Visa has collaborated with Maybank to launch the Arirang-themed Visa card: a slick, all-black matte card with the BTS tour name in shiny lettering and the Arirang red logo on the top right.

There are two ways to get it from the Malaysian bank: offline and online. Here’s how:

Offline

From 23rd September 2026 onwards, fans can head to 12 Maybank branches nationwide to get their hands on the BTS World Tour Arirang Maybank Visa card.

The branches all open at 9.30am on weekdays, with card replacements and applications for new Maybank accounts to secure the card all done over the counter.

To ensure there are enough cards to go around, each branch has a strict daily 60-card issuance rule – in other words, each bank will only grant 60 BTS Visa cards per day to 60 customers. Expect queues even before opening hours because of this.


Image credit: Lizzy

Once you’re through the bank doors as one of 60 lucky fans of the day, it’ll be time to cheer. Look forward to fast service from bank staff who’ll hand you a queue number, and proceed to take your MyKad or passport, current debit card if not lost, and a thumbprint for application when your number is called. At the end of the process, you’ll be issued the BTS Visa card along with an envelope containing a sticker and celebratory message.

There’s a small “replacement” fee of RM12 to get the card, which will be deducted from your Maybank account funds.

Image credit: Lizzy

Here are the locations where you can process your application in person:

  1. Bukit Bintang
  2. Mid Valley City
  3. KL Main Branch (Menara Tun Perak)
  4. Dataran Maybank
  5. Petaling Jaya Main Branch
  6. Shah Alam Main Branch
  7. Penang Main Branch (Lebuh Union)
  8. Ipoh Main Branch (Jalan Sultan Idris Shah)
  9. Kuantan Main Branch (Jalan Sultan Abdullah)
  10. Johor Bahru Main Branch (City Square)
  11. Karamunsing (Bangunan Maybank)
  12. Kuching Main Branch

Online

Opt to skip the physical queues altogether if you’re an existing Maybank debit cardholder. You can get the BTS World Tour Arirang card online through the bank’s Maybank2u website, with online replacement requests accepted from 28th September onwards.

There’s also a RM12 replacement fee for this option, but it’ll be free if you have just 12 months left before your card’s expiry date.

Here’s how to submit a replacement request online:

  1. Log in to Maybank2u
  2. Go to Settings, select ‘Cards’
  3. Select ‘Manage Debit Cards’, then ‘Debit Card – Replace, Activate & Block’
  4. Click the three dots next to your debit card, select ‘Replace/Renew Card’
  5. Find the BTS World Tour Arirang debit card as your design of choice, and then click Next
  6. Fill in your delivery address, acknowledge the Terms & Conditions, and click ‘Submit’
  7. Verify your request with an SMS TAC or Secure 2U via the Maybank2U app
  8. Voilà, the replacement has been processed

Guide to get the BTS World Tour Arirang Visa card in Malaysia

Not every fan can say they have a Visa card with their favourite group on it. If you identify as an ARMY, the limited-edition BTS World Tour Arirang Visa card will be one to get, even if the process to get them might feel a little like the war for tickets.

Cover image adapted from: @votingbrigade via X, Lizzy

title: 'Ekonom Maybank Ungkap Penyebab Belanja APBN Belum Dorong Ekonomi
body: 'KONTAN.CO.ID - JAKARTA. Belanja pemerintah yang meningkat belum sepenuhnya memberikan dampak terhadap sektor riil dan pertumbuhan ekonomi Indonesia.  Kepala Ekonom Maybank Indonesia Juniman menilai keterbatasan keterlibatan sektor swasta menjadi salah satu faktor yang membuat efek pengganda belanja pemerintah belum maksimal.  Sampai Agustus 2026, belanja APBN tumbuh 17,1% secara tahunan (year on year/yoy), sedangkan pendapatan negara meningkat 25,4% yoy. Dengan perkembangan tersebut, APBN mencatat defisit Rp 240 triliun atau setara 0,93% terhadap produk domestik bruto (PDB).  Di sisi lain, keseimbangan primer masih mencatat surplus sebesar Rp 154 triliun.  "Keseimbangan primernya juga masih surplus, artinya pendapatan dikurangi belanja masih surplus," ujar Juniman kepada Kontan, Minggu (20/9/2026).  Meski kondisi fiskal hingga Agustus masih terjaga, Juniman mengingatkan tekanan terhadap defisit APBN akan meningkat mulai September. Hal ini sejalan dengan pola belanja pemerintah yang biasanya meningkat pada September hingga Desember.  Peningkatan belanja tersebut salah satunya berasal dari pembayaran subsidi energi dan nonenergi yang umumnya dilakukan setelah proses audit Badan Pengawasan Keuangan dan Pembangunan (BPKP).  "Makanya, pada Agustus pembayaran tersebut memang belum terlihat. Artinya, pembayaran subsidi masih belum seluruhnya dilakukan," katanya.  Namun, besarnya pertumbuhan belanja pemerintah belum otomatis menghasilkan multiplier effect yang signifikan terhadap perekonomian.  Menurut Juniman, aliran belanja pemerintah masih banyak mengarah ke sektor non-tradable. Sementara itu, sektor tradable seperti pertanian dan manufaktur belum memperoleh dorongan yang sebanding.  Sejumlah program pemerintah, seperti Makan Bergizi Gratis (MBG), Koperasi Merah Putih, dan Sekolah Rakyat, juga dinilai lebih banyak memiliki karakter konsumtif.  Di sisi lain, hilirisasi yang menjadi salah satu agenda pemerintah cenderung bersifat capital intensive sehingga kemampuan menyerap tenaga kerja relatif terbatas. Kondisi serupa juga terjadi di sektor pertanian yang semakin banyak memanfaatkan mesin dan teknologi dalam proses produksi.  "Belanja pemerintah tumbuh 21,05% yoy di kuartal kedua, tapi ekonomi kita hanya tumbuh sekitar 5% yoy," ujar Juniman.  Peran Swasta Perlu Diperkuat  Juniman menilai keterbatasan dampak belanja pemerintah terhadap pertumbuhan ekonomi juga tidak terlepas dari masih kecilnya keterlibatan sektor swasta dalam berbagai program ekonomi pemerintah.  Kontribusi government spending disebut hanya sekitar 6% terhadap PDB. Sementara itu, konsumsi rumah tangga menyumbang hampir 54% terhadap PDB. Dengan struktur tersebut, penguatan daya beli masyarakat menjadi salah satu faktor penting untuk menopang pertumbuhan ekonomi.  "Jadi, walaupun belanja pemerintah ditingkatkan sampai berapa pun, kalau porsinya hanya sekitar 6% terhadap PDB, perannya tetap relatif kecil," katanya.  Karena itu, menurut Juniman, APBN perlu diarahkan untuk menciptakan insentif yang dapat menggerakkan sektor riil dan usaha masyarakat, khususnya kelompok kelas menengah.  Ia mengatakan masyarakat berpendapatan rendah relatif telah mendapatkan dukungan melalui berbagai program bantuan sosial, seperti Program Keluarga Harapan (PKH) dan bantuan lainnya. Sementara itu, kelas menengah masih membutuhkan stimulus untuk mempertahankan konsumsi.  Juniman juga menyoroti dominasi pemerintah dalam sejumlah program ekonomi, termasuk hilirisasi, MBG, dan Koperasi Merah Putih. Menurut dia, keterlibatan sektor swasta masih terbatas, sementara Danantara juga menaungi badan usaha milik negara (BUMN) yang terkait dengan pemerintah.  "Seharusnya pemerintah melibatkan swasta untuk menggerakkan mesin ekonomi," ujarnya.  Ia melihat pola tersebut memiliki kemiripan dengan periode pemerintahan sebelumnya, ketika sejumlah proyek besar banyak dikerjakan oleh BUMN. Saat ini, pola serupa dinilai terlihat dalam sejumlah program prioritas pemerintah, meskipun bentuk proyeknya berbeda.  Apabila sektor swasta tidak ikut bergerak, peningkatan pendapatan masyarakat akan lebih sulit terjadi. Kondisi tersebut berpotensi membuat konsumsi rumah tangga stagnan atau tumbuh lebih lambat.  Padahal, konsumsi rumah tangga memiliki kontribusi sekitar 54% terhadap PDB.  "Kalau konsumsi melambat, sementara daya beli hanya tumbuh 4%–5%, sulit bagi ekonomi kita untuk mencapai 6%," kata Juniman.  Sementara itu, kontribusi ekspor yang sekitar 20% dan investasi sekitar 20%–30% dinilai belum cukup untuk mengimbangi perlambatan konsumsi. Terlebih, kondisi ekonomi global masih menghadapi berbagai tantangan sehingga Indonesia tidak dapat sepenuhnya mengandalkan ekspor sebagai sumber pertumbuhan.  Defisit APBN 2026 Diproyeksi Mendekati 3%  Dari sisi fiskal, Juniman memperkirakan defisit APBN akan meningkat signifikan mulai September seiring dengan akselerasi belanja pemerintah.  "Defisit biasanya mendekati 1,9% atau 1,8%, kemudian langsung lompat dan mendekati 2%. Setelah itu, pada Oktober dan November akan terus meningkat sampai akhirnya mencapai level yang diinginkan pemerintah, yaitu 2,85%," jelasnya.  Juniman memperkirakan defisit APBN 2026 berada di kisaran 2,8% hingga 2,93% terhadap PDB. Proyeksi tersebut masih berada dalam kisaran pemerintah dengan asumsi dilakukan refocusing, efisiensi, dan efektivitas belanja, khususnya untuk program-program prioritas.  Menurut Juniman, sejumlah program seperti MBG, Koperasi Merah Putih, dan Sekolah Rakyat sulit untuk dihentikan. Oleh karena itu, pemerintah perlu mencari ruang efisiensi dari pos belanja lainnya, termasuk belanja kompensasi subsidi, terutama subsidi energi.  "Pemerintah mau tidak mau harus melakukan efisiensi karena belanja yang lain sudah dihabiskan dan sudah tidak bisa lagi ditekan," katanya.  Untuk pertumbuhan ekonomi, Juniman memperkirakan ekonomi Indonesia pada 2026 tumbuh sebesar 5,3%, atau di bawah target APBN sebesar 5,4%.  Ia juga memproyeksikan pertumbuhan ekonomi pada kuartal III 2026 melambat menjadi sekitar 5,2%. Sementara itu, pertumbuhan ekonomi pada kuartal IV 2026 diperkirakan berada di kisaran 5,2% hingga 5,25%.  Adapun target pertumbuhan ekonomi sebesar 6% pada tahun depan dinilai membutuhkan kontribusi yang lebih besar dari sektor swasta.  "Mesin pertumbuhan harus dikerahkan, terutama di sektor swasta. Tanpa peran swasta, sulit bagi ekonomi kita untuk tumbuh di atas 6%," pungkas Juniman.

title: 'Maybank, ABS jalin kerjasama tingkat piawaian penasihat kekayaan
body: 'PETALING JAYA: Malayan Banking Berhad (Maybank) dan Asian Banking School (ABS) menandatangani Memorandum Persefahaman (MoU) bagi membangunkan kerangka pensijilan profesional penasihat kekayaan pertama yang diiktiraf industri di Malaysia. Kerangka kerja yang dikenali sebagai Program Pensijilan Pengurusan dan Penasihat Kekayaan ABS itu bertujuan menetapkan standard kompetensi khusus bagi profesional penasihat kekayaan dalam sektor perbankan. Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif Kumpulan Perkhidmatan Kewangan Komuniti Maybank, Syed Ahmad Taufik Albar berkata, kerjasama itu membolehkan Maybank menyumbang pengalaman melangkaui organisasi bagi meningkatkan standard profesional di Malaysia. “Maybank terus melabur dalam membangunkan profesional kekayaan kami menerusi Maybank Wealth Academy bagi membina keupayaan penasihatan holistik yang memenuhi keperluan kewangan pelanggan. “Peluang ini turut membuka ruang untuk memeluaskan elemen program berkenaan ke peringkat serantau dari semasa ke semasa,” katanya dalam kenyataan. Sementara itu, Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif ABS, Profesor Dr. Manivanan Saman berkata, gabungan kepakaran ABS dan pengalaman praktikal Maybank bertujuan mewujudkan laluan kredibel yang memberikan penanda aras lebih jelas kepada profesional kekayaan. “Maybank bertindak sebagai Rakan Industri Pengasas dengan menyumbang kepakaran dan pengalaman dalam pembangunan bakat, manakala ABS membawa kepakaran dalam pembangunan dan pensijilan perbankan profesional,” katanya. Pengambilan pertama bagi program berkenaan dijangka bermula pada separuh kedua tahun 2027, dengan Maybank berhasrat mengintegrasikannya ke dalam Maybank Wealth Academy. Langkah berkenaan memperkukuh francais pengurusan kekayaan Maybank yang baru-baru ini dinamakan sebagai Bank Swasta Terbaik Malaysia 2026 oleh Euromoney serta Bank Pengurusan Kekayaan Terbaik di Malaysia oleh Alpha Southeast Asia bagi tahun ke-10 berturut-turut. –UTUSAN

title: 'Sabah Energy Corp raises RM350 mil in maiden sukuk, Maybank IB appointed as adviser
body:
'

KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 17): Sabah Energy Corporation Sdn Bhd (SEC) has raised RM350 million through its maiden sukuk issuance under a RM3 billion sukuk wakalah programme.

The issuance was announced in a joint statement with Malayan Banking Bhd (KL:MAYBANK). 

The sukuk was rated AAA with a stable outlook by RAM Rating Services Bhd and was priced through book-building, with demand reaching 2.2 times the amount offered.

Maybank Investment Bank Bhd was appointed as the sole principal adviser, lead arranger, lead manager and sustainability structure adviser, as well as shariah adviser and facility agent. 

“This landmark issuance broadens and diversifies SEC's access to long-term ringgit funding while raising the profile of both SEC and Sabah among domestic and international institutional investors. The strong over-subscription reflects investors' confidence in SEC's credit strength and growth trajectory," said Maybank IB chief executive officer Michael Oh-Lau.

Maybank said the issuance gives the Sabah state-owned energy company a longer-term funding source as it plans investments across its energy businesses, including natural gas infrastructure, power generation and renewable energy.

SEC said the funding platform will support its strategic roadmap called PETA (Pelan Strategik dan Hala Tuju) 2030, which covers the expansion of its gas and infrastructure operations, power generation and renewable energy activities, as well as investments across Sabah's energy value chain.

“In turn, this supports the broader outcomes envisaged under SERAMP 2040: stronger energy security, a faster energy transition and more reliable supply for Sabah," said SEC group chief executive officer Datuk Adzmir Abd Rahman. 

SEC has been Sabah's sole natural gas aggregator, transporter and distributor since its corporatisation in 1997. 

It has since expanded into power generation, renewable energy and offshore oil and gas support services.

title: 'Maybank Islamic agih wakalah zakat RM869,806 bantu asnaf di Kedah
body: 'Kuala Lumpur: Lembaga Zakat Negeri Kedah (LZNK) menerima suntikan Wakalah Agihan Zakat bernilai RM869,806.58 daripada Maybank Islamic Berhad bagi menyokong pelaksanaan empat inisiatif utama pembangunan ekonomi dan kebajikan golongan asnaf di negeri Kedah. Peruntukan strategik itu merangkumi penyediaan modal perniagaan, latihan kemahiran teknologi pembuatan, pengurusan pusat agihan makanan, serta pembekalan mesin jahitan untuk menjana pendapatan keluarga fakir dan miskin. Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif Maybank Islamic Berhad, Mohamad Yasin Abdullah berkata, komitmen bank itu terhadap golongan memerlukan tidak terhad kepada bantuan kewangan semata-mata, malah memberi fokus mendalam kepada pembinaan keupayaan, peluang serta pendedahan yang mampu membantu golongan asnaf mengubah taraf kehidupan mereka. "Sebagai badan korporat dan institusi perbankan Islam, Maybank Islamic komited dalam usaha kami untuk memajukan dan membantu golongan asnaf dengan memberi peluang dan pendedahan kepada mereka mengenai mekanisme terbaik untuk mengubah kehidupan mereka. "Bagi mencapai matlamat ini, kami telah merangka pelbagai program tanggungjawab sosial korporat, terutamanya dalam menyantuni golongan yang memerlukan di seluruh cawangan Kumpulan Maybank dan bekerjasama erat dengan Majlis Agama Negeri dan badan-badan zakat di seluruh Malaysia, termasuk LZNK," katanya dalam kenyataan. Sementara itu, Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif LZNK, Datuk Syeikh Zakaria Othman berkata, model wakalah zakat berupaya bertindak sebagai intervensi pembangunan tersusun yang menghubungkan latihan kemahiran, peluang kerjaya, serta bantuan asas. "Dana berkenaan bukan sekadar bantuan jangka pendek, sebaliknya bertujuan mewujudkan ekosistem pendapatan yang lebih stabil kepada penerima manfaat menerusi pendekatan berfokus dan berimpak tinggi," katanya. Daripada keseluruhan peruntukan, komponen terbesar iaitu RM484,880 disalurkan bagi menyokong Program Latihan Kemahiran Teknologi Pembuatan di KHTP Techno Centre yang berlangsung selama tiga bulan bermula April hingga Julai lalu. Program latihan intensif itu berjaya melatih seramai 40 peserta asnaf fakir dan miskin, di mana 92.5 peratus atau 37 daripadanya terus memperoleh pekerjaan tetap di pelbagai syarikat korporat dan agensi perindustrian sebaik tamat kursus. Selain itu, sebanyak RM150,000 turut diperuntukkan sebagai modal permulaan perniagaan kepada tiga peserta Bengkel Jahitan LZNK di Kota Setar, dengan setiap seorang menerima RM50,000 bagi pembiayaan peralatan dan operasi, di samping tawaran melanjutkan pengajian ke peringkat diploma di IKM Alor Setar. Bagi aspek kebajikan asas, Maybank Islamic membiayai RM200,696.58 untuk Program Pusat Agihan Makanan menerusi 16 masjid terpilih di daerah Kuala Muda, yang menyaksikan agihan 3,840 kit makanan sepanjang tempoh enam bulan. Bagi menggalakkan aktiviti keusahawanan dari rumah, peruntukan RM34,230 pula diagihkan menerusi penyediaan mesin jahitan kepada 13 peserta daripada empat Bengkel Jahitan LZNK bagi membolehkan mereka mengambil tempahan sampingan dari rumah.

title: 'Maybank completes acquisition of remaining interest in Maybank Ageas
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) has completed the proposed acquisition of the remaining 30.95 per cent interest in Maybank Ageas Holdings Bhd after signing a share purchase agreement with Ageas Insurance International NV (Ageas) on Sept 8, 2026. In a statement today, the bank said it completed the acquisition after receiving regulatory approval from Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) on Sept 1, 2026. Maybank Ageas is the holding company for the Etiqa business in Malaysia and Singapore, providing a full range of life and general conventional insurance products as well as family and general takaful products through multi-channel distribution. Maybank president and group chief executive officer Datuk Seri Khairussaleh Ramli said the acquisition's completion was a major milestone for the bank as it continues to advance Etiqa's ambition to be a national champion, expand across Southeast Asia and build a global takaful powerhouse under ROAR30. "With Maybank Ageas being a wholly owned subsidiary of Maybank, it strengthens Etiqa's position as a national insurance and takaful champion, driving deeper penetration of Maybank's customer base. "Our focus will be unlocking further value for our customers across Southeast Asia via our regional wealth propositions through cross-selling and delivering more integrated and personalised financial solutions," he added. Meanwhile, the bank said Maybank Ageas is expected to remain well-positioned to capture growth opportunities in the insurance and takaful sector, supported by Maybank's extensive customer base and distribution network, and the increasing market demand for more integrated and personalised protection solutions.

body: 'Kuala Lumpur – Malayan Banking Berhad (Maybank) has today completed the proposed acquisition of the remaining 30.95% interest in Maybank Ageas Holdings Berhad (MAHB) (Proposed Acquisition) after signing a share purchase agreement (SPA) with Ageas Insurance International NV (Ageas) on 8 September 2026. This follows regulatory approvals from Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) that were received on 1 September 2026 for the Proposed Acquisition. MAHB is the holding company for the Etiqa business in Malaysia and Singapore, providing a full range of life and general conventional insurance products as well as family and general takaful products through multi-channel distribution. President and Group CEO of Maybank, Dato’ Sri Khairussaleh Ramli, said that this is a major milestone for Maybank as it continues to advance Etiqa’s ambition to be a national champion, expand across Southeast Asia and build a global takaful powerhouse under ROAR30. “With MAHB being a wholly owned subsidiary of Maybank, it strengthens Etiqa’s position as a national insurance and takaful champion, driving deeper penetration of Maybank’s customer base. Our focus will be unlocking further value for our customers across Southeast Asia via our regional wealth propositions through cross-selling and delivering more integrated and personalised financial solutions. It will also enhance sustainable and resilient long-term value creation for Maybank with improved capital management within the MAHB group, hence facilitating more effective capital management at the Maybank group level.” “The Etiqa brand remains a strong and well-established insurance and takaful franchise, and it will continue to be positioned as one of Maybank’s flagship brands.” Meanwhile, MAHB is expected to remain well-positioned to capture growth opportunities in the insurance and takaful sector. This will be supported by Maybank’s extensive customer base and distribution network, and the increasing market demand for more integrated and personalised protection solutions. “We would also like to thank Ageas for their 25 years partnership with Maybank and contribution in developing the Etiqa franchise. Moving forward, the full ownership provides Maybank and MAHB with greater agility to accelerate product innovation, deepen bancassurance penetration and expand takaful propositions while enhancing capital and operational efficiency across the Group,” added Dato’ Sri Khairussaleh Ramli.

title: 'Maybank ungguli Anugerah IR Bursa Malaysia 2026 dengan empat pengiktirafan
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR, 7 September 2026 – Bursa Malaysia Berhad mengiktiraf kecemerlangan amalan perhubungan pelabur (IR) menerusi penganjuran Anugerah IR Bursa Malaysia 2026, yang diadakan buat julung kalinya bagi menggalakkan peningkatan standard ketelusan dan komunikasi pasaran modal dalam kalangan syarikat tersenarai awam (PLC). Majlis anugerah berkenaan menyaksikan penyampaian pengiktirafan kepada 32 pemenang merangkumi lapan kategori utama. Malayan Banking Berhad (Maybank) dinobatkan sebagai Syarikat Terbaik dalam IR (Keseluruhan), selain memenangi kategori Pelaporan Kewangan Terbaik serta Syarikat Terbaik dalam IR bagi Sektor Perkhidmatan Kewangan Kategori Permodalan Besar. Presiden dan Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif Kumpulan Maybank, Dato’ Sri Khairussaleh Ramli, pula dinamakan sebagai CEO Terbaik dalam IR. Menyampaikan ucaptama pada majlis berkenaan, Ketua Setiausaha Perbendaharaan, Kementerian Kewangan, Tan Sri Johan Mahmood Merican, menegaskan bahawa komunikasi yang terbuka dan konsisten oleh PLC merupakan antara pemacu utama penciptaan nilai jangka panjang serta daya saing pasaran. Sementara itu, Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif Bursa Malaysia, Dato’ Fad’l Mohamed, berkata dapatan kajian Bursa Malaysia menunjukkan hanya 32 peratus PLC mempunyai fungsi IR dalaman khusus, manakala 17 peratus menggunakan perkhidmatan pihak luar dan 51 peratus lagi masih belum mempunyai struktur IR yang rasmi. “Apabila jangkaan syarikat, pasaran dan pelabur menjadi semakin matang, perhubungan pelabur yang berkesan melangkaui sekadar menyampaikan prestasi kewangan. Ia membantu pelabur memahami kedudukan strategik syarikat untuk masa hadapan,” katanya. Antara pemenang utama lain termasuk Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB) bagi kategori Komunikasi Kelestarian Terbaik, Malkit Singh Maan daripada Hong Leong Bank Berhad bagi kategori CFO Terbaik dalam IR, serta Oriental Kopi Holdings Berhad bagi kategori Syarikat IPO Terbaik dalam IR. Penilaian pemenang dilaksanakan menerusi pendekatan berasaskan pasaran yang melibatkan pelabur serta penganalisis tempatan dan antarabangsa. title: 'Maybank MAE APP推出Savings+新功能，可以直接通过MAE APP来购买货币市场基金
body: 'Maybank MAE APP推出Savings+新功能，可以直接通过MAE APP来购买货币市场基金。 Savings+是马银行（Maybank）所推出的新功能，储户将可直接通过MAE APP把钱投资到货币市场基金（MMF）。Savings+的最低起步资金是RM10。截至2026年6月30日的潜在回报是3.32%p.a.。 通过Savings+功能，储户可以把闲置的现金来赚取低风险回报。回报将会按日计算，并每月存入储户的账户内。 有兴趣使用Savings+功能，储户可以打开MAE APP后点击View All。接着找到Savings+的图标，就可开始使用Savings+的功能。 货币市场基金（Money Market Fund）是一种主要投资于短期、低风险、高流动性金融工具的开放式基金。它介于银行存款与其它高风险投资基金之间，是管理闲置现金的理想工具。 货币市场基金主要投资优质短期资产，本金发生亏损的概率极低，但并不等于完全没有风险。货币市场基金也可以快速申购和赎回，资金变现能力极强。此外，货币市场基金的收益率通常高于普通银行储蓄存款，利息一般按日计算。 （资料仅供参考，没有任何的投资建议） Tags maybank

body: 'Maybank unveiled its new investment product called the Savings+, which is a new money market investment feature on the MAE app that offers customers accessible alternative to put their extra cash to work and potentially earn returns, without having to use a separate investment platform or app.  Through Maybank Savings+, customers can invest in a Shariah-compliant money market fund managed by Maybank Asset Management Sdn Bhd. The fund aims to maintain liquidity by investing in relatively short-term, liquid assets, while offering potential returns of up to 3.32% p.a
